paras.t: Denique non obstante quod per Moysen facta sunt signa hæc, quibus Ægyptus destructa est, tamen Ægyptii videntes tot supernaturalia per Moysen fieri, habuerunt eum pro viro eximio, sicut subjungitur : Fuitque Moyses vir magnus valde in terra Ægypti coram servis Pharaonis et omni populo Ægyptiorum. Nec dubium, quin et coram Hebræis. Pharao autem elatione cæcatus, ultimo dixit ad eum, Cave ne ultra videas faciem meam, etc., ut patuit in fine præcedentis capituli.
paras.en: Lastly, although these signs by which Egypt was laid waste were done through Moses, yet the Egyptians, seeing so many supernatural things done through Moses, held him to be an outstanding man, as is added: [[11:3|And Moses was a very great man in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharao's servants, and of all the people|Fuitque Moyses vir magnus valde in terra Ægypti coram servis Pharaonis et omni populo]] of the Egyptians. Nor is there any doubt that he was so in the sight of the Hebrews too. But Pharao, blinded by pride, said to him at the last, [[Ex 10:28|beware thou see not my face any more|Cave ne ultra videas faciem meam]], etc., as appeared at the end of the preceding chapter.

paras.t: Et ait Pharaoni et ejus ministris, insinuando eis revelationem sibi factam a Deo : Hæc dicit Dominus : Media nocte ingre[…] Ægyptum, quod intelligitur de nocte illa secunda, in qua primogenita sunt occisa, quæ fuit post aliquot dies post hæc, ut ex sequenti capitulo elucescit. Ingressus est autem Dominus Ægyptum non per suæ deitatis motum aut mutationem, sed per justitiæ suæ effectum. Nam subditur : et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum, a primogenito Pharaonis inclusive, qui sedet in solio ejus, hoc est, jus hereditarium regnandi habet pro patre suo : vel, jam constitutus fuit in principatu a patre suo : quod tamen non videtur, quia in textu ubique Pharao iste insinuatur regnasse usque ad suam submersionem ; usque ad primogenitum ancillæ, quæ est ad molam : hoc est a supremo usque ad infimum inclusive ; et omnia primogenita jumentorum morientur, prout sequenti recitatur capitulo. Eritque clamor magnus in universa terra Ægypti, qualis nec ante fuit, nec postea futurus est. Ululabant namque, flebant, et clamitabant Ægyptii, tam ex dolore plagæ inflictæ, quam ex timore plagæ gravioris infligendæ. Verumtamen instante fine sæculi, arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione eorum quæ supervenient universo orbi, erit ubique terrarum incomparabilis dolor, timor, angustia. Moyses vero nunc loquitur de speciali Ægyptiorum calamitate atque clamore, non de universali generis humani ærumna.
paras.en: [[11:4|And he said|Et ait]] to Pharao and his ministers, making known to them the revelation given him by God: [[11:4|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[11:4|At midnight|Media nocte]] […] [[11:4|I will enter into Egypt|Ægyptum]] [part of a word is lost in the transcription here; below Denis reads *ingrediar Ægyptum*, "I will enter Egypt", where the Vulgate has *egrediar in Ægyptum*], which is to be understood of that later night in which the firstborn were slain, which came some days after this, as is clear from the next chapter. Now the Lord entered Egypt not by any movement or change of His Godhead, but by the effect of His justice. For it is added: [[11:5|And every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians shall die, from the firstborn of Pharao|et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum, a primogenito Pharaonis]] inclusive, [[11:5|who sitteth on his throne|qui sedet in solio ejus]], that is, who holds the hereditary right to reign after his father; or, who had already been set in the government by his father: though this does not seem so, because everywhere in the text this Pharao is implied to have reigned until he was drowned; [[11:5|even to the firstborn of the handmaid that is at the mill|usque ad primogenitum ancillæ, quæ est ad molam]]: that is, from the highest to the lowest inclusive; [[11:5|and all the firstborn of beasts|et omnia primogenita jumentorum]] shall die, as is told in the next chapter. [[11:6|And there shall be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as neither hath been before, nor shall be hereafter|Eritque clamor magnus in universa terra Ægypti, qualis nec ante fuit, nec postea futurus est]]. For the Egyptians howled, wept and cried out, as much from the pain of the plague inflicted as from fear of a heavier plague yet to be inflicted. Yet when the end of the world is at hand, with men [[Luke 21:26|withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world|arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione eorum quæ supervenient universo orbi]], there will be everywhere on earth a pain, fear and anguish beyond compare. But Moses is speaking here of the particular calamity and cry of the Egyptians, not of the universal affliction of the human race.

paras.t: Apud omnes autem filios Israel non mutiet canis ab homine usque ad pecus : hoc est, tanta quies atque securitas erunt in Hebræis et eorum pecoribus, quod nec canis, qui ex facili latrat occasione, latratum emittet. Per quem modum loquendi designatur præcipua pax Hebræorum. Et potest hoc verbum per modum hyperbolicæ locutionis intelligi. Ut sciatis quanto miraculo dividat Dominus Ægyptios et Israel, hoc est, quam miraculose ostendat pietatem suam circa Israelitas, et rigorem justitiæ circa Ægyptios.
paras.en: [[11:7|But with all the children of Israel there shall not a dog make the least noise, from man even to beast|Apud omnes autem filios Israel non mutiet canis ab homine usque ad pecus]]: that is, there shall be such quiet and security among the Hebrews and their flocks that not even a dog, which barks at the slightest occasion, shall give a bark. This manner of speaking signifies the singular peace of the Hebrews. And this saying can also be understood as a hyperbole. [[11:7|that you may know how wonderful a difference the Lord maketh between the Egyptians and Israel|Ut sciatis quanto miraculo dividat Dominus Ægyptios et Israel]], that is, how miraculously He shows His loving kindness towards the Israelites and the rigour of His justice towards the Egyptians.

paras.t: Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me. Hoc Moyses dixit de se ipso : nam subditur, et adorabunt me adoratione duliæ, id est rogabunt. Unde aliqui habent, Orabunt. Dicentes : Egredere tu et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi, hoc est tota plebs Israelitica : Post hæc egrediemur Ægyptum. Vel sensus est, quod servi Pharaonis descendentes in terram Gessen, adorabunt Deum Israel, quem ex tantis prodigiis aliqualiter cognoverunt, ut ipse Dominus Deus Hebræorum cum populo suo ab Ægypto discederet, ne amplius plagaret Ægyptios. Moyses quippe post hæc rediit ad terram Gessen, et eo exsistente ibidem, primogenita sunt percussa. Quo facto, servi Pharaonis venerunt illuc, ut infra habetur.
paras.en: [[11:8|And all these thy servants shall come down to me|Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me]]. Moses said this of himself: for it is added, [[11:8|and shall worship me|et adorabunt me]] with the worship of dulia [that is, the honour paid to a creature, as distinct from latria, the worship due to God alone], that is, they shall entreat me. Hence some read *Orabunt*, "they shall pray". [[11:8|saying: Go forth thou, and all the people that is under thee|Dicentes : Egredere tu et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi]], that is, the whole people of Israel: [[11:8|after that we will go out|Post hæc egrediemur]] of Egypt. Or the sense is that Pharao's servants, coming down into the land of Gessen, will worship the God of Israel, whom they had come to know in some measure from such great wonders, praying that the Lord God of the Hebrews would Himself depart from Egypt with His people, so as to plague the Egyptians no more. For after this Moses went back to the land of Gessen, and while he was there the firstborn were struck. When this was done, Pharao's servants came there, as is told below.

paras.t: Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis. Moyses quamvis esset mitissimus, tamen ex zelo justitiæ fuit multum iratus secundum rationis dictamen, tam inauditam impii regis obdurationem, ingratitudinem, rebellionem, et comminationem detestans atque admirans, imo et juste puniri saltem in vita hac cupiens. Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen : Non audiet auribus cordis eos Pharao, donec rursus tangatur, ut multa signa fiant in terra Ægypti. Quod ex Pharaonis obstinatione consecutum est, non directe causaliter, sed concomitanter. Certumque est, quod Pharao non ob hoc non audivit Moysen, quatenus signa multiplicarentur, quia non intendebat, neque optabat hoc. Porro post hæc facta est percussio primogenitorum, divisio maris Rubri, submersio Ægyptiorum. Moyses autem et Aaron fecerunt ministerialiter, non efficienter et principaliter, omnia ostenta quæ scripta sunt, coram Pharaone, hoc est præfata signa quæ fuerunt ostensione et admiratione dignissima. Nec solum fuit miranda signorum illorum productio, sed et eorum, saltem aliquorum, cessatio, ut ex præhabitis constat.
paras.en: [[11:9|And he went out from Pharao exceeding angry|Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis]]. Moses, though he was most meek[[Num 12:3||]], was yet very angry out of zeal for justice, according to the dictate of reason, abhorring and marvelling at the unheard-of hardness, ingratitude, rebellion and threatening of the wicked king, and indeed desiring that he be justly punished, at least in this life. [[11:9|But the Lord said to Moses|Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[11:9|Pharao will not hear|Non audiet]] with the ears of the heart [[11:9|you|eos]] [Denis reads *eos*, "them", where the Vulgate has *vos*, "you"] until he is struck again, [[11:9|that many signs may be done in the land of Egypt|ut multa signa fiant in terra Ægypti]]. This followed from Pharao's obstinacy not as its direct effect but as something accompanying it. And it is certain that Pharao did not refuse to hear Moses for this end, that the signs might be multiplied, for he neither intended nor desired this. Moreover, after this came the striking of the firstborn, the dividing of the Red Sea, and the drowning of the Egyptians. [[11:10|And Moses and Aaron did|Moyses autem et Aaron fecerunt]], as ministers, not as the efficient and principal cause, [[11:10|all the wonders that are written, before Pharao|omnia ostenta quæ scripta sunt, coram Pharaone]], that is, the aforesaid signs, which were most worthy to be shown and marvelled at. And not only was the bringing about of those signs to be marvelled at, but also the ceasing of them, at least of some, as is plain from what has gone before.

paras.t: Juxta intelligentiam spiritualem docemur ex isto capitulo, quod Deo resistere non est consultum, sicut et Christus locutus est Paulo : Durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare. Idcirco qui Dei sentit percussionem, protinus se emendet, ne durioribus plagis afficiatur, attendens quod scriptum est : Amove a me plagas tuas. Et causa ibidem subjicitur : A fortitudine manus tuæ ego defeci in increpationibus.
paras.en: According to the spiritual understanding, we are taught by this chapter that it is not wise to resist God, as Christ too said to Paul: [[Acts 9:5|It is hard for thee to kick against the goad|Durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare]]. Therefore whoever feels God's stroke should amend himself at once, lest he be afflicted with harder plagues, heeding what is written: [[Ps 38:11|Remove thy scourges from me|Amove a me plagas tuas]]. And the reason is given in the same place: [[Ps 38:11|The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes|A fortitudine manus tuæ ego defeci in increpationibus]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxviii, 11, 12; in the Vulgate these words begin v. 12, in the Douay-Rheims they end v. 11; *plagas*, "plagues" or "strokes", is the Douay's "scourges"].

paras.t: Quid autem per vasa aurea atque argentea Ægyptiorum, et mutuationem eorum signetur, in expositione tertii capituli patuit. Fuit autem Moyses vir magnus valde coram servis Pharaonis. Sic et quilibet nostrum studeat esse spiritualiter magnum, hoc est valde virtuosus ac sapiens, ita ut sit bonus odor Christi in omni loco, et sæcularibus exemplaris exsistat. Est itaque magnus valde, qui est profunde humilis, perfecte patiens, fractus, et sibimet mortuus, vivens ac fervens in Domino.
paras.en: What is signified by the vessels of gold and silver of the Egyptians, and by the borrowing of them, was shown in the exposition of the third chapter[[Ex 3:22||]]. [[11:3|And Moses was a very great man|Fuit autem Moyses vir magnus valde]] [[11:3|in the sight of Pharao's servants|coram servis Pharaonis]]. So too let each of us strive to be great in spirit, that is, very virtuous and wise, so that he may be the [[2 Cor 2:15|good odour of Christ|bonus odor Christi]] in every place, and a pattern to those of the world. And so he is very great who is deeply humble, perfectly patient, broken and dead to himself, living and fervent in the Lord.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Media nocte ingrediar Ægyptum, et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum. Hoc spiritualiter agitur, dum Deus corda hominum visitat gratiose, quando adhuc sunt in profunda vitiorum caligine, perimitque in eis universa peccata mortalia, illos ad veram contritionem instigans. Tunc plane generatur incomparabilis dolor, clamorque cordis, id est interna ac fervens devotio inter eos, qui in tenebris sæculi, quasi in Ægypto, fuerunt. Contritio namque est maximus dolor, quia de malo culpæ et summi boni offensa atque amissione, oportet maxime dolere, quemadmodum et necesse est summum bonum incomparabiliter semper diligere. Qui vero sic visitantur et illustrantur a Domino, sua perpendunt peccata, et intime deflent ea.
paras.en: [[11:4|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[11:4|At midnight I will enter into Egypt|Media nocte ingrediar Ægyptum]], [[11:5|And every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians shall die|et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum]]. This is done spiritually when God visits the hearts of men with His grace while they are still in the deep darkness of vice, and slays in them all mortal sins, moving them to true contrition. Then indeed there arises a pain beyond compare, and a cry of the heart, that is, an inward and fervent devotion, among those who were in the darkness of the world as in Egypt. For contrition is the greatest pain, since for the evil of guilt, and for the offence and loss of the highest good, one must grieve most of all, just as one must always love the highest good beyond compare. Those who are thus visited and enlightened by the Lord weigh their sins and weep for them from the heart.

paras.t: Apud filios Israel non mutiet canis : id est, in cordibus contemplativorum abundabit pax pectoris, nec iræ ceterarumque passionum erit tumultus in eis, sed vita secreta, quemadmodum in Isaia Dominus protestatur : Erit opus justitiæ pax, et cultus justitiæ silentium : et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta. Et […] quanto […] ho, etc. Ex his equidem claret quantum inter carnales et spirituales, inter sæculares et vere religiosos, inter passionatos et contemplativos distet ac differat, et quam diversimode Dominus operetur in eis.
paras.en: [[11:7|with all the children of Israel there shall not a dog make the least noise|Apud filios Israel non mutiet canis]]: that is, in the hearts of contemplatives peace of heart shall abound, and there shall be in them no tumult of anger or of the other passions, but a hidden life, as the Lord declares in Isaias: [[Is 32:17|the work of justice shall be peace, and the service of justice quietness|opus justitiæ pax, et cultus justitiæ silentium]]: [[Is 32:18|And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]]. And […] [[11:7|how wonderful|quanto]] […], etc. [most of this lemma, from v. 7, is lost in the transcription]. From this it is clear how far the carnal and the spiritual, the worldly and the truly religious, the slaves of passion and the contemplatives, stand apart and differ, and in how different ways the Lord works in them.

paras.t: Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me, etc. Dum enim iniqui ita præveniuntur et compunguntur a Spiritu Sancto, humiliant se, atque in mentis humiliatione accedunt ad thronum gratiæ Dei, dicentes : Egredere tu. Quia ex consideratione suorum excessuum, divina visitatione se fatentur indignos, cum sancto Petro dicentes : Exi a me, quia homo peccator sum, Domine. Verumtamen non volunt relinqui a Domino, sed peculiari ejus consolatione ac præsentia suavi reputant se indignissimos esse, et quasi indecens eis apparet, quod Dominus tam misericordissime agit cum eis. Et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi, egredietur a nostra oppressione. Nempe iniqui qui justos premunt ac persequuntur, quum sic convertuntur, dimittunt justos egredi liberos, et venerantur eosdem, imo eorum obsequio indignos se arbitrantur.
paras.en: [[11:8|And all these thy servants shall come down to me|Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me]], etc. For when the wicked are thus forestalled and pricked to the heart by the Holy Ghost, they humble themselves and, in humility of mind, draw near [[Heb 4:16|to the throne of grace|ad thronum gratiæ]] of God, [[11:8|saying: Go forth thou|dicentes : Egredere tu]]. For in considering their excesses they confess themselves unworthy of God's visitation, saying with St Peter: [[Luke 5:8|Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord|Exi a me, quia homo peccator sum, Domine]]. Yet they do not wish to be left by the Lord; but they reckon themselves most unworthy of His special consolation and sweet presence, and it seems to them almost unfitting that the Lord deals so very mercifully with them. [[11:8|and all the people that is under thee|Et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi]] shall go out from our oppression. For the wicked who oppress and persecute the just, when they are thus converted, let the just go out free and revere them, and indeed think themselves unworthy to serve them.

paras.t: Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis. Sic et justi contra perversorum duritiam interdum zelo justitiæ irascuntur, et cupiunt eos in hac vita castigari a Domino, ne pereant in æternum. Verumtamen zelus hujusmodi esse debet secundum scientiam, hoc est discretione condiri, ut memor sit homo propriæ fragilitatis, nec immoderate fervescat : imo pro eorum oret salute quibus irascitur.
paras.en: [[11:9|And he went out from Pharao exceeding angry|Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis]]. So too the just are at times angered, out of zeal for justice, against the hardness of the perverse, and desire that they be chastised by the Lord in this life, lest they perish for ever. Yet zeal of this kind must be according to knowledge, that is, seasoned with discretion, so that a man is mindful of his own frailty and does not burn beyond measure: rather, let him pray for the salvation of those with whom he is angry.

12.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli duodecimi: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen
12.title_en: Literal explanation of the twelfth chapter: The Lord also said to Moses

paras.t: Antequam Moyses decimæ plagæ in præcedenti capitulo comminatæ inflictionem describat, nunc quædam interserit de institutione et ritu Paschæ, hoc est tam festi quam agni paschalis, quod ad litteram Deus instituit, in commemorationem liberationis Hebræorum ex Ægypto. Spiritualiter vero per illud apertissime designavit generalem mundi redemptionem, per Christi passionem effectam.
paras.en: Before Moses describes the infliction of the tenth plague threatened in the preceding chapter, he now inserts certain things concerning the institution and rite of the Pasch, that is, both of the feast and of the paschal lamb, which God instituted according to the letter in commemoration of the deliverance of the Hebrews out of Egypt. But spiritually He most plainly signified by it the general redemption of the world, accomplished by the passion of Christ.

paras.t: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron in terra Ægypti. Istud creditur eis dixisse, quum a Pharaone redissent ad suos in terram Gessen, post nonæ plagæ inflictionem, ut præcedenti tangebatur articulo. Mensis iste, vobis principium mensium, supple, exsistens, primus erit in mensibus anni: id est, Hoc præcipio, ut vos Hebræi computationem anni incipiatis a mense isto, tanquam a primo anni mense, et propter beneficia quæ vobis in isto mense exhibeo, de Ægyptia servitute et aliis malis vos liberando, multaque bona præstando, ut consequenter dicetur. Alii vero populi ab aliis mensibus inchoant annum. Nam Christiani morem Romanorum sequendo, a Januario annum incipiunt, Arabes vero post æstivale solstitium.
paras.en: [[12:1|And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt|Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron in terra Ægypti]]. He is believed to have said this to them when they had returned from Pharao to their own people in the land of Gessen, after the infliction of the ninth plague, as was touched on in the preceding article. [[12:2|This month shall be to you the beginning of months|Mensis iste, vobis principium mensium]] (supply: *being* [Denis supplies a participle, *exsistens*, for the verbless Latin clause]), [[12:2|it shall be the first in the months of the year|primus erit in mensibus anni]]: that is, This I command, that you Hebrews begin the reckoning of the year from this month, as from the first month of the year, and that on account of the benefits which I show you in this month, delivering you from the Egyptian bondage and other evils and bestowing many good things, as will be said next. Other peoples, however, begin the year from other months. For Christians, following the custom of the Romans, begin the year from January, and the Arabs after the summer solstice.

paras.t: Per hunc mensem Glossa et Rabanus, ac alii multi Catholici Aprilem intelligunt, qui secundum eos, appellatur Nisan apud Hebræos. Et dicitur Aprilis quasi aperilis, quia in eo terra aperitur ad producendum virgulta, flores, ac herbas. Porro Lyra hoc reprobat, dicens, per hunc mensem qui est primus apud Hebræos, intelligi Martium: quia secundum omnes, September est septimus mensis apud Hebræos. September autem non est septimus ab Aprili, sed a Martio. Quod argumentum faciliter solveretur, dicendo quod computatio illa ab Aprili et Martio usque Septembrem, potest fieri per inclusionem aut exclusionem extremi vel extremorum, et ita September erit septimus ab Aprili. Quemadmodum transfigurationem Christi quam scribit Lucas factam post octo dies, Matthæus refert factam post sex dies: quod prætacto modo ab expositoribus concordatur.
paras.en: By this month the Gloss and Rabanus and many other Catholics understand April, which according to them is called Nisan among the Hebrews. And it is called *Aprilis* as though *aperilis* [from *aperire*, to open], because in it the earth is opened to bring forth shoots, flowers and herbs. Lyra, however, rejects this, saying that by this month, which is the first among the Hebrews, March is meant: because according to all, September is the seventh month among the Hebrews; but September is not the seventh from April, but from March. This argument would easily be answered by saying that the reckoning from April and from March up to September can be made by including or excluding the end or the ends, and so September will be the seventh from April. Just as the transfiguration of Christ, which Luke writes took place after eight days[[Luke 9:28||]] [the margin gives Luc. ix, 2; the passage is Luke 9:28], Matthew relates took place after six days[[Matt 17:1||]]: which the expositors reconcile in the way just touched on.

paras.t: Denique Magister in historiis de hac re magistralius ac resolutius scribit, dicendo: Mensis iste erit vobis primus in mensibus anni, hic est Aprilis, id est lunatio aprilis, quæ sæpe in Martio inchoat: qui mensis ab Hebræis dicitur Nisan. Voluit quippe Dominus Hebræos a ceteris nationibus differre in temporis computatione, sicut in religione et circumcisionis charactere. Romani autem ex traditione Numæ Pompilii, primum mensem ponunt Januarium, quia tunc sol incipit ascendere post solstitium hiemale. Sed congruentius videtur fieri ab Hebræis in Martio. In Aprili ergo cærimoniali differunt a nobis (quia videlicet ille est in Martio); in temporali nobiscum conveniunt. Hæc Magister ibidem.
paras.en: Then the Master in the Histories [that is, Peter Comestor, in the *Historia scholastica*] writes of this matter in a more masterly and decisive way, saying: [[12:2|This month|Mensis iste]] shall be to you [[12:2|the first in the months of the year|primus in mensibus anni]]; this is April, that is, the April lunation, which often begins in March: which month is called Nisan by the Hebrews. For the Lord willed the Hebrews to differ from the other nations in the reckoning of time, as in religion and in the mark of circumcision. The Romans, however, from the tradition of Numa Pompilius, place January as the first month, because then the sun begins to climb after the winter solstice. But it seems to be done more fittingly by the Hebrews in March. In the ceremonial April, then, they differ from us (namely, because theirs is in March); in the temporal one they agree with us. Thus far the Master there.

paras.t: Denique de hac materia scribit Rabbi Paulus prolixe, inter cetera dicens: Mensis apud Hebræos Nisan vocatus, proprie loquendo, non est Aprilis noster, nec Martius. Quum enim ipsi computent menses per lunationes, raro contingit, quod prima dies lunationis concurrat cum prima Martii die, sed communiter venit in diebus primum Martii diem sequentibus: ideo mensis Nisan frequenter concurrit cum Aprili secundum aliquam sui partem. Unde opinio catholicorum doctorum dicentium Aprilem esse primum mensem apud Hebræos, vera est, secundum sanum intellectum, scilicet ut frequenter, et ut in pluribus mensis Aprilis concurrit cum primo mense apud Hebræos secundum aliquam sui partem.
paras.en: Lastly Rabbi Paul [that is, Paul of Burgos, a converted rabbi, author of the Additions to Lyra] writes at length on this matter, saying among other things: The month called Nisan among the Hebrews is, properly speaking, neither our April nor March. For since they reckon the months by lunations, it seldom happens that the first day of the lunation falls on the first day of March; commonly it comes on the days following the first of March: therefore the month Nisan frequently coincides with April in some part of it. Hence the opinion of the Catholic doctors who say that April is the first month among the Hebrews is true in a sound sense, namely that frequently and for the most part the month of April coincides in some part of it with the first month among the Hebrews.

paras.t: Circa hoc dico, verum esse quod noster Aprilis aut Martius non est præcise mensis ille, quem Hebræi nominant Nisan, ut ex dictis elicitur.
paras.en: On this I say that it is true that our April or March is not precisely the month which the Hebrews call Nisan, as is gathered from what has been said.

paras.t: Loquimini ad universum cœtum filiorum Israel, et dicite eis: Decima die mensis hujus, qui est primus inter menses anni secundum vos, tollat unusquisque agnum per familias et domos suas: hoc est, quilibet paterfamilias seu principalis in domo sua atque familia, sumat de grege agnum. Sin autem minor est numerus, ut sufficere possit ad vescendum agnum, id est, si habitantes in una domo, non sint tot, ut queant paschalem comedere agnum. Dicitur autem in Scholastica historia: Aiunt quidam, quod decem capita seu homines erant in esu agni unius. Assumet vicinum suum, qui conjunctus est domui ejus, juxta numerum animarum quæ sufficere possint ad esum agni, hoc est, tot homines Hebræos sibi vicinos, assumet ad manducandum secum agnum illum, ut simul cum illis valeat agnum paschalem comedere. Unde in tali casu poterant duarum domorum personæ conjungi ad edendum unum agnum paschalem.
paras.en: [[12:3|Speak ye to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them|Loquimini ad universum cœtum filiorum Israel, et dicite eis]]: [[12:3|On the tenth day of this month|Decima die mensis hujus]], which is the first among the months of the year according to you, [[12:3|let every man take a lamb by their families and houses|tollat unusquisque agnum per familias et domos suas]]: that is, let each father of a family, or head in his house and family, take a lamb from the flock. [[12:4|But if the number be less than may suffice to eat the lamb|Sin autem minor est numerus, ut sufficere possit ad vescendum agnum]], that is, if those dwelling in one house are not so many that they can eat the paschal lamb. Now it is said in the Scholastic History: Some say that ten heads, or men, shared in eating one lamb. [[12:4|he shall take unto him his neighbour that joineth to his house|Assumet vicinum suum, qui conjunctus est domui ejus]], [[12:4|according to the number of souls which may be enough to eat the lamb|juxta numerum animarum quæ sufficere possint ad esum agni]], that is, he shall take so many Hebrew men, his neighbours, to eat that lamb with him, that together with them he may be able to eat the paschal lamb. Hence in such a case the persons of two houses could be joined to eat one paschal lamb.

paras.t: Erit autem agnus absque macula, masculus, anniculus, id est unius anni, vel potius infra vel non ultra unius anni ætatem: poterat enim assumi et offerri ab octava suæ nativitatis die, et non ante, usque ad consummationem sui primi anni, non postea; masculus, quia non poterat esse agna; absque macula, id est non monstruosa fœditate deformis. Itaque macula non sumitur hic pro varietate colorum in pelle seu vellere, sicut in Genesi, ubi pecora diversorum colorum, maculosa dicuntur; sed pro monstruositate, de qua macula in Levitico legitur, Si cæcum fuerit, si fractum, aut impetiginem habens. Perfectiora etenim Deo sunt offerenda, juxta illud Malachiæ: Maledictus dolosus qui habet in grege suo masculum, et votum faciens, immolat debile Domino. Juxta quem ritum tolletis et hœdum, videlicet decima die mensis istius, et servabitis eum usque ad quartamdecimam diem mensis hujus. Ad quam etiam diem agnus fuit servandus.
paras.en: [[12:5|And it shall be a lamb without blemish, a male, of one year|Erit autem agnus absque macula, masculus, anniculus]], that is, of one year, or rather under, or not beyond, the age of one year: for it could be taken and offered from the eighth day after its birth, and not before, until the completion of its first year, not after; [[12:5|a male|masculus]], because it could not be a ewe lamb; [[12:5|without blemish|absque macula]], that is, not disfigured by a monstrous deformity. So *blemish* [*macula*, literally a spot] is not taken here for a variety of colours in the skin or fleece, as in Genesis, where cattle of divers colours are called spotted[[Gen 30:32||]]; but for deformity, of which blemish we read in Leviticus: [[Lev 22:22|If it be blind, or broken|Si cæcum fuerit, si fractum]], or having [[Lev 22:22|a dry scurf|impetiginem]]. For the more perfect things are to be offered to God, according to that of Malachias: [[Mal 1:14|Cursed is the deceitful man that hath in his flock a male, and making a vow offereth in sacrifice that which is feeble to the Lord|Maledictus dolosus qui habet in grege suo masculum, et votum faciens, immolat debile Domino]]. [[12:5|according to which rite also you shall take a kid|Juxta quem ritum tolletis et hœdum]], namely on the tenth day of this month, [[12:6|And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month|et servabitis eum usque ad quartamdecimam diem mensis hujus]]. To which day the lamb also was to be kept.

paras.t: Præterea quidam dixerunt, hoc loco duplicem oblationem juberi a Domino: unam agni, quem dixerunt decima die offerri in qualibet domo. Aliam hœdi, quem dicebant quartadecima die immolari a toto Israelitico populo simul collecto, non seorsum in domibus singulorum: quia in textu subjungitur, Immolabitque eum universa multitudo filiorum Israel ad vesperam. Sed hujus oppositum probatur ex textu, quia post pauca adjicitur: Sument de sanguine ejus, ac ponent super utrumque postem, et in superliminaribus domorum, in quibus comedent illum: et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni; caput cum pedibus ejus et intestinis vorabitis; nec remanebit ex eo quidquam usque mane. Certum est quod universi Hebræi in domibus suis non poterant vesci carnibus hœdi unius, nec de ejus sanguine poterat tanta linitio fieri, nec fuit periculum quod de carnibus unius hœdi posset tot manducantibus aliquid superesse.
paras.en: Some, moreover, have said that a twofold offering is commanded by the Lord in this place: one of a lamb, which they said was offered on the tenth day in each house; the other of a kid, which they said was sacrificed on the fourteenth day by the whole Israelite people gathered together, not separately in the houses of each: because in the text there follows: [[12:6|and the whole multitude of the children of Israel shall sacrifice it in the evening|Immolabitque eum universa multitudo filiorum Israel ad vesperam]]. But the opposite of this is proved from the text, since a little after it is added: [[12:7|they shall take of the blood thereof, and put it upon both the side posts, and on the upper door posts of the houses, wherein they shall eat it|Sument de sanguine ejus, ac ponent super utrumque postem, et in superliminaribus domorum, in quibus comedent illum]]: [[12:8|And they shall eat the flesh that night roasted at the fire|et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni]]; [[12:9|you shall eat the head with the feet and entrails thereof|caput cum pedibus ejus et intestinis vorabitis]]; [[12:10|Neither shall there remain any thing of it until morning|nec remanebit ex eo quidquam usque mane]]. It is certain that all the Hebrews in their houses could not feed on the flesh of one kid, nor could so much smearing be done with its blood, nor was there any danger that anything of the flesh of one kid could be left over with so many eating it.

paras.t: Itaque, sicut Lyra et Rabbi Paulus testantur, Translatio nostra hoc loco discrepat ab Hebraica veritate in verbis: quia pro his verbis, Juxta quem ritum tolletis hœdum, in Hebræo habetur, De arietibus vel de capris accipietis illum, videlicet agnum. Unde dictio Hebraica ibi pro agno posita, quandoque pro hœdo accipitur, et ita non sumpsit eam Hieronymus. Idcirco non fuit duplex oblatio, sed una, quæ fieri debuit de agno, si bono modo posset haberi; alioquin de hœdo fieri poterat. His concordat quod Septuaginta transtulerunt, Ab agnis et hœdis accipietis illud: quasi diceretur, Id quod offeretur, erit agnus aut hœdus. Sicque quod habet translatio nostra, Juxta quem ritum accipietis et hœdum, intelligendum est in casu, quo agnus haberi nequibat. Verumtamen Rabbi Paulus his contradicit, et dicit: Immolatio paschalis, secundum doctores Hebræos, de agno debebat fieri, et non de hœdo: quod congruit tam litterali causæ sacrificii hujus, quam etiam figurali. Primum patet, quia secundum Rabbi Moysen Gerundensem et alios, præcipiebatur agnus occidi in primo mense, quoniam signum Arietis est tunc in potissimo suo statu, quum sol tunc in eodem sit signo communiter. Et quia Ægyptii arietem venerabantur, volebat Dominus per occisionem agni ostendere, quod etiam in diis Ægyptiorum faceret ultionem; quæ ratio non haberet locum in hœdo. Secundum patet, quoniam Christus significatur per agnum, non per hœdum; imo ipse per hœdos significat reprobos apud Matthæum loquens: Hœdos statuet a sinistris.
paras.en: Therefore, as Lyra and Rabbi Paul testify, our translation in this place differs in its words from the Hebrew verity: for in place of these words, [[12:5|according to which rite also you shall take a kid|Juxta quem ritum tolletis hœdum]], the Hebrew has: From the rams or from the goats you shall take it, namely the lamb. Hence the Hebrew word put there for lamb is sometimes taken for a kid, and Jerome did not take it in this way. Therefore there was not a twofold offering but one, which was to be made of a lamb if one could conveniently be had; otherwise it could be made of a kid. With this agrees what the Seventy translated: From the lambs and the kids you shall take it: as if it were said, That which shall be offered shall be a lamb or a kid. And so what our translation has, [[12:5|according to which rite also you shall take a kid|Juxta quem ritum accipietis et hœdum]], is to be understood of the case in which a lamb could not be had. Rabbi Paul, however, contradicts this and says: The paschal sacrifice, according to the Hebrew doctors, was to be made of a lamb and not of a kid; which agrees both with the literal reason of this sacrifice and with the figurative one. The first is plain, because according to Rabbi Moses of Gerona and others, the lamb was commanded to be slain in the first month because the sign of the Ram is then at its strongest, since the sun is then commonly in that same sign. And because the Egyptians worshipped the ram, the Lord willed by the slaying of the lamb to show that He was taking vengeance even on the gods of the Egyptians; which reason would have no place in a kid. The second is plain, since Christ is signified by the lamb, not by the kid; indeed He Himself signifies the reprobate by kids, speaking in Matthew: He shall set [[Matt 25:33|the goats on his left|Hœdos statuet a sinistris]] [*hædos*, kids].

paras.t: Circa hæc dico, quod duæ rationes istæ, ad probandum propositum sunt invalidæ. Dominus enim in sacrificiorum institutione ac jussione, respectum non habuit ad signa zodiaci vel luminaria cœli. Ægyptii quoque non solum colebant arietem seu potius Jovem in forma arietis, sed etiam hircos, quia in similitudine hirci apparuerunt eis interdum diaboli, ut et Lyra hic refert. Insuper Christus interdum in Scripturis veteris Testamenti designatur per hircum, quemadmodum in Levitico patet de hirco, qui portavit omnes iniquitates filiorum Israel in desertum: per quod passio Christi extra portam crucifixi, et ibi peccata mundi tollentis, evidenter signata est. Idem patet de hirco, cujus sors exiit Domino. Imo et per capream figuratur, juxta illud in Canticis: Fuge, dilecte mi, similis esto capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum. Nec obstat, quod per hircum reprobi aliquando exprimantur, sicut per leonem quandoque intelligitur Christus, quandoque diabolus: Christus, ob suam fortitudinem ac regiam dignitatem, juxta illud in Apocalypsi, Vicit leo de tribu Juda; diabolus, ob suam ferocitatem, principe Apostolorum hortante, Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit quærens quem devoret. Imo et reprobi nonnunquam designantur per oves, secundum illud Psalmi: Sicut oves in inferno positi sunt. Siquidem per eamdem rem, secundum diversas suas proprietates, designantur diversa.
paras.en: On these I say that these two reasons are not valid to prove the point. For the Lord, in instituting and commanding sacrifices, had no regard to the signs of the zodiac or the lights of heaven. The Egyptians, moreover, worshipped not only the ram, or rather Jupiter in the form of a ram, but also he-goats, because devils sometimes appeared to them in the likeness of a he-goat, as Lyra also reports here. Besides, Christ is sometimes designated in the Scriptures of the Old Testament by a he-goat, as is plain in Leviticus of the goat that carried all the iniquities of the children of Israel into the desert[[Lev 16:22||]]: by which the passion of Christ, crucified outside the gate[[Heb 13:12||]] and there taking away the sins of the world[[John 1:29||]], is evidently signified. The same is plain of the goat [[Lev 16:9|whose lot fell to be offered to the Lord|cujus sors exiit Domino]] [the margin gives Lev. xvi, 7–9]. Indeed He is figured even by the roe, according to that in the Canticles: [[Cant 8:14|Flee away, O my beloved, and be like to the roe, and to the young hart|Fuge, dilecte mi, similis esto capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum]]. Nor does it stand in the way that the reprobate are sometimes expressed by the he-goat; just as by the lion sometimes Christ is understood, sometimes the devil: Christ, for His strength and royal dignity, according to that in the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 5:5|the lion of the tribe of Juda|leo de tribu Juda]] [[Apoc 5:5|hath prevailed|Vicit]]; the devil, for his ferocity, as the prince of the Apostles exhorts: [[1 Pet 5:8|your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit quærens quem devoret]]. Indeed the reprobate too are sometimes designated by sheep, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 48:15|They are laid in hell like sheep|Sicut oves in inferno positi sunt]]. For by the same thing, according to its different properties, different things are designated.

paras.t: Præterea, dato quod aliqui doctores Hebræi sint opinati, quod immolatio paschalis non nisi de agno fieri debuit, nihilo minus multi solennes et antiqui Hebræorum doctores dixerunt oppositum. Unde circa præinductam litteram Septuaginta interpretum, Ab agnis et hœdis accipietis illud, loquitur Augustinus: Conantur Judæi asserere, etiam hœdum accipiendum ad celebrandum Pascha, tanquam si diceretur, Ab agnis agnum sumi oportet, vel ab hœdis hœdum, si illud desit. In Scholastica quoque historia dicitur: Decima die mensis hujus tollet domus quælibet agnum, vel si non poterit agnum, saltem hœdum. Sed et Lyra refert doctores Hebræorum ita sentire. Denique, si de solo agno fieri poterat illa oblatio, translatio Hieronymi quam Ecclesia approbat, esset falsa, sufficissetque dicere in Hebræo, De arietibus accipietis illum, nec addi oportuisset. Vel de capris, nisi propter mysticam quandam significationem, ex qua argumentum sumi non potest ad litteram, ut Augustinus testatur.
paras.en: Further, granted that some Hebrew doctors held that the paschal sacrifice was to be made only of a lamb, nevertheless many eminent and ancient doctors of the Hebrews said the opposite. Hence on the text of the Seventy translators cited above, *From the lambs and the kids you shall take it*, Augustine says: The Jews try to maintain that a kid also is to be taken for celebrating the Pasch, as if it were said: From the lambs a lamb must be taken, or from the kids a kid, if that is lacking. In the Scholastic History, too, it is said: On the tenth day of this month every house shall take a lamb, or if it cannot have a lamb, at least a kid. And Lyra also reports that the doctors of the Hebrews hold this. Finally, if that offering could be made only of a lamb, the translation of Jerome, which the Church approves, would be false; and it would have been enough to say in the Hebrew, *From the rams you shall take it*, and there would have been no need to add *or from the goats*, unless for the sake of some mystical meaning, from which no argument can be drawn according to the letter, as Augustine testifies.

paras.t: Præterea quæritur, cur in littera de agno non dicitur, quod servandus erat usque ad quartamdecimam diem, quemadmodum hoc de hœdo exprimitur. Deinde, cur utrumque animal jubetur per quatuor dies ante suam immolationem accipi et servari. Respondetur ad primum, quod ex quo una fuit oblatio illa paschalis de agno aut hœdo, idcirco quod de reservatione hœdi exprimitur, de agno intelligi datur. Ad aliud respondetur, quod ideo, ne Hebræi tunc diversimode occupati, se disponendo ad exitum ab Ægypto, obliviscerentur accipere agnum vel hœdum in die immolationis. Et item, ut infra illud quatriduum diligenter perpenderent, an aliqua macula esset in hœdo immolationis, et item an in agno. Alia autem est ratio spiritualis, quæ infra tangetur. Et quoniam causæ prætactæ præcipiendi agnum vel hœdum per quatuor dies, postea cessaverunt: dicunt Hebræi, quod præceptio illa non obligabat nec servabatur in posterum, quando ex consuetudine facilius attenderetur, an agnus vel hœdus immolatitius esset.
paras.en: It is asked further why in the text it is not said of the lamb that it was to be kept until the fourteenth day, as this is expressed of the kid; and next, why each animal is commanded to be taken and kept for four days before its sacrifice. To the first it is answered that, since that paschal offering was one, of a lamb or of a kid, what is expressed of keeping the kid is given to be understood of the lamb. To the other it is answered that it was so that the Hebrews, then busied in various ways preparing for their departure from Egypt, should not forget to take the lamb or kid on the day of sacrifice; and also that within those four days they might weigh carefully whether there was any blemish in the kid for sacrifice, and likewise in the lamb. There is also another, spiritual reason, which will be touched on below. And since the reasons just mentioned for prescribing the lamb or kid four days beforehand afterwards ceased, the Hebrews say that that precept did not bind and was not kept in later times, when by custom it was more easily seen whether the lamb or kid was fit for sacrifice.

paras.t: Sequitur: Immolabitque eum hœdum aut agnum universa multitudo filiorum Israel, id est, unusquisque paterfamilias aut quælibet persona capitalis de multitudine Israelitarum, offeret in domo sua. Quod dictum est, casu prætacto excepto: sicque quod ait, Universa multitudo, divisim, non collectim, accipitur; et per agnum seu hœdum, agni aut hirci pluraliter intelliguntur. Ad vesperam quartadecima die mensis præfati, seu luna quartadecima, quando die sequenti valde mane egressuri erant Ægyptum. Fuit equidem immolatio illa, dispositio ad egressum, atque ad liberationem a percussione, qua angelus primogenita Ægyptiorum occidit. Et fiebat ad vesperam, quam Judæi a septima hora incipiebant, pertinuitque ad diem sequentem secundum computationem eorum.
paras.en: There follows: [[12:6|and the whole multitude of the children of Israel|universa multitudo filiorum Israel]] [[12:6|shall sacrifice it|Immolabitque eum]] (the kid or the lamb), that is, each father of a family, or any head of a household of the multitude of the Israelites, shall offer it in his own house. This is said with the exception of the case mentioned above; and so when he says *the whole multitude*, it is taken distributively, not collectively [that is, of each one severally, not of all together]; and by *lamb* or *kid*, lambs or goats are understood in the plural. [[12:6|in the evening|Ad vesperam]], on the fourteenth day of the said month, or the fourteenth moon, since on the following day, very early, they were to go out of Egypt. For that sacrifice was a preparation for the departure, and for the deliverance from the stroke by which the angel killed the firstborn of the Egyptians. And it was done in the evening, which the Jews began from the seventh hour, and it belonged to the following day according to their reckoning.

paras.t: Et sument de sanguine ejus, videlicet agni aut hœdi oblati (communiter tamen exstitit agnus), ac ponent super utrumque postem, id est, ambos januæ postes tingent sanguine illo, et in superliminaribus domorum, id est, etiam superliminaria domorum sic tingent, in quibus domibus comedent illum, utpote agnum aut hœdum oblatum atque assatum; fiebatque tinctio illa cum fasciculo hyssopi. Porro postes sunt ligna, inter quæ clauditur janua secundum longitudinem suam. Et superliminare vocatur, lignum seu limen superius, scilicet lignum transversaliter positum supra postes. Sicque in qualibet domo habitationis hominum, non brutorum, fiebat linitio illa cum sanguine, propter causam quæ infra in textu exprimitur.
paras.en: [[12:7|And they shall take of the blood thereof|Et sument de sanguine ejus]], namely of the lamb or kid offered (though commonly it was a lamb), [[12:7|and put it upon both the side posts|ac ponent super utrumque postem]], that is, they shall stain both posts of the door with that blood, [[12:7|and on the upper door posts of the houses|et in superliminaribus domorum]], that is, they shall stain the lintels of the houses too in the same way, [[12:7|wherein|in quibus]] houses [[12:7|they shall eat it|comedent illum]], that is, the lamb or kid offered and roasted; and that staining was done with a bunch of hyssop. Now the posts are the timbers between which the door is shut along its length. And the lintel [*superliminare*, the "upper threshold"] is the name for the upper timber or threshold, namely the timber laid crosswise above the posts. And so in every house where men, not beasts, dwelt, that smearing with blood was done, for the reason which is expressed below in the text.

paras.t: Et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni. Agnum namque seu hœdum oblatum in vespera, jussit Dominus paulo post igne assari, ad innuendum et recolendum, quod igne diuturnæ et maximæ tribulationis in Ægypto assati erant: et quoniam præparatio illa carnium, per assationem expeditius fieri potuit. Eadem enim nocte Ægyptii erant ad eos venturi, ut eos egredi cogerent. Et azymos panes, qui etiam celerius præparantur ex aquæ et farinæ commixtione. Jussi enim sunt agnum illum comedere, tanquam mox egressuri. Idcirco omnia paraverunt, prout velocius fieri valuit. Cum lactucis agrestibus: quæ sunt herbæ multum amaræ, quas cum carnibus edere jubebantur, ad reminiscendum amarissimæ afflictionis, quam in Ægypto erant perpessi. Non comedetis ex eo crudum quid, id est semicoctum ex festinatione. Nam et in Hebræo, ut fertur, semicoctum habetur. Voluit quippe Dominus cultores suos differre ab idololatris, qui aliqua idolis immolata, solebant comedere semicocta. Vel ad litteram, noluit Dominus, ut in tantum festinarent coquendo, quod semicoctum quid comederent, quum hoc corruptivum sit vitæ. Nec coctum aqua, id est, nihil de carnibus illis erit bullitum, vel quia idololatræ sic agebant, vel quoniam tardior est præparatio talis; sed assum tantum igni.
paras.en: [[12:8|And they shall eat the flesh that night roasted at the fire|Et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni]]. For the Lord commanded the lamb or kid offered in the evening to be roasted with fire a little after, to hint at and recall that they had been roasted in Egypt in the fire of a long and very great tribulation; and because that preparation of the flesh could be done more speedily by roasting, for that same night the Egyptians were to come to them to force them to go out. [[12:8|and unleavened bread|Et azymos panes]], which also are prepared more quickly, from a mixture of water and flour. For they were commanded to eat that lamb as men about to depart at once; therefore they prepared everything as quickly as could be done. [[12:8|with wild lettuce|Cum lactucis agrestibus]]: these are very bitter herbs, which they were commanded to eat with the flesh, in remembrance of the most bitter affliction which they had suffered in Egypt. [[12:9|You shall not eat thereof any thing raw|Non comedetis ex eo crudum quid]], that is, half-cooked through haste; for in the Hebrew too, so it is said, *half-cooked* is found. For the Lord willed His worshippers to differ from the idolaters, who used to eat some things offered to idols half-cooked. Or, according to the letter, the Lord did not wish them to hurry so much in cooking that they should eat something half-cooked, since this is harmful to life. [[12:9|nor boiled in water|Nec coctum aqua]], that is, none of that flesh shall be boiled, either because the idolaters did so, or because such preparation is slower; [[12:9|but only roasted at the fire|sed assum tantum igni]].

paras.t: Caput cum pedibus ejus et intestinis vorabitis. In Hebræo, secundum Lyram, non habetur, Vorabitis. Propter quod, secundum Hebræos, sensus est, quod caput cum pedibus, intestinisque agni primo lotis, erant assanda simul cum corpore agni, non seorsum, nec separatim: idcirco apparet quod translator adjunxit, Vorabitis, quia subjungitur, nec remanebit ex eo quidquam usque mane, id est, totum in ipsa nocte edetis, non tamen ossa, sed quidquid de carnibus eis adhæserit: ad insinuandum, quod valde mane fuerant exituri, nec tempus habituri ad manducandum, quia Ægyptii non sinebant eos aliquam facere moram. Ideo quoque dixit, Vorabitis, quoniam stando festinanter edebant. Si quid residuum fuerit comestioni, ejus comburetis: hoc est, taliter consumi […] per ignem, ut nihil remaneat. Quamvis autem præceperit Dominus, ut tot assumerentur ad comedendum, quod agnum comedere totum possent, in hoc tamen poterat error excusabilis intervenire, ita quod non poterant tantum comedere, sicut putabant se comesturos. Nec voluit Deus ut se ultra vires aut gulose replerent, ideo addidit istud.
paras.en: [[12:9|you shall eat the head with the feet and entrails thereof|Caput cum pedibus ejus et intestinis vorabitis]]. In the Hebrew, according to Lyra, *you shall eat* [*vorabitis*, literally "you shall devour"] is not found. Therefore according to the Hebrews the sense is that the head with the feet and entrails of the lamb, first washed, were to be roasted together with the body of the lamb, not apart or separately: and so it appears that the translator added *you shall eat*, because there follows: [[12:10|Neither shall there remain any thing of it until morning|nec remanebit ex eo quidquam usque mane]], that is, you shall eat it all in that very night, not the bones, however, but whatever of the flesh clings to them: to hint that they were to go out very early and would have no time for eating, because the Egyptians would not let them make any delay. He said *you shall eat* [*devour*] also because they ate standing and in haste. [[12:10|If there be any thing left|Si quid residuum fuerit]] from the eating, [[12:10|you shall burn it|ejus comburetis]]: that is, it shall be so consumed […] by fire that nothing remains. Now although the Lord commanded that so many be taken to eat that they could eat the whole lamb, yet an excusable error could come in here, so that they could not eat as much as they thought they would. And God did not will that they fill themselves beyond their strength or gluttonously; therefore He added this.

paras.t: Sic autem comedetis illum, scilicet agnum aut hœdum assatum: Renes vestros accingetis, et calceamenta habebitis in pedibus, tenentes baculos in manibus, et comedetis festinanter. Quorum omnium causa subjungitur: est enim Phase. Quid autem designat Phase, subjungitur: id est transitus Domini, quod translator apposuit. Hoc est, agnus iste paschalis seu manducatio ejus, vel paschalis ista celebritas, transitus Domini appellatur, vel transitum ejus designat: quia in illa hora filii Israel, Deo jubente, de Ægypto egressi sunt: præcipienteque Domino, angelus ejus pertransivit Ægyptios, primogenita occidendo, templa quoque et idola evertendo. Itaque, quoniam paschalis ille agnus et esus sic transitus Dei fuit, ideo filii Israel jussi sunt agnum comedere, tanquam mox transituri, et sicut vere parati ad emigrandum velociter. Ad quod pertinet esse accinctum, calceatum, baculoque provisum.
paras.en: [[12:11|And thus you shall eat it|Sic autem comedetis illum]], namely the lamb or kid roasted: [[12:11|you shall gird your reins, and you shall have shoes on your feet|Renes vestros accingetis, et calceamenta habebitis in pedibus]], [[12:11|holding staves in your hands, and you shall eat in haste|tenentes baculos in manibus, et comedetis festinanter]]. The cause of all these things is added: [[12:11|for it is the Phase|est enim Phase]]. And what *Phase* signifies is added: [[12:11|that is the Passage|id est transitus]] [[12:11|of the Lord|Domini]], which the translator put in. That is, this paschal lamb or the eating of it, or this paschal solemnity, is called the passage of the Lord, or signifies His passage: because at that hour the children of Israel went out of Egypt at God's command; and at the Lord's command His angel passed through the Egyptians, killing the firstborn and overturning the temples and idols too. So, since that paschal lamb and eating was thus the passage of God, the children of Israel were commanded to eat the lamb as men about to pass on at once, and as truly ready to depart quickly. To this belongs being girded, shod, and provided with a staff.

paras.t: Et transibo per terram Ægypti nocte illa, percutiamque omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti ab homine usque ad pecus inclusive, id est tam primogenita hominum, quam pecorum; et in cunctis diis Ægypti faciam judicia, id est, Ægyptiorum deos seu idola justo judicio destruam. Ista peregit Dominus, cujus magnitudinis non est finis, non in propria persona eundo aut locum mutando, vel ista per se immediate exsequendo, sed per angelum atque per suæ justitiæ operationem. Quocirca habetur in Glossa: Ferunt Hebræi, quod omnia idola Ægypti confracta sunt nocte illa, templa quoque vel terræ motu vel Nili inundatione. Recitat etiam Lyra: Dicunt Hebræi, quod nocte illa omnia idola Ægyptiorum lignea fuerunt subito putrefacta, et omnia metallina resoluta ac fusa in terram, omnia quoque lapidea comminuta, in idololatriæ detestationem, et in signum quod solus Hebræorum Deus fuit adorandus. Idcirco adjungit: Ego Dominus. Quasi dicat: Ego solus omnipotens sum, in cujus manu cuncta sunt posita, quem solum decet latriæ cultus, tanquam summum et incomparabilem Dominum, qui ait per Isaiam: Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum. Gloriam meam alteri non dabo, nec laudem meam sculptilibus.
paras.en: [[12:12|And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night|Et transibo per terram Ægypti nocte illa]], [[12:12|and will kill every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast|percutiamque omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti ab homine usque ad pecus]] inclusive, that is, the firstborn both of men and of beasts; [[12:12|and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments|et in cunctis diis Ægypti faciam judicia]], that is, I will destroy the gods or idols of the Egyptians by a just judgment. The Lord, of whose greatness there is no end, accomplished these things, not by going in His own person or changing place, or by carrying them out immediately by Himself, but through an angel and through the working of His justice. Hence it is said in the Gloss: The Hebrews say that all the idols of Egypt were broken that night, and the temples too, either by an earthquake or by the flooding of the Nile. Lyra also relates: The Hebrews say that that night all the wooden idols of the Egyptians suddenly rotted, and all the metal ones melted and ran out on the ground, and all the stone ones were broken in pieces, in detestation of idolatry and as a sign that the God of the Hebrews alone was to be adored. Therefore he adds: [[12:12|I am the Lord|Ego Dominus]]. As if he should say: I alone am almighty, in whose hand all things are placed, to whom alone the worship of latria [the worship due to God alone] is fitting, as the supreme and incomparable Lord, who says by Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to graven things|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum. Gloriam meam alteri non dabo, nec laudem meam sculptilibus]] [the margin gives Is. xiii, 8; the passage is Is 42:8].

paras.t: Consequenter panditur causa linitionis postium ac superliminarium cum sanguine agni oblati. Erit autem sanguis vobis in signum in ædibus in quibus eritis, id est, linitio illa cum sanguine in domibus habitationum vestrarum, erit vobis in liberationem de manu angeli primogenita occidentis. Ideo subditur: et videbo sanguinem, id est, tinctionem illam cum sanguine, gratam habeo, in quantum ex mea jussione a vobis peracta est, et redemptionem mundi per sanguinem Christi significat: distinctivumque signum fuit inter Hebræos atque Ægyptios, quos voluit Dominus hoc signo foris distingui, quemadmodum intus distinguebantur per fidem et religionem ab invicem; et transibo vos, id est, domos vestras pertransibo, nullum in eis percutiendo. Ideo subditur: nec erit in vobis plaga disperdens, id est percussio primogenita occidens, quando percussero terram Ægypti, hoc est primogenita Ægyptiorum.
paras.en: Next is set out the reason for smearing the posts and lintels with the blood of the lamb offered. [[12:13|And the blood shall be unto you for a sign in the houses where you shall be|Erit autem sanguis vobis in signum in ædibus in quibus eritis]], that is, that smearing with blood in the houses where you dwell shall be for your deliverance from the hand of the angel who kills the firstborn. Therefore it is added: [[12:13|and I shall see the blood|et videbo sanguinem]], that is, I hold that staining with blood pleasing, inasmuch as it has been done by you at My command and signifies the redemption of the world by the blood of Christ; and it was a distinguishing sign between the Hebrews and the Egyptians, whom the Lord willed to be distinguished outwardly by this sign, as inwardly they were distinguished from one another by faith and religion; [[12:13|and shall pass over you|et transibo vos]], that is, I will pass over your houses, striking no one in them. Therefore it is added: [[12:13|and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you|nec erit in vobis plaga disperdens]], that is, the stroke that kills the firstborn, [[12:13|when I shall strike the land of Egypt|quando percussero terram Ægypti]], that is, the firstborn of the Egyptians.

paras.t: Habebitis autem hunc diem vestræ egressionis de Ægypto, et liberationis a morte primitivorum, in monumentum, id est in jugi memoria, non obliviscendo beneficiorum tantorum; et celebrabitis eam solennem Domino in generationibus vestris, id est, tam vos quam posteri vestri omni anno festivum agetis hunc diem, in commemorationem beneficiorum vobis in eo desuper præstitorum, ut datori eorum sitis grati; cultu sempiterno, id est perpetue, statu veteris Testamenti durante. Circa hoc loquitur Augustinus: Diligenter scrutandum est, quomodo Scriptura soleat appellare æternum, quoniam nefas habet hoc prætermittere aut mutare. Aliud enim est, quum præcipitur quamdiu aliquid fiat, sic ut præceptum est, ut arca septies circuiret Jericho muros. Aliud, quum aliquid præcipitur sic observari, ut nullus terminus præfigatur. Aut ergo sic appellavit scriptura ista, æternum, ut filii Israel illud non auderent prætermittere sponte: aut quia æternum est, quod per illam celebritatem paschalem significatur. Hinc alii sic exponunt, Cultu sempiterno, id est absque certa temporis determinatione: quia paschalis solennitas, quantum ad id quod significabatur per eam, perfectius observatur in evangelica, quam in Mosaica lege, quantum lux et veritas transcendit figuram et umbram. Nam omnia in figura tunc contingebant.
paras.en: [[12:14|And this day|Habebitis autem hunc diem]] of your going out of Egypt and of your deliverance from the death of the firstborn [[12:14|shall be for a memorial to you|in monumentum]], that is, in constant remembrance, not forgetting such great benefits; [[12:14|and you shall keep it a feast to the Lord in your generations|et celebrabitis eam solennem Domino in generationibus vestris]], that is, both you and your descendants shall keep this day as a feast every year, in commemoration of the benefits bestowed on you from above on it, that you may be grateful to their Giver; [[12:14|with an everlasting observance|cultu sempiterno]], that is, perpetually, while the state of the Old Testament lasts. On this Augustine says: We must examine carefully how Scripture is wont to call a thing eternal, since it holds it wrong to omit or change this. For it is one thing when it is commanded how long something is to be done, as it was commanded that the ark should go round the walls of Jericho seven times[[Jos 6:4||]]; another when something is commanded to be observed in such a way that no term is fixed. Either, then, this scripture called it eternal so that the children of Israel would not dare to omit it of their own will; or because what is signified by that paschal solemnity is eternal. Hence others expound thus: [[12:14|with an everlasting observance|Cultu sempiterno]], that is, without a fixed limit of time: because the paschal solemnity, as to what was signified by it, is more perfectly observed in the law of the Gospel than in the Mosaic law, by as much as light and truth surpass figure and shadow. For then [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|omnia in figura tunc contingebant]].

paras.t: Porro, ut Rabbi Paulus affirmat, in Hebræo habetur, In sæculum. Unde sensus in Hebraico proprius iste est: Celebrabitis diem hanc solennem in sæculum. Sæculum autem apud Hebræos, sicut et apud nos, ponitur pro quolibet spatio temporis determinantis durationem vitæ alicujus. Unde et in Scripturis duratio totius temporis vitæ præsentis, sæculum nuncupatur. Et duratio vitæ futuræ, dicitur aliud sæculum per se. Sicque intelligitur illud, Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel a sæculo et in sæculum. Et illud in Symbolo: Et vitam venturi sæculi. Hinc antiqui Hebræi totum tempus durationis Mosaicæ legis, unum sæculum vocant, et tempus Messiæ aliud sæculum, propter distinctionem eorum quæ in utroque sæculo ad spiritualem pertinent vitam. Unde quum in præceptis hujusmodi, præsertim cærimonialibus, additur, Et in sæculum: intelligendum est de toto tempore durationis Mosaicæ legis, quæ est usque ad aliud sæculum, scilicet usque ad tempus Messiæ et durationis legis ipsius. Et iste est modus respondendi proprius Hebræis, quum de evacuatione cærimonialium agitur: qui modus loquendi de duplici sæculo, communiter tenetur etiam a Talmudistis in variis locis. Hæc Rabbi Paulus.
paras.en: Further, as Rabbi Paul affirms, the Hebrew has *for ever* [*in sæculum*, literally "unto the age"]. Hence the proper sense in the Hebrew is this: You shall keep this day solemn for ever. Now *sæculum* [age, world], among the Hebrews as among us, is used for any space of time that bounds the duration of the life of something. Hence in the Scriptures, too, the duration of the whole time of the present life is called a *sæculum*, and the duration of the life to come is called another *sæculum* in its own right. And so is understood that verse: [[Ps 40:14|Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity|Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel a sæculo et in sæculum]] [Latin *a sæculo et in sæculum*, literally "from age to age"]; and that in the Creed: And the life of the world to come [*venturi sæculi*, of the age to come]. Hence the ancient Hebrews call the whole time that the Mosaic law lasts one age, and the time of the Messias another age, because of the difference between the things that belong to the spiritual life in each age. Hence when in precepts of this kind, especially ceremonial ones, *and for ever* is added, it is to be understood of the whole time that the Mosaic law lasts, which is until the other age, namely until the time of the Messias and of the duration of his law. And this is the way of answering proper to the Hebrews when the abolition of the ceremonies is discussed: and this way of speaking of a twofold age is commonly held by the Talmudists too, in various places. Thus far Rabbi Paul.

paras.t: Septem diebus azyma comedetis, id est panes non fermentatos. Et incipiebantur dies illi ab hora immolationis agni paschalis, quem cum talibus panibus edere tenebantur. A die primo non erit fermentatum in domibus vestris ; hoc est, a præfato quartodecimo die mensis Nisan, non erit in domibus Hebræorum panis fermentatus, neque fermentum, ita quod ante horam vespertinam in qua agnus offerebatur, tollendum fuit ab eorum habitaculis omne fermentum ac fermentatum. Quicumque Hebræorum comederit fermentatum a die primo, id est ab hora vespertina præfati diei, usque ad diem septimum inclusive, quia nec in eo hoc licuit, peribit anima illa de Israel, id est, homo hoc faciens, peccabit mortaliter atque damnabitur, nec inter electos computabitur Israelitas, nisi pœnitentiam egerit. Porro primus dies ille fuit dies quartusdecimus primi mensis Hebræorum, et dies septimus fuit dies vicesimus primus ejusdem mensis.
paras.en: [[12:15|Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread|Septem diebus azyma comedetis]], that is, loaves not leavened. And those days began from the hour when the paschal lamb was sacrificed, which they were bound to eat with such loaves. [[12:15|in the first day there shall be no leaven in your houses|A die primo non erit fermentatum in domibus vestris]]; that is, from the aforesaid fourteenth day of the month Nisan there shall be no leavened bread, nor leaven, in the houses of the Hebrews, so that before the evening hour in which the lamb was offered all leaven and everything leavened had to be removed from their dwellings. [[12:15|whosoever|Quicumque]] of the Hebrews [[12:15|shall eat any thing leavened, from the first day|comederit fermentatum a die primo]], that is, from the evening hour of the aforesaid day, [[12:15|until the seventh day|usque ad diem septimum]] inclusive, since this was not lawful on that day either, [[12:15|that soul shall perish out of Israel|peribit anima illa de Israel]]: that is, the man who does this shall sin mortally and be damned, and shall not be counted among the chosen Israelites, unless he do penance. Now that first day was the fourteenth day of the first month of the Hebrews, and the seventh day was the twenty-first day of the same month.

paras.t: Dies prima erit sancta atque solennis, id est deputata actibus sacris ad agnum paschalem spectantibus. Incepitque illa solennitas a vespera primæ diei, in qua agnus immolabatur. Et dies septima eadem festivitate venerabilis erit, qua dies prima. Illam tamen celebritatem pro magna parte agebant in exterioribus et carnalibus quibusdam eminentiis, ut in ornato vestitu, lautisque refectionibus, juxta illud in Esdra : Ite, comedite pinguia, et bibite mulsum. Dies enim Domini sanctus est. Fuit namque lex illa grossa et figuralis, non perfecta et spiritualis, sed juxta capacitatem populi et congruentiam temporis data. Propter quod ait Apostolus : Nihil ad perfectum adduxit lex. Nihil operis servilis et exterioris facietis in eis per vos ipsos, neque per vestros ministros, exceptis his quæ ad vescendum pertinent, id est ad præparationem ciborum. Ex his elicitur, quod diebus intermediis poterant operari, ut in Scholastica legitur historia. Patet quoque ex his, quod sabbati celebritas strictius servabatur quam ista, quantum ad cessationem ab opere. Unde et si solennitas ista venit in sabbato, non licuit in ea cibaria parare.
paras.en: [[12:16|The first day shall be holy and solemn|Dies prima erit sancta atque solennis]], that is, set apart for the sacred acts belonging to the paschal lamb. And that solemnity began from the evening of the first day, in which the lamb was sacrificed. [[12:16|and the seventh day shall be kept with the like solemnity|Et dies septima eadem festivitate venerabilis]] as the first day. Yet they kept that feast in great part with certain outward and carnal shows, such as fine clothing and sumptuous meals, according to that word in Esdras: [[2 Esd 8:10|Go, eat fat meats, and drink sweet wine|Ite, comedite pinguia, et bibite mulsum]]; [[2 Esd 8:10|because it is the holy day of the Lord|Dies enim Domini sanctus est]]. For that law was coarse and figurative, not perfect and spiritual, but given according to the capacity of the people and what befitted the time. Wherefore the Apostle says: [[Heb 7:19|the law brought nothing to perfection|Nihil ad perfectum adduxit lex]]. [[12:16|you shall do no work|Nihil operis]] (servile and outward work) [[12:16|in them|facietis in eis]], either by yourselves or by your servants, [[12:16|except those things that belong to eating|exceptis his quæ ad vescendum pertinent]], that is, to the preparing of food. From this it is gathered that they could work on the days in between, as we read in the Scholastic History [of Peter Comestor]. It is plain also from this that the feast of the sabbath was kept more strictly than this one, as regards ceasing from work. Hence, if this solemnity fell on a sabbath, it was not lawful to prepare food on it.

paras.t: Et observabitis azyma, id est esum azymorum panum, septem diebus, ut patuit. In eadem enim ipsa die, videlicet die quintadecima primi mensis, ad quam diem pertinebat vespera præcedentis diei, quia ab illa vespera cœpit, ut dictum est, educam exercitum vestrum, id est vos ipsos per modum exercitus congrue adunatos ac ordinatos, de terra Ægypti, et custodietis diem istum in generationibus vestris, id est, diem celebrabitis vos et posteri vestri tempore opportuno per successiones generationum vestrarum, ritu perpetuo. Tamen, ut dicunt Catholici et Hebræi, quemadmodum dispensatum fuit cum Israelitis, quod non circumcidebantur quamdiu fuerunt in deserto, ita et in observatione hujus præcepti, ita quod in deserto non leguntur Pascha hoc celebrasse nisi semel, videlicet in anno secundo egressionis ab Ægypto, ut infra habebitur. Nempe quamdiu fuerant in deserto, satis memores erant egressionis illius, idcirco ob illam commemorandam rationabiliter fuit dilata celebratio illa.
paras.en: [[12:17|And you shall observe the feast of the unleavened bread|Et observabitis azyma]], that is, the eating of unleavened loaves, for seven days, as has been shown. [[12:17|for in this same day|In eadem enim ipsa die]], namely the fifteenth day of the first month, to which the evening of the preceding day belonged, because it began from that evening, as was said, [[12:17|I will bring forth your army|educam exercitum vestrum]], that is, yourselves, fittingly gathered and ordered in the manner of an army, [[12:17|out of the land of Egypt, and you shall keep this day in your generations|de terra Ægypti, et custodietis diem istum in generationibus vestris]], that is, you and your descendants shall celebrate the day at its due time through the succession of your generations, [[12:17|by a perpetual observance|ritu perpetuo]]. Yet, as both Catholics and Hebrews say, just as the Israelites were dispensed from circumcision as long as they were in the desert, so too in the keeping of this precept; so that in the desert they are not read to have celebrated this Pasch except once, namely in the second year after the going out from Egypt, as will be seen below. For as long as they were in the desert they were mindful enough of that going out; therefore the celebration meant to commemorate it was reasonably put off.

paras.t: Primo mense, qui dicitur Aprilis vel Martius apud nos, et Nisan apud Judæos, quartadecima die mensis hujus ad vesperam comedetis azyma, usque ad diem vicesimam primam ejusdem mensis ad vesperum : forsitan exclusive, quia dies illa vicesima prima terminabatur in exordio vesperæ suæ, quæ et pertinuit ad diem sequentem. Septem diebus fermentatum non invenietur in domibus vestris : id est, hoc jubeo, ut non solum non manducetur, sed neque exsistat in habitaculis vestris. Qui comederit fermentatum infra hos septem dies, peribit anima ejus de cœtu Israel, sicut expositum est, tam de advenis quam de indigenis terræ, hoc est, sive fuerit proselytus, sive natione Hebræus. Itaque per advenas intelliguntur ad Judaismum conversi. Omne fermentatum non comedetis. In cunctis habitaculis vestris edetis azyma. Frequenter legislator unum et idem resumit, ut strictius observetur in memoria et effectu.
paras.en: [[12:18|The first month|Primo mense]], which with us is called April or March, and with the Jews Nisan, [[12:18|the fourteenth day of the month|quartadecima die mensis]], of this month, [[12:18|in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the same month, in the evening|ad vesperam comedetis azyma, usque ad diem vicesimam primam ejusdem mensis ad vesperum]]: perhaps exclusively, because that twenty-first day ended at the beginning of its evening, which belonged to the following day. [[12:19|Seven days there shall not be found any leaven in your houses|Septem diebus fermentatum non invenietur in domibus vestris]]: that is, I command this, that it be not only not eaten, but not even present in your dwellings. [[12:19|he that shall eat leavened bread|Qui comederit fermentatum]] within these seven days, [[12:19|his soul shall perish out of the assembly of Israel|peribit anima ejus de cœtu Israel]], as has been explained, [[12:19|whether he be a stranger or born in the land|tam de advenis quam de indigenis terræ]]: that is, whether he be a proselyte or a Hebrew by birth. So by strangers are understood those converted to Judaism. [[12:20|You shall not eat any thing leavened|Omne fermentatum non comedetis]]. [[12:20|in all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread|In cunctis habitaculis vestris edetis azyma]]. The lawgiver often repeats one and the same thing, so that it may be kept more strictly in memory and in deed.

paras.t: Vocavit autem Moyses omnes seniores filiorum Israel, scilicet patresfamilias et principales, ad quos pertinebat agnum aut hædum offerre : et dixit ad eos : Ite, tollentes animal per familias vestras, id est, unusquisque in sua familia principalis, pergat ad domum seu gregem suum, et inde accipiat agnum, si potest, vel hædum, et immolate Phase, id est agnum paschalem, qui transitum Domini repræsentet, juxta sensum præhabitum. Fasciculumque hyssopi intingite in sanguine, qui est in limine, id est in sanguine agni vel hædi oblati, reservato et exsistente in vase circa limen domus, et adspergite ex eo superliminare et utrumque postem. Ut tangit Augustinus, sanguis recipiebatur in vase, et vas illud cum sanguine ponebatur juxta limen, quia ex eo liniendi erant postes et superliminare. Unde, ut dicitur, in Hebræo habetur. In catino, id est vase argenteo, in quo recipiebatur sanguis agni oblati. Porro, ad fasciculum requiruntur ad minus tres calami colligati, ut fertur. Cur autem tinctio illa fiebat per fasciculum hyssopi, ad litteram dici potest, quod propter munditiam herbæ illius, et reverentiam oblationis ad Dei honorem, vel propter convenientiam proprietatum hyssopi, cum proprietatibus agni, de quibus dicetur sequenti articulo. Nullus vestrum egrediatur ostium domus suæ usque mane. Cujus causa subjungitur : Transibit enim Dominus percutiens Ægyptios, per ministerium angeli. Quumque viderit, id est esse cognoverit et approbaverit, sanguinem in superliminari, et in utroque poste ostii domorum vestrarum, transcendet ostium domus ipse angelus ; et non sinet percussorem, videlicet angelum, ingredi domus vestras, et lædere : id est, præcipiet angelo, ut neminem vestrum lædat. Cur Deus præcepit neminem Hebræorum egredi domum suam nocte illa? numquid, ne angelus per errorem aut ignorantiam occideret eum? Non utique. An forsan ideo, ne Ægyptii prope Hebræos commorantes, perciperent et suspicarentur aliquid mali per Hebræos nocturno tempore esse patratum?
paras.en: [[12:21|And Moses called all the ancients of the children of Israel|Vocavit autem Moyses omnes seniores filiorum Israel]], namely the fathers of families and the heads of houses, to whom it belonged to offer the lamb or kid: [[12:21|and said to them: Go take a lamb by your families|et dixit ad eos : Ite, tollentes animal per familias vestras]] [Denis's text, with the Vulgate, has *animal*, "the beast"], that is, let each head in his own family go to his house or flock and take from it a lamb if he can, or else a kid, [[12:21|and sacrifice the Phase|et immolate Phase]], that is, the paschal lamb, which is to represent the passing of the Lord, in the sense given above.
