[[12:22|And dip a bunch of hyssop in the blood that is at the door|Fasciculumque hyssopi intingite in sanguine, qui est in limine]] [literally "on the threshold"], that is, in the blood of the lamb or kid offered, kept and standing in a vessel by the threshold of the house, [[12:22|and sprinkle the transom of the door therewith, and both the door cheeks|et adspergite ex eo superliminare et utrumque postem]]. As Augustine touches on it, the blood was caught in a vessel, and that vessel with the blood was set by the threshold, because the posts and the transom were to be smeared from it. Hence, as is said, the Hebrew has: In the basin, that is, in a vessel of silver, in which the blood of the lamb offered was caught. Further, for a bunch at least three stalks tied together are required, as it is said. As to why that dipping was done with a bunch of hyssop, it can be said according to the letter that it was because of the cleanness of that herb and out of reverence for an offering made to the honour of God, or because the properties of hyssop agree with the properties of the lamb, of which we shall speak in the next article. [[12:22|let none of you go out of the door of his house till morning|Nullus vestrum egrediatur ostium domus suæ usque mane]]. The reason for this is added: [[12:23|For the Lord will pass through striking the Egyptians|Transibit enim Dominus percutiens Ægyptios]], by the ministry of an angel. [[12:23|and when he shall see|Quumque viderit]], that is, shall know it to be there and approve it, [[12:23|the blood on the transom, and on both the posts|sanguinem in superliminari, et in utroque poste]] of the door of your houses, [[12:23|he will pass over the door of the house|transcendet ostium domus]], the angel himself; [[12:23|and not suffer the destroyer|et non sinet percussorem]], namely the angel, [[12:23|to come into your houses and to hurt you|ingredi domus vestras, et lædere]]: that is, he will command the angel to hurt none of you. Why did God command that none of the Hebrews should go out of his house that night? Was it lest the angel through error or ignorance should kill him? Surely not. Or was it perhaps lest the Egyptians living near the Hebrews should perceive, and suspect, that some evil had been done by the Hebrews in the night-time?

paras.t: Deinde Moyses ad unumquemque loquitur Hebræorum patrum : Custodi verbum istud, id est præceptum de oblatione et celebritate paschali, legitimum, id est juste impositum, tibi et filiis tuis usque in æternum, id est per omne tempus durationis tuæ, sicut expositum est. Quumque introieritis terram, quam Dominus Deus daturus est vobis ut pollicitus est, observabitis cærimonias istas, id est ritum istum et modum colendi Deum, observantiasque prætactas figurativas. Verumtamen isti quibus Moyses loquebatur, non introierunt in propria persona terram promissam, quæ et sub conditione fuit eis promissa, videlicet si non demererentur ejus ingressum, sed sub personis eorum, loquitur posteris eorumdem. Et quum dixerint vobis filii vestri, Quæ est ista religio? id est, legalis observantia seu veneratio Dei, actusque latriæ ad quam sacrificium pertinet. Solet autem religio pro latria accipi. Dicetis eis : Victima transitus Domini est : hoc est, immolatio et celebratio ista paschalis, est memorativa transitus Dei seu angeli ejus : quando transivit super domos filiorum Israel, id est habitacula eorum transiliit, in Ægypto, percutiens Ægyptios, et domos nostras liberans, id est habitatores domorum nostrarum ab illa percussione præservans. Incurvatusque populus adoravit, id est, populus Israeliticus, his auditis, gratias egit Deo cum inclinatione, oravitque eum, ut ista impleret.
paras.en: Then Moses speaks to each one of the fathers of the Hebrews: [[12:24|Thou shalt keep this thing|Custodi verbum istud]], that is, the precept about the paschal offering and feast, [[12:24|as a law|legitimum]], that is, justly imposed, [[12:24|for thee and thy children for ever|tibi et filiis tuis usque in æternum]], that is, through the whole time of thy lasting, as has been explained. [[12:25|And when you have entered into the land which the Lord will give you, as he hath promised, you shall observe these ceremonies|Quumque introieritis terram, quam Dominus Deus daturus est vobis ut pollicitus est, observabitis cærimonias istas]], that is, this rite and manner of worshipping God, and the figurative observances touched on above. Yet those to whom Moses was speaking did not enter the promised land in their own persons (it was also promised them under a condition, namely if they did not forfeit their entry into it); but in their persons he speaks to their descendants. [[12:26|And when your children shall say to you: What is the meaning of this service?|Et quum dixerint vobis filii vestri, Quæ est ista religio?]], that is, this legal observance or worship of God, and act of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], to which sacrifice belongs. For *religio* [here rendered "service"] is wont to be taken for latria. [[12:27|You shall say to them: It is the victim of the passage of the Lord|Dicetis eis : Victima transitus Domini est]]: that is, this paschal sacrifice and feast is a memorial of the passing of God or of his angel, [[12:27|when he passed over the houses of the children of Israel|quando transivit super domos filiorum Israel]], that is, leapt over their dwellings, [[12:27|in Egypt, striking the Egyptians, and saving our houses|in Ægypto, percutiens Ægyptios, et domos nostras liberans]], that is, preserving the dwellers in our houses from that stroke. [[12:27|And the people bowing themselves, adored|Incurvatusque populus adoravit]]: that is, the people of Israel, having heard these things, gave thanks to God with a bow, and prayed him to fulfil them.

paras.t: Factum est autem in noctis medio, in cujus noctis initio comestus fuit agnus paschalis, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito Pharaonis qui sedebat in solio ejus, usque ad primogenitum captivæ quæ erat in carcere, hoc est, inclusive usque ad primogenitum cujuscumque infimæ atque vilissimæ mulieris Ægyptiæ, et omne primogenitum jumentorum, videlicet primogenitam ovem in grege ovium, primogenitum equum in specie equorum, etc. Et si in domo aliqua non fuit nisi unigenitus, ille fuit percussus : quod et de jumentis sentiendum videtur. Sicque primogenitus non distinguitur nunc contra unigenitum, sed contra secundogenitum, quemadmodum in Evangelio Christifera Virgo scribitur peperisse Filium suum primogenitum. Porro secundum doctores, Deus sic ordinavit atque providit, quod in qualibet domo Ægyptiorum, fuit primogenitus aut unigenitus aliquis : quod tamen videtur non parum mirabile in tanto regno. Apparet vero, quod quamvis in aliquibus domibus non fuisset nisi vir unus, vel uxoratus vel non uxoratus, ille fuisset primogenitus domus illius, non quod haberet parentes viventes, sed quia in domo sua nullus senior eo, seu ante ipsum natus exsistens. Surrexitque Pharao nocte et omnes servi ejus, cunctaque Ægyptus, id est ceteri Ægyptii ad surgendum dispositi ; et ortus est clamor magnus in Ægypto : quia ex dolore plagæ inflictæ, et ex timore plagæ gravioris futuræ, clamabant et ululabant. Neque enim erat domus in qua non jaceret mortuus, id est, in qualibet domo habitationis Ægyptiorum, jacuit ad minus unus occisus. Et si in una domo habitaverunt plures primogeniti diversorum parentum, erant in una domo plures sic mortui. Quamvis autem occisio seu mors illa fuit secundum Augustinum occulto angelicoque percussu, poterant tamen viventes faciliter aliquo signo cognoscere mortem sic percussorum.
paras.en: [[12:29|And it came to pass at midnight|Factum est autem in noctis medio]] (at the beginning of which night the paschal lamb had been eaten), [[12:29|the Lord slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharao, who sat on his throne, unto the firstborn of the captive woman that was in the prison|percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito Pharaonis qui sedebat in solio ejus, usque ad primogenitum captivæ quæ erat in carcere]]: that is, down to and including the firstborn of any Egyptian woman, however low and base, [[12:29|and all the firstborn of cattle|et omne primogenitum jumentorum]], namely the firstborn sheep in a flock of sheep, the firstborn horse among horses, etc. And if in any house there was only an only-begotten, he was struck: and the same seems to be meant of the beasts. And so *firstborn* is not here set against *only-begotten*, but against *second-born*, as in the Gospel the Virgin who bore Christ is written to have [[Luke 2:7|brought forth her first born son|peperisse Filium suum primogenitum]]. Further, according to the doctors, God so ordained and provided that in every house of the Egyptians there was some firstborn or only-begotten: which nevertheless seems no small wonder in so great a kingdom. But it appears that even if in some houses there was only one man, married or unmarried, he would have been the firstborn of that house: not that he had living parents, but because in his house there was no one older than he, or born before him. [[12:30|And Pharao arose in the night, and all his servants, and all Egypt|Surrexitque Pharao nocte et omnes servi ejus, cunctaque Ægyptus]], that is, the rest of the Egyptians who were minded to rise; [[12:30|and there arose a great cry in Egypt|et ortus est clamor magnus in Ægypto]]: for they cried and howled from grief at the plague inflicted, and from fear of a heavier plague to come. [[12:30|for there was not a house wherein there lay not one dead|Neque enim erat domus in qua non jaceret mortuus]]: that is, in every house where Egyptians dwelt there lay at least one slain. And if several firstborn of different parents lived in one house, there were several so dead in one house. And although that slaying or death was, according to Augustine, by a hidden stroke of an angel, the living could nevertheless easily know by some sign the death of those thus struck.

paras.t: Vocatisque Pharao Moyse et Aaron nocte, ait. Pharao per nuntios Moysen Aaronque vocavit, et sequentia verba per eosdem nuntios protulit eis. Præterea quamvis Deus per Moysen jusserat, ut nullus filiorum Israel egrederetur domum suam in nocte illa, Moyses tamen et Aaron vocati, forsitan ex Dei dispensatione, exierunt ad Pharaonis ministros aut infra domum manentes audierunt alloquebanturque ipsos. Surgite, egredimini a populo meo, et vos et filii Israel. Ite, et immolate Domino sicut dicitis. Oves vestras, et armenta assumite, ut petieratis; et abeuntes, benedicite mihi, id est, gratias agite quod ita licentio vos, vel benedicite mihi, imprecando mihi bona, ne plura flagella super me et subditos meos Ægyptios veniant. Urgebantque Ægyptii populum Hebræorum exire de terra velociter, scilicet summo mane, dicentes: Omnes moriemur, id est, percutiemur ad mortem, sicut primogenita nostra percussa sunt, si isti Hebræi tardaverint apud nos. De hoc tamen non fuit periculum, quia non tenuissent Hebræos secum contra Dei præceptum. Et ut Josephus refert, flebant, veniamque petebant Ægyptii pro eo, quod ita afflixerunt Hebræos.
paras.en: [[12:31|And Pharao calling Moses and Aaron, in the night, said|Vocatisque Pharao Moyse et Aaron nocte, ait]]. Pharao called Moses and Aaron through messengers, and spoke the following words to them through the same messengers. Moreover, although God had commanded through Moses that none of the children of Israel should go out of his house that night, Moses and Aaron, when called, perhaps by God's dispensation, went out to Pharao's ministers; or else, staying within the house, they heard them and spoke with them. [[12:31|Arise and go forth from among my people, you and the children of Israel|Surgite, egredimini a populo meo, et vos et filii Israel]]: [[12:31|go, sacrifice to the Lord as you say|Ite, et immolate Domino sicut dicitis]]. [[12:32|Your sheep and herds take along with you, as you demanded, and departing bless me|Oves vestras, et armenta assumite, ut petieratis; et abeuntes, benedicite mihi]]: that is, give thanks that I thus let you go; or, bless me by calling down good things upon me, so that no more scourges come upon me and upon the Egyptians my subjects. [[12:33|And the Egyptians pressed the people|Urgebantque Ægyptii populum]] of the Hebrews [[12:33|to go forth out of the land speedily|exire de terra velociter]], namely at earliest morning, [[12:33|saying: We shall all die|dicentes: Omnes moriemur]]: that is, we shall be struck to death, as our firstborn have been struck, if these Hebrews delay among us. Yet there was no danger of this, for they would not have kept the Hebrews with them against God's command. And as Josephus relates, the Egyptians wept and asked pardon for having so afflicted the Hebrews.

paras.t: Tulit ergo populus conspersam farinam, id est aqua permixtam, antequam fermentaretur: quia præ festinatione non habuerunt tempus fermentandi; et ligans farinam ita conspersam in palliis, ne deflueret, posuit super humeros suos. Feceruntque filii Israel sicut præcepit Dominus Moysi, id est ipsis per Moysen, et ipsi Moysi ut præciperet eis. Et petierunt ab Ægyptiis sibi vicinis, vasa argentea et aurea, vestemque plurimam. Dominus autem dedit gratiam populo coram Ægyptiis, ut commodarent eis; et spoliaverunt Ægyptios. Istud jam sæpe præhabitum est, atque expositum: Et spoliaverunt Ægyptios, id est, divitias istas tulerunt ab eis, non tamen per injustitiam, aut rapinam, aut violentiam aliquam, sed ex commissione divina, quia Dei sunt omnia, et cui vult aufert ea, et cui vult tribuit ea. Ægyptii quoque meruerunt hæc sibi auferri, et filii Israel serviendo Ægyptiis gratis, meruerunt hanc mercedem suscipere. Idcirco non fuit spoliatio proprie, sed per similitudinem quamdam. Unde spoliare sumitur hic extense.
paras.en: [[12:34|The people therefore took dough|Tulit ergo populus conspersam farinam]] [literally "sprinkled meal"], that is, meal mixed with water, [[12:34|before it was leavened|antequam fermentaretur]]: for in their haste they had no time to leaven it; [[12:34|and tying it|et ligans]], the meal so mixed, [[12:34|in their cloaks|in palliis]], lest it run out, [[12:34|put it on their shoulders|posuit super humeros suos]]. [[12:35|And the children of Israel did as|Feceruntque filii Israel sicut]] the Lord commanded Moses [so Denis's text, as in v. 28; the Vulgate here has "as Moses had commanded"], that is, commanded them through Moses, and commanded Moses himself to command them. [[12:35|and they asked of the Egyptians|Et petierunt ab Ægyptiis]], their neighbours, [[12:35|vessels of silver and gold, and very much raiment|vasa argentea et aurea, vestemque plurimam]]. [[12:36|And the Lord gave favour to the people in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them|Dominus autem dedit gratiam populo coram Ægyptiis, ut commodarent eis]]; [[12:36|and they stripped the Egyptians|et spoliaverunt Ægyptios]]. This has already often come up before and been explained: [[12:36|and they stripped the Egyptians|Et spoliaverunt Ægyptios]], that is, they took these riches from them, yet not by injustice, or robbery, or any violence, but by divine commission; for all things are God's, and he takes them from whom he will, and gives them to whom he will. The Egyptians also deserved to have these things taken from them, and the children of Israel, by serving the Egyptians without pay, deserved to receive this wage. Therefore it was not properly a spoiling, but by a certain likeness. Hence *to strip* is taken here in a wide sense.

paras.t: Profectique sunt filii Israel de Ramesse in Socoth, id est, de terra Gessen exeuntes, primo castrametati sunt seu tabernacula sua fixerunt in loco Socoth vocato: qui locus est alius a loco in quo Jacob de Mesopotamia rediens, fixit in terra Chanaan mansionem, quem et Socoth, id est tabernacula, nuncupavit, ut in Genesi legitur: sexcenta fere millia peditum virorum, absque parvulis et mulieribus, id est, quasi sexcenta millia virorum Hebræorum pedestrium pugnatorum egressa sunt, inter quos parvuli seu pueri qui infra viginti annos erant, et mulieres, computati non sunt. Qualiter autem populus Israel potuit ita multiplicari in Ægypto infra annos quibus ibi morati sunt, discussum est in expositione primi capituli hujus libri. Sed et vulgus promiscuum innumerabile ascendit cum eis, id est, Ægyptii utriusque sexus ultra modum multi, associaverunt se Hebræis. Nam visis tot signis, relicta idololatria, crediderunt in Deum verum, et cum filiis Israel exierunt Ægyptum in solitudinem, quæ altior erat Ægypto in situ: propter quod ascendisse dicuntur. Et vulgus illud, secundum Scholasticam historiam, famulabatur Hebræis. Et multi Ægyptiorum fleverunt, quia tam duri fuerunt Hebræis. Coxeruntque farinam, quam dudum de Ægypto conspersam tulerant, videlicet primo die suæ egressionis, et fecerunt ex eo subcinericios panes azymos: in loco qui dicitur Socoth aut circiter. Neque enim poterant fermentari ob temporis brevitatem ipsi panes, seu farinæ conspersæ aut massæ, ex quibus facti sunt panes, cogentibus exire ipsos Hebræos Ægyptiis, et nullam facere sinentibus moram, nec pulmenti quidquam occurrerat præparare, id est, filiis Israel non vacabat coquere quidquam pulmenti aut confectionis propter importunam illam coactionem exeundi celeriter. De hoc Magister in historiis scribit: Fecerunt subcinericios panes azymos, ex modico tantum tempore coagulatos. His namque usi sunt triginta diebus, nec ultra eis suffecerunt quæ tulerant de Ægypto, licet sub necessitate custodirentur, nec ad satietatem reficerentur ex eis.
paras.en: [[12:37|And the children of Israel set forward from Ramesse to Socoth|Profectique sunt filii Israel de Ramesse in Socoth]]: that is, going out from the land of Gessen, they first encamped, or pitched their tents, in the place called Socoth; which is another place than that in which Jacob, returning from Mesopotamia, made his dwelling in the land of Chanaan and called it Socoth, that is, Tents, as we read in Genesis[[Gen 33:17||]]: [[12:37|being about six hundred thousand men on foot, beside children|sexcenta fere millia peditum virorum, absque parvulis et mulieribus]] and women [Denis's text adds *et mulieribus*]: that is, about six hundred thousand Hebrew men, fighting men on foot, went out, among whom the little ones or boys under twenty years of age, and the women, were not counted. How the people of Israel could multiply so greatly in Egypt within the years they stayed there was discussed in the exposition of the first chapter of this book. [[12:38|And a mixed multitude, without number, went up also with them|Sed et vulgus promiscuum innumerabile ascendit cum eis]]: that is, Egyptians of both sexes, exceedingly many, joined themselves to the Hebrews. For having seen so many signs, they abandoned idolatry and believed in the true God, and went out of Egypt with the children of Israel into the wilderness, which lay higher than Egypt: for which reason they are said to have gone up. And that multitude, according to the Scholastic History, served the Hebrews. And many of the Egyptians wept because they had been so hard on the Hebrews. [[12:39|And they baked the meal, which a little before they had brought out of Egypt in dough|Coxeruntque farinam, quam dudum de Ægypto conspersam tulerant]], namely on the first day of their going out, [[12:39|and they made hearth cakes unleavened|et fecerunt ex eo subcinericios panes azymos]] [*subcinericii*, loaves baked under the ashes], in the place called Socoth or thereabouts. [[12:39|for it could not be leavened|Neque enim poterant fermentari]], because of the shortness of the time, those loaves, or the moistened meal or lumps of dough from which the loaves were made, [[12:39|the Egyptians pressing them to depart|cogentibus exire]], the Hebrews, [[12:39|and not suffering them to make any stay|Ægyptiis, et nullam facere sinentibus moram]], [[12:39|neither did they think of preparing any meat|nec pulmenti quidquam occurrerat præparare]]: that is, the children of Israel had no leisure to cook any pottage or dish because of that pressing compulsion to go out quickly. Of this the Master [Peter Comestor] writes in the Histories: They made hearth cakes unleavened, set in only a little time. For they used these for thirty days, and what they had brought from Egypt did not last them longer, though it was kept sparingly, and they did not eat their fill of it.

paras.t: Habitatio autem filiorum Israel, qua manserunt in Ægypto, fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum. Sic et Apostolus ait ad Galatas : Hoc autem dico, testamentum confirmatum a Deo, quæ post quadringentos et triginta annos facta est lex, etc. Qualiter autem accipienda sit computatio ista, diversi diversimode tradiderunt, quorum computationem B. Augustinus pro magna reprobat parte. Deinde approbat computationem Eusebii Cæsariensis in Chronica sua, incipientis horum computationem annorum ab eo tempore, quo Abraham Deo jubente egressus est de terra sua, veniendo de Haran ad terram Chanaan, qui tunc erat septuaginta quinque annorum, ut in Genesi patet. Quumque centum esset annorum, natus est ei Isaac. Isaac vero vixit annis centum octoginta. Sicque ab exitu Abrahæ de Haran, usque ad mortem Isaac, fuerunt anni ducenti et quinque. Porro in morte Isaac fuit Jacob centum viginti annorum. Natus est etiam Jacob ipso Isaac sexagenario existente. Deinde post annos decem, quum Jacob esset centum triginta annorum, ingressus est cum sobole sua Ægyptum. Sicque a præfato Abrahæ exitu, usque ad introitum Jacob in Ægyptum, fluxerunt anni ducenti et quindecim : tuncque Joseph erat triginta novem annorum. Fuit quippe triginta annorum, quando eductus de carcere, præsentatus est Pharaoni. Deinde post septem annos fertilitatis, duosque annos inopiæ, Jacob intravit Ægyptum. Joseph quoque post annos illos triginta novem, vixit annis septuaginta et uno, quia in toto vixit annis centum et decem. Adjunctis ergo annis septuaginta et uno ad annos ducentos et quindecim prætaxatos, fiunt anni ducenti octoginta sex ; quibus addendi sunt anni centum quadraginta quatuor, quibus populus Israel fuit atque servivit in Ægypto post obitum Joseph : sicque in toto habentur anni quadringenti et triginta. Idcirco non valet quod quidam computationem istam redarguit.
paras.en: [[12:40|And the abode of the children of Israel that they made in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years|Habitatio autem filiorum Israel, qua manserunt in Ægypto, fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum]]. So too the Apostle says to the Galatians: [[Gal 3:17|Now this I say: that the testament which was confirmed by God, the law which was made after four hundred and thirty years|Hoc autem dico, testamentum confirmatum a Deo, quæ post quadringentos et triginta annos facta est lex]], etc. How this reckoning is to be taken, different writers have handed down in different ways, whose reckoning Blessed Augustine for the most part rejects. Then he approves the reckoning of Eusebius of Caesarea in his Chronicle, who begins the count of these years from the time when Abraham at God's bidding went out of his country, coming from Haran to the land of Chanaan; he was then seventy-five years old, as is plain in Genesis[[Gen 12:4||]]. And when he was a hundred years old, Isaac was born to him[[Gen 21:5||]] [the margin gives Gen. xvii, 17, where Isaac's birth is foretold; the birth itself, at his father's age of a hundred, is Gen 21:5]. And Isaac lived a hundred and eighty years[[Gen 35:28||]]. And so from Abraham's going out of Haran to the death of Isaac there were two hundred and five years. Further, at Isaac's death Jacob was a hundred and twenty years old. For Jacob was born when Isaac was sixty[[Gen 25:26||]]. Then ten years later, when Jacob was a hundred and thirty years old, he entered Egypt with his offspring[[Gen 47:9||]]. And so from Abraham's aforesaid going out to Jacob's entry into Egypt two hundred and fifteen years ran their course: and Joseph was then thirty-nine years old. For he was thirty years old when, brought out of prison, he was presented to Pharao[[Gen 41:46||]]. Then after seven years of plenty and two years of want, Jacob entered Egypt[[Gen 42:1||]]. And Joseph, after those thirty-nine years, lived seventy-one years, since in all he lived a hundred and ten years[[Gen 50:22||]][[Gen 50:25||]]. Adding, then, seventy-one years to the two hundred and fifteen reckoned above, we get two hundred and eighty-six years; to which must be added the hundred and forty-four years in which the people of Israel lived and served in Egypt after the death of Joseph: and so in all we have four hundred and thirty years. Therefore the objection of one who rejected this reckoning does not hold.

paras.t: Verumtamen non fuerunt in servitute illa dura, de qua in primo hujus libri capitulo scriptum, toto tempore post mortem Joseph, quousque egressi sunt ; sed diu post mortem Joseph quum surrexit rex qui ignoravit famam et beneficia Joseph, prout in primi expositione capituli patuit. Idcirco quod fertur in textu, Habitatio filiorum Israel in Ægypto, fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum, non est intelligendum, quod tanto tempore in Ægypto sint demorati, sed nomine Ægypti designantur et aliæ terræ, in quibus patres eorum, Abraham, Isaac et Jacob peregrinati sunt. Exprimitur tamen in speciali Ægyptus, quia ibidem in majori numero personarum atque annorum sunt commorati, graviusque oppressi, et quia a fine majorique parte solet denominatio fieri. Verumtamen Augustinus ait in textu isto haberi, Incolatus quem incoluerunt in terra Ægypti et in terra Chanaan, ipsi et patres eorum. Utitur autem translatione Septuaginta interpretum, qui interdum aliquid addiderunt, vel subtraxerunt. Patres vero filiorum Israel, non solum fuerunt coloni et peregrini in terra Chanaan, sed et Abraham et Isaac diu demorati sunt in terra Philistiim, et Jacob in Mesopotamia Syriæ. Porro Josephus scribit : Reliquerunt Hebræi Ægyptum post annos triginta et quadringentos, quam pater noster Abraham venit in terram Chanaan : post adventum vero Jacob in Ægyptum, anno ducentesimo quintodecimo.
paras.en: Yet they were not in that hard bondage which is written of in the first chapter of this book[[Ex 1:11||]] for the whole time after the death of Joseph until they went out; but only from long after the death of Joseph, when there arose a king who knew nothing of the fame and the benefits of Joseph[[Ex 1:8||]], as was shown in the exposition of the first chapter. Therefore what is said in the text, [[12:40|the abode of the children of Israel that they made in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years|Habitatio filiorum Israel in Ægypto, fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum]], is not to be understood as if they had stayed so long a time in Egypt; but under the name of Egypt the other lands also are meant in which their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob sojourned. Egypt, however, is named in particular because there they dwelt in the greater number both of persons and of years, and were more heavily oppressed, and because a thing is wont to be named from its end and from its greater part. Augustine, however, says that this text reads: The sojourning which they sojourned in the land of Egypt and in the land of Chanaan, they and their fathers. But he uses the translation of the Seventy interpreters, who sometimes added or took away something. Now the fathers of the children of Israel were not only settlers and strangers in the land of Chanaan; Abraham and Isaac also stayed long in the land of the Philistines, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria. Further, Josephus writes: The Hebrews left Egypt four hundred and thirty years after our father Abraham came into the land of Chanaan, but in the two hundred and fifteenth year after Jacob's coming into Egypt.

paras.t: Quibus expletis, eadem die egressus est omnis exercitus Domini de terra Ægypti, id est, tota multitudo Israeliticæ plebis recte disposita, una die pariter exiit de Ægypto. Itaque sensus non est, quod eadem die, qua patres eorum introierunt Ægyptum, isti egressi sint. Nox ista observabilis est Domini, id est, nox in qua Hebræi ab Ægyptiis sollicitabantur exire, et in qua se disposuerunt ad exeundum valde mane, digna et apta est, ut in ea sit Dei celebritas, et cultui ejus vacetur propter beneficia tanta, ne oblivioni tradantur ; quando, id est in cujus noctis aurora, eduxit eos de terra Ægypti. Hanc observare debent om[nes] filii Israel in generationibus suis, id est, celebrem habere per suas posteritates et successiones. Paschalis enim solemnitas incepit a vespere noctem hanc præcedente.
paras.en: [[12:41|Which being expired, the same day all the army of the Lord went forth out of the land of Egypt|Quibus expletis, eadem die egressus est omnis exercitus Domini de terra Ægypti]]: that is, the whole multitude of the Israelite people, rightly ordered, went out of Egypt together on one day. So the sense is not that these went out on the same day on which their fathers had entered Egypt. [[12:42|This is the observable night of the Lord|Nox ista observabilis est Domini]]: that is, the night in which the Hebrews were urged by the Egyptians to go out, and in which they made ready to go out very early in the morning, is worthy and fit to have a feast of God kept in it, and to be given to his worship because of such great benefits, lest they be forgotten; [[12:42|when|quando]], that is, at the dawn of which night, [[12:42|he brought them forth out of the land of Egypt|eduxit eos de terra Ægypti]]. [[12:42|this night all the children of Israel must observe in their generations|Hanc observare debent om[nes] filii Israel in generationibus suis]], that is, keep it as a feast through their descendants and successors. For the paschal solemnity began from the evening before this night.

paras.t: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron : Hæc est religio Phase, id est, istud quod sequitur, pertinet ad ritum et jussionem comedendi agnum paschalem, videlicet : Omnis alienigena non comedet ex eo, id est, nullus a fide et lege Judæorum extraneus, etiamsi sit natione Judæus, ad esum agni hujus est admittendus: quemadmodum ad sacram communionem nullus scienter admittitur, nisi catholicus. Omnis autem servus emptitius circumcidetur, et sic comedet, id est, quum fuerit circumcisus, vescetur agno paschali. Advena et mercenarius non edent ex eo, nisi prius circumcidantur: sicut nec aliquis potest communicare, nisi fuerit baptizatus. In una domo comedetur agnus paschalis, id est, quilibet cum sua familia comedet eum in domo sua, dummodo domestici ejus ad hoc sufficiant. Nec efferetis de carnibus ejus foras, id est, non mittetis aliis partem aliquam agni paschalis assati: nec os illius confringetis, id est, ossa ejus non dissipabitis nec frangetis. Litteralis ratio horum est, quoniam filii Israel in Ægypto hoc modo manducaverunt agnum paschalem, et cum festinatione tanta, quod non habebant tempus frangendi ossa ad quærendum medullam. Unusquisque etiam paterfamilias aut principalis in domo, pro redemptione sua atque domesticorum a percussione angeli, obtulit agnum in sua domo. Omnis cœtus filiorum Israel faciet illud, id est, unaquæque familia propriæ domus comedet modo præfato. Sicque, Omnis, sumitur nunc divisive, non penitus collective.
paras.en: [[12:43|And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: This is the service of the Phase|Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron : Hæc est religio Phase]]: that is, what follows belongs to the rite and command of eating the paschal lamb, namely: [[12:43|no foreigner shall eat of it|Omnis alienigena non comedet ex eo]]: that is, no one who is a stranger to the faith and law of the Jews, even if he is a Jew by birth, is to be admitted to the eating of this lamb; just as no one is knowingly admitted to holy communion unless he is a Catholic. [[12:44|But every bought servant shall be circumcised, and so shall eat|Omnis autem servus emptitius circumcidetur, et sic comedet]]: that is, when he has been circumcised he shall eat of the paschal lamb. [[12:45|The stranger and the hireling shall not eat thereof|Advena et mercenarius non edent ex eo]], unless they are first circumcised: just as no one can communicate unless he has been baptized. [[12:46|In one house shall it be eaten|In una domo comedetur]], the paschal lamb: that is, each one shall eat it with his family in his own house, provided his household are enough for it. [[12:46|neither shall you carry forth of the flesh thereof out of the house|Nec efferetis de carnibus ejus foras]]: that is, you shall not send any part of the roasted paschal lamb to others; [[12:46|neither shall you break a bone thereof|nec os illius confringetis]]: that is, you shall not scatter or break its bones. The literal reason for these things is that the children of Israel in Egypt ate the paschal lamb in this manner, and with such haste that they had no time to break the bones to get at the marrow. Also each father of a family, or head of a house, offered a lamb in his own house for the redeeming of himself and his household from the stroke of the angel. [[12:47|All the assembly of the children of Israel shall keep it|Omnis cœtus filiorum Israel faciet illud]]: that is, each family of its own house shall eat it in the aforesaid manner. And so *All* is taken here distributively, not wholly collectively.

paras.t: Quod si quis peregrinorum, id est extraneorum a lege vestra, in vestram voluerit transire coloniam, et facere Phase Domini, id est legem vestram assumere, et vester concivis fieri per cultus divini et sacramentorum communionem, circumcidetur prius omne masculinum ejus, id est universi ejus domestici sexus masculini: quia non satis erat quod ipse circumcidebatur, ad hoc ut de agno paschali vesceretur: et tunc rite celebrabit, id est agnum paschalem edet cum suis, secundum observantiam nunc præscriptam; eritque sicut indigena terræ, hoc est, similis erit natis in Judaismo, et velut Judæus habebitur. Si quis autem circumcisus non fuerit, non vescetur ex eo. Eadem lex erit indigenæ et colono, qui peregrinatur apud vos; id est, tam intranei seu concives natione Hebræi, quam extranei et tanquam peregrini inter vos habitantes, quantum ad hoc, erunt paris conditionis, et eadem jussione adstricti, quod nullus eorum poterit de agno manducare paschali, nisi prædicta impleverit.
paras.en: [[12:48|And if any stranger|Quod si quis peregrinorum]], that is, of those who are strangers to your law, [[12:48|be willing to dwell among you, and to keep the Phase of the Lord|in vestram voluerit transire coloniam, et facere Phase Domini]] [literally "to pass over into your settlement and to make the Phase of the Lord"], that is, to take up your law and become your fellow citizen through sharing in divine worship and the sacraments, [[12:48|all his males shall first be circumcised|circumcidetur prius omne masculinum ejus]], that is, all those of his household of the male sex: for it was not enough that he himself was circumcised for him to eat of the paschal lamb: [[12:48|and then shall he celebrate it according to the manner|et tunc rite celebrabit]], that is, he shall eat the paschal lamb with his household according to the observance now prescribed; [[12:48|and he shall be as he that is born in the land|eritque sicut indigena terræ]], that is, he shall be like those born in Judaism, and shall be held as a Jew. [[12:48|but if any man be uncircumcised, he shall not eat thereof|Si quis autem circumcisus non fuerit, non vescetur ex eo]]. [[12:49|The same law shall be to him that is born in the land, and to the proselyte that sojourneth with you|Eadem lex erit indigenæ et colono, qui peregrinatur apud vos]]: that is, both those within, the fellow citizens who are Hebrews by birth, and those from outside who dwell among you as strangers, shall in this be of equal condition and bound by the same command: that none of them may eat of the paschal lamb unless he has fulfilled what has been said.

paras.t: Feceruntque omnes filii Israel, sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi et Aaron; et eadem die eduxit Dominus filios Israel de terra Ægypti per turmas suas, hoc est cum distinctione specialium turmarum quæ inter eos fuerunt. Quamvis enim fuit unus totalis exercitus, tamen speciales cœtus, particularesque tribus ac cunei atque familiæ inter eos fuerunt, qui omnes pariter sunt educti.
paras.en: [[12:50|And all the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron|Feceruntque omnes filii Israel, sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi et Aaron]]; [[12:51|And the same day the Lord brought forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their companies|et eadem die eduxit Dominus filios Israel de terra Ægypti per turmas suas]], that is, with the distinction of the particular companies that were among them. For though it was one whole army, yet there were among them particular bands, and separate tribes, troops and families, all of whom were led out together.

paras.t: Circa præhabita quæritur, an angelus qui percussit primogenita Ægyptiorum, fuit angelus bonus an malus, et utrum fuit unus dumtaxat, an plures.
paras.en: Concerning what has been said, it is asked whether the angel who struck the firstborn of the Egyptians was a good angel or a bad one, and whether there was only one, or several.

paras.t: Strabus ait, et habetur in Glossa: An percussor primogenitorum fuit angelus bonus, an malus, non est necesse inquirere. Quicumque etenim fuit, præcepto Dei obedivit. Sciendum tamen, quod angeli mali permissione aut jussione Dei tales pestes facere solent. Hæc Strabus. Ex cujus verbis elicitur, quod ipse magis sentire videtur, quod fuerit angelus malus, et hoc tenent aliqui. Ad quod primo allegant illud in Psalmo: Misit in eos (utpote in Ægyptios) iram indignationis, iram, indignationem et tribulationem, immissiones per angelos malos. Unde et paulo post ibi subjungitur: Et percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti. Secundo allegant quod in isto fertur capitulo, Non sinet Dominus percussorem ingredi domos vestras, et lædere. Ex quo inferunt, quod percussor ille libenter intrasset domos Hebræorum ad percutiendum primogenita eorumdem, si Dominus permisisset: ergo et malus fuit. Tertio, idem probatur auctoritate Augustini, qui in expositione Psalmi septuagesimi septimi, in quo habentur verba Psalmistæ præallegata, apertissime dicit, quod fuit angelus malus.
paras.en: Strabo says, and it is found in the Gloss: Whether the striker of the firstborn was a good angel or a bad one, there is no need to inquire. For whoever he was, he obeyed the command of God. Yet it should be known that the bad angels are wont to bring such plagues by the permission or at the bidding of God. Thus Strabo. From his words it is gathered that he himself seems rather to think that it was a bad angel; and some hold this. In support of it they allege, first, that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 77:49|And he sent upon them|Misit in eos]] (namely upon the Egyptians) [[Ps 77:49|the wrath of his indignation: indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels|iram indignationis, iram, indignationem et tribulationem, immissiones per angelos malos]]. And so a little after it is added there: [[Ps 77:51|And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt|Et percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti]]. Secondly they allege what is said in this chapter: The Lord will [[12:23|not suffer the destroyer to come into your houses and to hurt you|Non sinet Dominus percussorem ingredi domos vestras, et lædere]]. From this they infer that that striker would gladly have entered the houses of the Hebrews to strike their firstborn, had the Lord allowed him: therefore he was a bad one. Thirdly, the same is proved by the authority of Augustine, who in his exposition of the seventy-seventh Psalm, in which stand the words of the Psalmist alleged above, says most plainly that it was a bad angel.

paras.t: Oppositum hujus probatur, primo ex eo, quod in libro Sapientiæ habetur: Tunc quum primum fuit exterminium primogenitorum, spoponderunt populum Dei se esse. Deinde subjungitur ibi, qualiter factum sit exterminium illud. Quum enim quietum silentium teneret omnia, et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet, omnipotens sermo tuus, Domine, exsiliens de cœlo, a regalibus sedibus venit, durus debellator in mediam exterminii terram prosilivit, gladius acutus, insimulatum (id est verum et non fictum) imperium tuum portans et stans replevit omnia morte et usque ad cœlum attingebat stans in terra. Circa quæ verba multi dicunt, percussionem illam factam per angelum bonum, imo verba illa clarissime contestantur, quod sit facta per bonum Dei ministrum aut executorem divinum. Secundo, idem videtur ex modo loquendi hujus capituli, in quo Dominus clare atque frequenter affirmat se percussurum seu percutientem primogenita Ægyptiorum, ut patuit. Et quamvis ea facere asseratur, quæ facit per angelos malos, præsertim loquendo de malis pœnalibus, non tamen videtur quod in Scripturis in recitatione historica asserat tam clare ac sæpe facturum, quod in isto capitulo asserit se facturum, nisi quod facit per se ipsum aut per angelos bonos. Tertio, idem probatur, quoniam Deus per angelum bonum interfecit exercitum Assyriorum sub rege piissimo Ezechia, ut legitur quarto Regum et secundo Paralipomenon libris. Similiter per angelos bonos evertit Sodomitas, ut in Genesi legitur. In Ezechiele quoque legitur Deus præcepisse angelis bonis percutere habitatores Jerusalem.
paras.en: The opposite of this is proved, first, from what is found in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 18:13|then first upon the destruction of the firstborn|Tunc quum primum fuit exterminium primogenitorum]], [[Wis 18:13|they acknowledged the people to be of God|spoponderunt populum Dei se esse]] [Denis's text reads se esse, "that they were", which the Vulgate lacks]. Then it is added there how that destruction was wrought: [[Wis 18:14|For while all things were in quiet silence, and the night was in the midst of her course|Quum enim quietum silentium teneret omnia, et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet]], [[Wis 18:15|Thy Almighty word leaped down from heaven from thy royal throne, as a fierce conqueror into the midst of the land of destruction|omnipotens sermo tuus, Domine, exsiliens de cœlo, a regalibus sedibus venit, durus debellator in mediam exterminii terram prosilivit]] [Denis's text adds Domine, exsiliens, "O Lord, leaping", and venit, "came"], [[Wis 18:16|With a sharp sword carrying thy unfeigned|gladius acutus, insimulatum]] (that is, true and not feigned) [[Wis 18:16|commandment, and he stood and filled all things with death, and standing on the earth, reached even to heaven|imperium tuum portans et stans replevit omnia morte et usque ad cœlum attingebat stans in terra]]. Concerning these words many say that that striking was done by a good angel; indeed those words testify most clearly that it was done by a good minister of God, a divine executor. Secondly, the same appears from the manner of speaking of this chapter, in which the Lord clearly and often affirms that He will strike, or is striking, the firstborn of the Egyptians, as was seen. And although He is said to do the things He does through bad angels, especially when speaking of the evils of punishment [that is, evils suffered as penalty, as distinct from the evil of sin], yet it does not seem that in the Scriptures, in historical narrative, He declares so clearly and so often that He will do a thing, as in this chapter He declares that He will do this, unless it be something He does by Himself or through good angels. Thirdly, the same is proved, since God by a good angel slew the army of the Assyrians under the most pious king Ezechias, as is read in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 19:35||]] and in the second of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 32:21||]]. Likewise by good angels He overthrew the Sodomites, as is read in Genesis[[Gen 19:1||]]. In Ezechiel also we read that God commanded good angels to strike the inhabitants of Jerusalem[[Ezech 9:5||]].

paras.t: Circa hanc quæstionem advertenda sunt verba beatissimi Augustini, in expositione præfati psalmi dicentis: Satis hic expressum est, judicio Dei hæc fieri in illis, puta Ægyptiis, per angelos malos. Itemque, Utitur Deus angelis malis, non solum ad puniendos malos, sicut in istis omnibus, puta Ægyptiis, de quibus loquitur psalmus iste, et sicut in rege Achab, quem fallaciæ spiritus ex Dei voluntate decepit, ut caderet in bello, verum etiam ad probandos et manifestandos bonos. In his verbis videtur Augustinus sentire, non solum percussionem primogenitorum, sed et alias plagas, esse inflictas Ægyptiis ab angelis malis. Quod præinductis non consonat, nec videtur posse salvari. Magi namque defecerunt in tertio signo, ita quod scinifes producere non valebant magica arte et diabolica ope, sicut verterunt aquam in sanguinem, et ranas fecerunt. Nec post tertium illud signum operati sunt aliquid simile signis quæ fecit Deus per Moysen et Aaron, aut per se, hoc est sine ipsorum administratione. Ergo dæmones non fecerunt aliquid simile octo signis et plagis, quibus Ægyptii sunt percussi.
paras.en: On this question we must attend to the words of the most blessed Augustine in his exposition of the said Psalm, where he says: It is expressed plainly enough here that these things were done by the judgment of God upon them, that is, the Egyptians, through bad angels. And again: God uses bad angels not only to punish the wicked, as in all these, that is, the Egyptians, of whom this Psalm speaks, and as in king Achab, whom the spirit of lying deceived by the will of God, that he might fall in battle[[3 Kings 22:20||]], but also to prove and make manifest the good. In these words Augustine seems to think that not only the striking of the firstborn but the other plagues as well were inflicted on the Egyptians by bad angels. This does not agree with what was brought forward above, nor does it seem possible to uphold it. For the magicians failed at the third sign, so that they could not produce sciniphs by magic art and the devil's aid[[Ex 8:18||]], as they had turned water into blood and made frogs. Nor after that third sign did they work anything like the signs which God did through Moses and Aaron, or by Himself, that is, without their ministry. Therefore the demons did nothing like the eight signs and plagues with which the Egyptians were struck.

paras.t: Nec aliquo modo dicendum est, quod Deus per dæmones fecit illa miracula, nec aliquis expositorum hoc dicit, sed per angelos sanctos. Nec ipse Augustinus audet hoc dicere. Siquidem post verba præhabita loquitur: Si per angelos malos Deus illas plagas inflixit Ægyptiis, numquid audebimus dicere, et aquam in sanguinem per eosdem angelos malos esse versam, et ranas per eos esse productas, quorum similia magi Pharaonis per veneficia sua fecerunt: ut angeli mali ex utraque parte consisterent, hinc illos affligentes, inde fallentes, secundum judicium et dispositionem justissimi Dei? Non audeo dicere. Ecce Augustinus non audet dicere, quod Deus per angelos malos induxit duas primas plagas. Verumtamen primogenita asserit per eos percussa, subdendo: Si ea quæ ibi mirabiliter facta sunt, malis angelis tribuere non audemus, habemus quod eis tribuere sine dubitatione possumus, scilicet mortes primogenitorum in hominibus et jumentis.
paras.en: Nor in any way is it to be said that God worked those miracles through demons, nor does any of the expositors say so, but rather through the holy angels. Nor does Augustine himself dare to say it. For after the words given above he says: If God inflicted those plagues on the Egyptians through bad angels, shall we dare to say that the water also was turned into blood by those same bad angels, and the frogs brought forth by them, the like of which Pharao's magicians did by their sorceries; so that bad angels stood on both sides, on this side afflicting them, on that deceiving them, according to the judgment and disposition of the most just God? I dare not say it. See, Augustine does not dare to say that God brought the first two plagues through bad angels. Yet he asserts that the firstborn were struck by them, adding: If we do not dare to ascribe to bad angels the things that were wonderfully done there, we have something we can ascribe to them without hesitation, namely the deaths of the firstborn in men and beasts.

paras.t: Verumtamen juxta præinducta, probabilius reor, quod sicut ceteras plagas Deus per angelos sanctos produxit ac intulit, ita et istam. Ad quod probandum valent motiva prætacta. Nam et eadem ratio in omnibus plagis his, ad hoc esse censetur. Nempe, cur potius inflixisset percussionem illam primogenitorum per dæmones, quam plagas scinifum, ranarum, muscarum, cynomyiæ, vulnera vesicarum, tonitrua, fulgura, grandines, tenebras, quibus non solum primogeniti, sed cuncti Ægyptii generaliter sunt percussi?
paras.en: Nevertheless, in keeping with what was brought forward above, I think it more probable that, as God brought about and inflicted the other plagues through the holy angels, so also this one. The reasons touched on above serve to prove this. For the same reason is judged to hold for this in all these plagues. Why, indeed, would He have inflicted that striking of the firstborn through demons rather than the plagues of sciniphs, frogs, flies, the dog-fly, the sores of blains, the thunders, lightnings, hail and darkness, with which not the firstborn only but all the Egyptians in general were struck?

paras.t: Itaque agnoscendum, quod sicut Scriptura nos docet, Deus quandoque punivit iniquos per angelos sanctos, ut patet de subversione Pentapolis, et percussione Assyriorum, et in Actibus Apostolorum fertur angelus Dei percussisse Herodem. Quandoque vero hoc fecit per angelos malos, quemadmodum primo Regum asseritur, quod spiritus Dei malus exagitabat Saulem. Interdum quoque percussit bonos per angelos malos, ut patet de Job, et Paulo apostolo qui fatetur: Datus est mihi stimulus carnis meæ angelus Satanæ, qui me colaphizet.
paras.en: It must therefore be acknowledged that, as Scripture teaches us, God sometimes punished the wicked through holy angels, as is plain from the overthrow of the Pentapolis [the five cities of the plain, Sodom and its neighbours][[Gen 19:1||]] and the striking of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 19:35||]]; and in the Acts of the Apostles an angel of God is said to have struck Herod[[Acts 12:23||]]. But sometimes He did this through bad angels, as it is said in the first book of Kings that an evil spirit from God troubled Saul[[1 Kings 16:15||]]. Sometimes too He struck the good through bad angels, as is plain in Job[[Job 1:12||]][[Job 2:6||]], and in Paul the Apostle, who confesses: [[2 Cor 12:7|there was given me a sting of my flesh, an angel of Satan, to buffet me|Datus est mihi stimulus carnis meæ angelus Satanæ, qui me colaphizet]].

paras.t: An autem aliquando percussit bonos per angelos sanctos, specialis est quæstio. Quocirca loquitur Augustinus in expositione psalmi præfati: Justos corporalibus pœnis per bonos angelos tentari et probari, non mihi occurrit: nihilo minus dicere possumus, quod etiam interdum justi per angelos bonos puniti sunt, ut patet circa finem secundi Regum de septuaginta millibus ab angelo sancto percussis, propter peccatum David in numeratione populi, de quibus David dixit ad Dominum: Isti qui oves sunt, quid fecerunt? Nec dubium quin multi boni inter illos fuerunt. Supra quoque præhabitum est, quod Dominus occurrit Moysi in diversorio, et voluit eum occidere: quod fuit per angelum sanctum.
paras.en: Whether He has ever struck the good through holy angels is a question of its own. On this Augustine says in his exposition of the said Psalm: That the just are tried and proved with bodily punishments through good angels does not occur to me. Nevertheless we can say that sometimes the just too have been punished through good angels, as is plain near the end of the second book of Kings from the seventy thousand struck by the holy angel for David's sin in numbering the people[[2 Kings 24:15||]], of whom David said to the Lord: [[2 Kings 24:17|these that are the sheep, what have they done?|Isti qui oves sunt, quid fecerunt?]] And there is no doubt that there were many good men among them. It was also set down above that the Lord met Moses in the inn and would have killed him[[Ex 4:24||]]: which was done through a holy angel.

paras.t: Præterea, ad objecta dicendum, quod illa auctoritas, Immissiones per angelos malos, intelligenda est de pessimis inspirationibus, quas dæmones immiserunt Ægyptiis, ex quibus tam obstinati et excæcati effecti sunt, quod Deo permittente est factum: non de inductionibus plagarum et interfectionum, quæ fuerunt mala pœnalia, non culpabilia, et ita fuerunt a Deo directe causaliter. Alia quoque auctoritas, secundum expositionem præhabitam, non militat contra prædicta. Nam, ut divinus Dionysius docet, angeli sancti non audent aliquid agere, nisi juxta legem eis a Deo præfixam: idcirco per id quod dicitur, Non sinet percussorem ingredi, etc., non datur intelligi quod percussor ille optavit Hebræos percutere, sed quod Deus ei præfixit, quid et qualiter ageret, quemadmodum secundo Regum legitur Deus angelo percutienti jussisse, Cesset manus tua, etc.
paras.en: Further, to the objections it must be said that the authority [[Ps 77:49|which he sent by evil angels|Immissiones per angelos malos]] is to be understood of the most wicked suggestions which the demons sent into the Egyptians, by which they were made so obstinate and blinded, which was done by God's permission; not of the bringing on of the plagues and slayings, which were evils of punishment, not of guilt, and so came from God directly as their cause. The other authority too, according to the exposition given above, does not tell against what has been said. For, as the divine Dionysius teaches, the holy angels dare do nothing except according to the law laid down for them by God: therefore by what is said, He will [[12:23|not suffer the destroyer to come into|Non sinet percussorem ingredi]] etc., it is not given to understand that that striker wished to strike the Hebrews, but that God laid down for him what he should do and how; just as we read in the second book of Kings that God commanded the striking angel: [[2 Kings 24:16|now hold thy hand|Cesset manus tua]], etc. [Denis has Cesset manus tua, "let thy hand cease", where the Vulgate reads contine manum tuam].

paras.t: At vero in his quæ non spectant directe ad fidem, nec ab Ecclesia determinata sunt, ipsemet Augustinus dicit, non accipi sufficiens argumentum ex sola allegatione ecclesiasticorum doctorum, sed in talibus licet viris eruditis tenere, quod rationi et Scripturis consonantius arbitrantur.
paras.en: But in things that do not bear directly on the faith and have not been determined by the Church, Augustine himself says that a sufficient argument is not had from the mere citing of the Church's doctors, but that in such matters learned men may hold what they judge more in agreement with reason and the Scriptures.

paras.t: Insuper, circa secundæ quæstionis solutionem possent valde multa difficilia atque subtilia introduci de motu, loco, et operatione angelorum, de quibus doctores super secundum Sententiarum, et in Summis suis tractant diffuse: de quibus nunc supersedendum opinor. Scriptura autem hæc loquitur, quasi percussor de domo in domum transierit, percutiendo primogenita hominum et brutorum; sed juxta doctores, angelus est in loco definitive, et illic est ubi operatur, nec ei debetur locus punctalis. Verum ad quæ virtus sua activa se potest extendere ad agendum, in eo est loco, vel esse potest. Potest autem se virtus angelica in longum et latum extendere pariter ad agendum: sed in quantum, quis novit? Ex verbis autem libri Sapientiæ introductis apparet, quod fuit unus tantum percussor. Quod si naturalis potestas angeli unius, non potuit se simul extendere ad percutiendum uno momento aut una horula, universa primogenita regni tam magni, tamen per supernaturalem Dei potentiam potuit hoc. Angelus autem qui populum Israeliticum pro peccato David percussit, successive hoc fecit a mane usque ad vesperam. Porro in Ezechiele leguntur multi angeli missi ad percutiendum Jerusalem: quod tamen in visione imaginaria sic fuit ostensum.
paras.en: Moreover, on the solution of the second question [whether the striker was one angel or many] a great many difficult and subtle points could be brought in about the motion, place and operation of the angels, which the doctors treat at length on the second book of the Sentences and in their Summas; these I think are to be left aside for now. Scripture, then, speaks as though the striker passed from house to house, striking the firstborn of men and beasts; but according to the doctors an angel is in a place definitively [that is, by being confined to it through his operation, not by being measured by it as a body is], and is there where he works, nor is a point-like place due to him. But wherever his active power can reach to act, in that place he is, or can be. Now angelic power can reach far and wide alike to act; but how far, who knows? From the words of the book of Wisdom brought in above, it appears that there was only one striker. And if the natural power of one angel could not reach at once, in one moment or one short hour, to strike all the firstborn of so great a kingdom, yet by the supernatural power of God it could do this. The angel who struck the people of Israel for David's sin did it by degrees, from morning until evening. Again, in Ezechiel many angels are read of as sent to strike Jerusalem[[Ezech 9:5||]]; yet this was shown so in an imaginary vision [that is, a vision of images formed in the imagination].

paras.t: Postremo, juxta eos qui dicunt percussionem primogenitorum esse factam ab angelo malo, dicendum esset, quod fuerunt dæmones multi percutientes, sicut et Augustinus allegat ac tenet. Hæc sine præjudicio et incauta assertione sint dicta.
paras.en: Lastly, according to those who say that the striking of the firstborn was done by a bad angel, it would have to be said that there were many demons striking, as Augustine too alleges and holds. Let these things be said without prejudice and without rash assertion.

12.title: Spiritualis et mystica ejusdem capituli duodecimi elucidatio
12.title_en: Spiritual and mystical explanation of the same twelfth chapter

paras.t: Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Mensis iste, vobis principium mensium, primus erit in mensibus anni. Recte mensis ille primus in mensibus anni jussus est esse, in quo agnus paschalis oblatus est, imo in quo Christus unigenitus Dei, pro mundi salute est immolatus; decuitque illo in mense typicum agnum offerri, et per ejus oblationem populum Israeliticum a corporali et Ægyptiaca servitute educi ac liberari, in quo Christus agnus Dei verus, universitatis salvator, elegit Deo Patri in cruce offerri, ac genus humanum a diabolica servitute, a jugo peccati, a damnatione inferni eruere.
paras.en: [[12:1|the Lord said to Moses|Dixit Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[12:2|This month shall be to you the beginning of months; it shall be the first in the months of the year|Mensis iste, vobis principium mensium, primus erit in mensibus anni]]. Rightly was that month commanded to be the first in the months of the year in which the paschal lamb was offered, nay rather in which Christ, the only-begotten of God, was sacrificed for the salvation of the world. And it was fitting that the figurative lamb should be offered in that month, and that through its offering the Israelite people should be led out and set free from bodily servitude in Egypt, in which Christ, [[John 1:29|the Lamb of God|agnus Dei]] in truth, the Saviour of all things, chose to be offered on the cross to God the Father, and to rescue mankind from the devil's servitude, from the yoke of sin, and from the damnation of hell.

paras.t: Decima die mensis hujus tollat unusquisque agnum. Quamvis pro totius mundi salute unus dumtaxat oblatus sit verus Agnus, nihilo minus Dominus jussit unumquemque patremfamilias inter Hebræos sumere et offerre, occidere atque comedere agnum cum suis: quia sic mortuus est Christus pro omnibus, ut et pro singulis mortuus sit et oblatus. Unde et unusquisque sic debet passionem Christi attendere, et ei gratus exsistere, quasi pro se solo sit crucifixus. Ad quod insinuandum dixit Apostolus: In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me. Circa quod ait Chrysostomus: Hoc est effectus servi fidelis, ut quod pro omnibus gestum est, quasi pro se solo reputet factum. Porro, quod agnus jubetur decimo die tolli et quartodecimo immolari, hoc signat, quod passio Christi figuratur in lege, quæ propter Decalogum per decem significatur, et in exordio evangelicæ legis impletur: quæ lex per quartumdecimum diem exprimitur, quoniam Decalogo quatuor Evangelia addit, et per quatuor mundi partes copiose diffusa est.
paras.en: [[12:3|On the tenth day of this month let every man take a lamb|Decima die mensis hujus tollat unusquisque agnum]]. Although for the salvation of the whole world only one true Lamb was offered, the Lord nevertheless commanded every father of a household among the Hebrews to take and offer, to kill and to eat a lamb with his own: because Christ so died for all that he died and was offered for each one as well. Hence each one too ought so to attend to the passion of Christ, and to be grateful to him, as though he had been crucified for him alone. To convey this the Apostle said: [[Gal 2:20|I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and delivered himself for me|In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me]]. On which Chrysostom says: This is the mark of a faithful servant, that what was done for all he should reckon as done for himself alone. Further, that the lamb is commanded to be taken on the tenth day and sacrificed on the fourteenth[[12:6||]] signifies that the passion of Christ is prefigured in the Law, which is signified by ten on account of the Decalogue, and is fulfilled at the beginning of the Gospel law: which law is expressed by the fourteenth day, since it adds the four Gospels to the Decalogue, and has been spread abroad abundantly through the four quarters of the world.

paras.t: Sin autem minor est numerus, etc. Sic quilibet Christifidelis videns se Christi beneficia atque mysteria non posse satis mirari, diligere, venerari, proximum suum invitet ad regratiandum secum in omnibus Christo, et ad supplendum proprium imperfectum. Nec enim quispiam valet Christo digne ac plene regratiari, etiam si millies moretur pro Christo. Quia (ut Climacus ait) aliud est sanguis Dei, aliud sanguis servi. Non quod unius speciei non fuerit sanguis Christi et hominum ceterorum, sed quia incomparabiliter pretiosior est sanguis unigeniti Filii Dei.
paras.en: [[12:4|But if the number be less|Sin autem minor est numerus]], etc. So let every one of Christ's faithful, seeing that he cannot sufficiently wonder at, love and revere the benefits and mysteries of Christ, invite his neighbour to give thanks to Christ together with him in all things, and to make up for his own imperfection. For no one is able to thank Christ worthily and fully, even if he were to die a thousand times for Christ. Because (as Climacus says) the blood of God is one thing, the blood of a servant another. Not that the blood of Christ and that of other men was not of one kind, but because the blood of the only-begotten Son of God is incomparably more precious.

paras.t: Erit autem agnus absque macula, masculus, anniculus. Per quod Christi illibatissima puritas designatur, in quo fuit totius virilitatis perfectio: qui in tricesimo tertio suæ ætatis anno, quando et cruci appensus est, erat tam purus et innocens, sicut in primo anno, quo ex Virgine natus est. Juxta quem ritum tolletis et hœdum. Solet per hœdum peccator intelligi: idcirco Christus, in quantum similitudinem carnis peccati et mortalitatem assumpsit, nec solum ex justis, sed et peccatoribus quoque et peccatricibus mediate humanam assumpsit naturam, significatur per hœdum: et rursus, quoniam ipse instar hœdi venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles: celerrime quoque omne bonum est prosecutus, et regia dignitate, pontificalique potestate quasi duplici cornu fuit munitus.
paras.en: [[12:5|And it shall be a lamb without blemish, a male, of one year|Erit autem agnus absque macula, masculus, anniculus]]. By this is designated the most spotless purity of Christ, in whom was the perfection of all manliness: who in the thirty-third year of his age, when he was also hung upon the cross, was as pure and innocent as in the first year, in which he was born of the Virgin. [[12:5|according to which rite also you shall take a kid|Juxta quem ritum tolletis et hœdum]]. By a kid a sinner is usually understood: therefore Christ is signified by the kid, inasmuch as he took on the likeness of sinful flesh and mortality, and took human nature not only from the just but also, through intermediate generations, from sinful men and sinful women; and again, because like a kid he [[Cant 2:8|cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping over the hills|venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles]] [the margin gives Cant. ii, 9; the words are from Cant 2:8, and v. 9 goes on to liken the beloved to a roe]: he also pursued every good most swiftly, and was armed, as with a double horn, with royal dignity and priestly power.

paras.t: Immolabitque eum universa multitudo filiorum Israel ad vesperam: quia in Cœna novissima Christus passionem suam apertissime denuntiavit, et suæ immolationis Sacramentum instituit, et Patri sponte se obtulit, dum a Bethania in Jerusalem, extra quam non capiebat perire Prophetam tanquam ad locum passionis voluntarie est profectus. Ipse quoque in vespera, hoc est in ultima mundi ætate, sustinuit mortem.
paras.en: [[12:6|and the whole multitude of the children of Israel shall sacrifice it in the evening|Immolabitque eum universa multitudo filiorum Israel ad vesperam]]: because at the Last Supper Christ announced his passion most openly[[Matt 26:20||]][[Matt 26:21||]][[John 13:21||]], and instituted the Sacrament of his sacrifice, and offered himself freely to the Father, when he set out of his own will from Bethania to Jerusalem, as to the place of his passion, outside which [[Luke 13:33|it cannot be that a prophet perish|non capiebat perire Prophetam]]. He too underwent death in the evening, that is, in the last age of the world.

paras.t: Et sument de sanguine ejus, et ponent super utramque postem. Per hoc significatum est, quod populus christianus corpus suum et animam fide et commemoratione assidua passionis dominicæ debeat communire, consignare ac custodire, Christumque intus per fidem et caritatem revolvere, ac crucis signaculo frontem armare, ipsumque ore fateri. Et in superliminaribus domorum: hoc est, altitudinem mentium, spem supernorum, intentionem et contemplationem cœlestium, debet jugiter in fide et dilectione passionis et sanguinis Christi fundare, intingere, conservare.
paras.en: [[12:7|And they shall take of the blood thereof, and put it upon both the side posts|Et sument de sanguine ejus, et ponent super utramque postem]]. By this it was signified that the Christian people ought to fortify, seal and guard its body and soul with faith and with constant remembrance of the Lord's passion, and to turn Christ over within itself by faith and charity, and to arm the forehead with the sign of the cross, and to confess him with the mouth. [[12:7|and on the upper door posts of the houses|Et in superliminaribus domorum]]: that is, the heights of their minds, the hope of things above, the aim and contemplation of heavenly things, it ought continually to ground, steep and keep in faith in and love of the passion and blood of Christ.

paras.t: Et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni: id est, Christifideles corpus Christi in sacramento Eucharistiæ sument, qui igne passionis assatus est, atque ex ardentissimæ caritatis igne se obtulit Patri oblationem et hostiam in odorem suavitatis, et ipse in nocte illa gravissime est afflictus. In cujus etiam noctis exordio se ipsum dedit discipulis manducandum, dicente Apostolo: Dominus noster in qua nocte tradebatur, accepit panem, etc. Et azymos panes: id est, exercitiis sinceriter virtuosis, et vitiorum commixtione carentibus, potissime contemplatione divinorum, et meditationibus mysticorum suas reficient mentes: cum lactucis agrestibus, quæ prorsus amaræ sunt, id est cum interna compassione Christi propter nos passi, et cum cordiali contritione ac deploratione præsentis exsilii. Quæ omnia in celebrantibus et communicantibus esse oportet, unde ait Vas electionis: Pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus. Itaque epulemur, non in fermento veteri, neque in fermento malitiæ et nequitiæ, sed in azymis sinceritatis et veritatis.
paras.en: [[12:8|And they shall eat the flesh that night roasted at the fire|Et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni]]: that is, Christ's faithful shall receive the body of Christ in the sacrament of the Eucharist, who was roasted with the fire of the passion, and out of the fire of most ardent charity offered himself to the Father as an oblation and a victim for an odour of sweetness, and who was himself most grievously afflicted on that night. At the beginning of that night, too, he gave himself to his disciples to be eaten, as the Apostle says: our Lord, [[1 Cor 11:23|the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread|in qua nocte tradebatur, accepit panem]], etc. [[12:8|and unleavened bread|Et azymos panes]]: that is, they shall refresh their minds with exercises sincerely virtuous and free of any admixture of vices, above all with the contemplation of divine things and meditations on the mysteries; [[12:8|with wild lettuce|cum lactucis agrestibus]], which is altogether bitter: that is, with inward compassion for Christ, who suffered for us, and with heartfelt contrition and lamentation over this present exile. All these things must be in those who celebrate and those who communicate; whence the Vessel of election [that is, St Paul, so called in Acts 9:15] says: [[1 Cor 5:7|Christ our pasch is sacrificed|Pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus]]. [[1 Cor 5:8|Therefore, let us feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness: but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth|Itaque epulemur, non in fermento veteri, neque in fermento malitiæ et nequitiæ, sed in azymis sinceritatis et veritatis]].

paras.t: Non comedetis ex eo crudum quid, nec coctum aqua: hoc est, corpus et sanguinem Christi non carnaliter, neque cum grossa imaginatione adspicietis, neque per philosophicam sapientiam mysteria Salvatoris discutietis; sed assum tantum igni: id est, per illuminationem et fervorem Spiritus Sancti intueri oportet, quidquid de ipso per fidem accipitur, ut per omnipotentiam Dei, incomprehensibilia fieri agnoscamus, per attestationem infallibilium, solique Deo possibilium signorum. Caput cum pedibus ejus et intestinis vorabitis: id est, universa quæ de Christo proponenda, credendaque sunt, videlicet divinitatis sublimia, et humanitatis declivia, ac ea quæ medio modo se habent, prompta fide et avida mente amplecti debetis. Interiora quoque et mystica, sed et exteriora ejus opera fideli mente apprehendetis, ut sitis in fide integri ac prorsus catholici. Nec remanebit ex eo quidquam usque mane: quia nihil de pertinentibus ad mysteria Salvatoris est relinquendum, aut convertendum in dubium. In Sacramento quoque non sunt caro, sanguis, anima et deitas Christi, ab invicem separata, sed totus ibidem continetur ac sumitur Christus. Si quid residuum fuerit, igne comburetis: id est, ea quæ fidei sunt, nec comprehendi queunt, omnipotentiæ et infallibili attestationi Spiritus Sancti, qui amor et ignis appellatur, sunt humiliter reservanda ac committenda, ita ut nihil vertatur in hæsitationem; sed licet angelus de cœlo evangelizet oppositum, respuatur.
paras.en: [[12:9|You shall not eat thereof any thing raw, nor boiled in water|Non comedetis ex eo crudum quid, nec coctum aqua]]: that is, you shall not look upon the body and blood of Christ carnally, nor with a gross imagination, nor shall you pick apart the mysteries of the Saviour by philosophical wisdom; [[12:9|but only roasted at the fire|sed assum tantum igni]]: that is, whatever is received of him by faith must be beheld by the light and fervour of the Holy Ghost, so that we acknowledge that incomprehensible things come about through the omnipotence of God, on the testimony of signs that are infallible and possible to God alone. [[12:9|you shall eat the head with the feet and entrails thereof|Caput cum pedibus ejus et intestinis vorabitis]]: that is, all that is to be set forth and believed concerning Christ, namely the heights of his divinity and the lowly things of his humanity, and those that stand between, you ought to embrace with ready faith and an eager mind. His inward and mystical works too, and his outward ones as well, you shall lay hold of with a faithful mind, that you may be whole in the faith and wholly catholic. [[12:10|Neither shall there remain any thing of it until morning|Nec remanebit ex eo quidquam usque mane]]: because nothing of what belongs to the mysteries of the Saviour is to be left aside or called into doubt. In the Sacrament, too, the flesh, blood, soul and Godhead of Christ are not separated from one another, but the whole Christ is contained and received there. [[12:10|If there be any thing left, you shall burn it with fire|Si quid residuum fuerit, igne comburetis]]: that is, the things of faith that cannot be comprehended are to be humbly reserved and committed to the omnipotence and infallible testimony of the Holy Ghost, who is called love and fire, so that nothing is turned into hesitation; but though [[Gal 1:8|an angel from heaven|angelus de cœlo]] should preach the contrary, let it be rejected.

paras.t: Sic autem comedetis illum: id est, ad communionem sacram ita vos disponetis ac ibitis. Renes vestros accingetis: id est, fluxum et desideria turpia restringetis, ut sitis corde et corpore casti, juxta illud Evangelii, Sint lumbi vestri præcincti. Calceamenta habebitis in pedibus: id est, gressus actionum vestrarum munietis sanctorum patrum exemplis; tenentes baculos in manibus, id est, crucis vexilla tenentes fide fortissima. Baculi quoque sunt curæ pastorales, sustentamenta virtutum, consolationes supernorum charismatum. Et comedetis festinanter: id est, cum omni promptitudine caritatis et agilitate virtutum accipietis sacramenta cœlestia, et exsequemini divina præcepta, mentesque vestras spiritualiter reficietis. Est enim Phase, id est transitus Domini: hoc est, per istam refectionem tanquam per salutare viaticum, ire debetis de præsenti exsilio ad beatificam deitatis hujus Agni fruitionem, et in omni bono incessanter proficere, quia nescitis diem et horam.
paras.en: [[12:11|And thus you shall eat it|Sic autem comedetis illum]]: that is, thus shall you dispose yourselves for holy communion, and so go to it. [[12:11|you shall gird your reins|Renes vestros accingetis]]: that is, you shall restrain the flux and base desires, that you may be chaste in heart and body, according to that word of the Gospel, [[Luke 12:35|Let your loins be girt|Sint lumbi vestri præcincti]]. [[12:11|you shall have shoes on your feet|Calceamenta habebitis in pedibus]]: that is, you shall fortify the steps of your actions with the examples of the holy fathers; [[12:11|holding staves in your hands|tenentes baculos in manibus]], that is, holding the standards of the cross with a most steadfast faith. The staves are also pastoral cares, the supports of the virtues, the consolations of heavenly gifts. [[12:11|and you shall eat in haste|Et comedetis festinanter]]: that is, you shall receive the heavenly sacraments with all the readiness of charity and nimbleness of the virtues, and carry out the divine precepts, and refresh your minds spiritually. [[12:11|for it is the Phase (that is the Passage) of the Lord|Est enim Phase, id est transitus Domini]]: that is, through this refreshment, as through a saving viaticum, you must pass from the present exile to the beatific enjoyment of the Godhead of this Lamb, and advance unceasingly in every good, because [[Matt 25:13|you know not the day nor the hour|nescitis diem et horam]] [the margin note is partly unreadable: Matth. xxv, 1…].

paras.t: Et transibo per terram Ægypti nocte illa, percutiamque omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, ab homine usque ad pecus. Per terram Ægypti intelligitur omnis natio incredulorum ac perversorum. In quibus Deus primogenita interfecit, quosdam misericorditer convertendo: in quibus primitiva et capitalia vitia dissipavit, ita quod desierunt esse quod erant per culpam, quemadmodum Salomon protestatur, Verte impios, et non erunt; quosdam vero juste derelinquendo, in quibus fuit mors culpæ, deinde mors æternæ miseriæ: sicque primogenita magis occidit, quia magnos in hoc sæculo præsertim reliquit, sicut ait Apostolus: Non multi sapientes, non multi nobiles sunt inter vos, sed abjecta mundi elegit Deus. Et in cunctis diis Ægypti faciam judicia. Per hoc figuratum est, quod Christus per suos implevit Apostolos, per quorum miracula, fana paganorum destruxit et idola. Erit autem sanguis vobis in signum. Quemadmodum enim Hebræi, quorum postes et liminaria erant sanguine tincta, de morte qua Ægyptii perierunt, sunt liberati; sic in Christi fide, et merito suæ passionis ac pretio sanguinis, redimuntur fideles nunc a morte peccati, deinde a morte infernalis supplicii, quibus plagantur increduli et ingrati.
paras.en: [[12:12|And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and will kill every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast|Et transibo per terram Ægypti nocte illa, percutiamque omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, ab homine usque ad pecus]]. By the land of Egypt is understood every nation of the unbelieving and perverse. Among them God slew the firstborn, converting some in mercy: in whom he destroyed the first and capital vices [that is, the chief or deadly sins, from which the others spring], so that they ceased to be what they were through sin, as Solomon declares, [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]]; but others by justly abandoning them, in whom there was the death of sin, and afterwards the death of eternal misery. And so he slew rather the firstborn, because he chiefly left aside the great ones of this world, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:26|not many wise|Non multi sapientes]], [[1 Cor 1:26|not many noble|non multi nobiles]] are among you, but the abject things of the world hath God chosen[[1 Cor 1:28||]]. [[12:12|and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments|Et in cunctis diis Ægypti faciam judicia]]. By this was prefigured what Christ fulfilled through his Apostles, through whose miracles he destroyed the temples and idols of the pagans. [[12:13|And the blood shall be unto you for a sign|Erit autem sanguis vobis in signum]]. For just as the Hebrews, whose posts and thresholds were dyed with blood, were delivered from the death by which the Egyptians perished, so in the faith of Christ, and by the merit of his passion and the price of his blood, the faithful are redeemed now from the death of sin, and afterwards from the death of the punishment of hell, with which the unbelieving and ungrateful are stricken.

paras.t: Habebitis autem hunc diem, etc., solennem. Christiani quippe Pascha Christi verissime celebrant, et suam per Christum redemptionem jugiter recolunt. Septem diebus azyma comedetis.
