Siquidem ipse Deus altissimus designatur, et appellatur nomine isto nominante, Omnipotens: sicque Omnipotens, est nominans nomen Dei. Nomen quoque Dei nominatum, id est ipse Deus hoc nomine, Omnipotens Deus, designatus, est realiter prorsus omnipotens. Nam quidquid contradictionem non implicat, et cuicumque ratio entis competere valet, hoc ipse potest. Cui in libro Sapientiæ dicitur: Subest tibi, quum volueris, posse. Jeremias quoque ait: Domine Deus, non erit tibi difficile omne verbum.
paras.en: [[15:3|The Lord is as a man of war|Dominus quasi vir pugnator]], that is, like a warrior, one who wages none but just and valiant wars. Lyra, however, says elsewhere that *as* (*quasi*) is not in the Hebrew, but the translator added it to suggest that God is called a man of war not because there is sex in Him, or anything bodily, according to the nature of the Godhead. So He is called a man of war in the way in which the Saviour says: [[John 15:1|I am the true vine: and my Father is the husbandman|Ego sum vitis vera, et Pater meus agricola est]]; which, according to Augustine, is to be understood by likeness, not properly. [[15:3|Almighty is his name|Omnipotens nomen ejus]]. This may be understood both of the naming name and of the named name [*nomen nominans*, the word that names, and *nomen nominatum*, the thing named by it]. For the most high God Himself is designated and called by this naming name, *Almighty*; and so *Almighty* is the naming name of God. And the named name of God, that is, God Himself designated by this name *Almighty God*, is really and altogether almighty. For whatever implies no contradiction, and whatever the notion of being can belong to, that He can do. To whom it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 12:18|thy power is at hand when thou wilt|Subest tibi, quum volueris, posse]]. Jeremias also says: [[Jer 32:17|O Lord God|Domine Deus]], [[Jer 32:17|no word shall be hard to thee|non erit tibi difficile omne verbum]].

paras.t: Currus Pharaonis, et exercitum ejus projecit in mare: quemadmodum præcedenti capitulo dictum est, Respiciens Dominus super castra Ægyptiorum per columnam ignis et nubis, subvertit rotas curruum, ferebanturque in profundum. Siquidem, ut ex Josepho atque Scholastica historia circa hoc tactum est, Dominus projecit super Ægyptios, fundum maris siccatum ingressos, intolerabiles imbres, gravesque tonitruos, coruscationes, ac lampades. Erant ibi currus sexcenti, et quinquaginta millia equitum, ducentaque millia peditum.
paras.en: [[15:4|Pharao's chariots and his army he hath cast into the sea|Currus Pharaonis, et exercitum ejus projecit in mare]]: as was said in the preceding chapter: [[Ex 14:24|the Lord looking upon the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of the cloud|Respiciens Dominus super castra Ægyptiorum per columnam ignis et nubis]] [[Ex 14:25|overthrew the wheels of the chariots, and they were carried into the deep|subvertit rotas curruum, ferebanturque in profundum]]. For, as was touched on there from Josephus and the Scholastic History, the Lord hurled upon the Egyptians, when they had entered the dried-up bottom of the sea, unbearable downpours, heavy thunders, lightnings and fiery flashes. There were there six hundred chariots, fifty thousand horsemen and two hundred thousand foot.

paras.t: Electi principes ejus, quos ipse præ cæteris elegit in duces bellorum, submersi sunt in mari Rubro; abyssi operuerunt eos. Abyssus et mare ac pelagus, pro eodem accipi solent. Unde et Jonas: Abyssus, inquit, vallavit me, pelagus operuit caput meum. Sed nunc de aquis ejusdem maris pluraliter dicitur, Abyssi, propter multitudinem partium aquæ profundarum, vel potius propter duas partes maris divisi, quæ ex utroque latere super Ægyptios irruerunt. Descenderunt in profundum quasi lapis, quia et corda habuerunt lapidea, omni iniquitate gravata. Iniquitas autem gravat mentem. Propter quod Zacharias ait propheta: Iniquitas sedet super talentum plumbi. Et Isaias: Væ populo gravi iniquitate. Hinc monet Apostolus: Deponentes omne pondus, et circumstans nos peccatum.
paras.en: [[15:4|his chosen captains|Electi principes ejus]], whom he chose above the rest as leaders in war, [[15:4|are drowned in the Red Sea|submersi sunt in mari Rubro]]; [[15:5|The depths have covered them|abyssi operuerunt eos]]. *Abyss*, *sea* and *main* [*abyssus*, *mare*, *pelagus*] are commonly taken for the same thing; hence Jonas too: [[Jon 2:6|the deep|Abyssus]], he says, [[Jon 2:6|hath closed me round about, the sea hath covered my head|vallavit me, pelagus operuit caput meum]]. But here *depths* [*abyssi*] is said in the plural of the waters of that one sea, because of the many parts of the deep water, or rather because of the two parts of the divided sea, which rushed in upon the Egyptians from either side. [[15:5|they are sunk to the bottom like a stone|Descenderunt in profundum quasi lapis]], because they also had hearts of stone, weighed down with every iniquity. And iniquity weighs down the mind; for which reason Zacharias the prophet says: Iniquity sits upon a talent of lead[[Zach 5:7||]][[Zach 5:8||]] [Denis sums up the prophet's vision of a woman, who is wickedness, sitting in a vessel shut with a talent of lead]. And Isaias: [[Is 1:4|Woe|Væ]] [[Is 1:4|a people laden with iniquity|populo gravi iniquitate]]. Hence the Apostle warns: [[Heb 12:1|laying aside every weight and sin which surrounds us|Deponentes omne pondus, et circumstans nos peccatum]].

paras.t: Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine; Dextera tua, Domine, percussit inimicum. Solet in Scripturis per dexteram Dei, ejus benignitas seu gratiosa protectio aut succursus intelligi, juxta illud Sapientiæ: Dextera sua teget eos. Et in Job: Operi manuum tuarum porriges dexteram. Interdum per dexteram designatur potestas, juxta illud Job: Confitebor quod salvare te possit dextera tua. Aliquando vero per dexteram Dei significatur ejus æqualitas, seu potior bonitatis ejus fruitio, ut in Psalmo: Sede a dextris meis. Quandoque per dexteram Dei exprimitur rigor divinæ justitiæ, et districta ultio ejus, qua Deus durius percutit: quemadmodum per dexteram homo fortius verberat, quam per sinistram. Sicque in Psalmo accipitur: Dextera tua inveniat omnes qui te oderunt. Pones eos ut clibanum ignis, etc. Sic quoque accipitur modo, quum dicitur: Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine, hoc est, rigor seu vis tuæ justitiæ magnifice se ostendit in forti Ægyptiorum punitione, per quam magnificata est, id est, magna esse innotuit, et magna, imo immensa, a multis est reputata. Quæ etiam percussit inimicum, hoc est, Pharaonem principem hostium populi tui in mari exstinxit, imo et ante per decem plagas dure multipliciterque afflixit. Quidam tamen per dexteram Dei, intelligunt unigenitum Filium ejus: de qua expositione in sequenti articulo erit sermo.
paras.en: [[15:6|Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength|Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine]]: [[15:6|thy right hand, O Lord, hath slain the enemy|Dextera tua, Domine, percussit inimicum]] [*percussit*, "struck"]. In the Scriptures the right hand of God is usually understood as His kindness, or His gracious protection or help, according to that of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:17|with his right hand he will cover them|Dextera sua teget eos]]. And in Job: [[Job 14:15|to the work of thy hands thou shalt reach out thy right hand|Operi manuum tuarum porriges dexteram]]. Sometimes the right hand signifies power, according to that of Job: [[Job 40:9|I will confess that thy right hand is able to save thee|Confitebor quod salvare te possit dextera tua]]. Sometimes again the right hand of God signifies equality with Him, or the higher enjoyment of His goodness, as in the Psalm: [[Ps 109:1|Sit thou at my right hand|Sede a dextris meis]]. And sometimes the right hand of God expresses the rigour of divine justice and His strict vengeance, with which God strikes the harder, just as a man strikes harder with the right hand than with the left. So it is taken in the Psalm: [[Ps 20:9|let thy right hand find out all them that hate thee|Dextera tua inveniat omnes qui te oderunt]]. [[Ps 20:10|Thou shalt make them as an oven of fire|Pones eos ut clibanum ignis]], etc. And so it is taken now, when it is said: [[15:6|Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength|Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine]], that is, the rigour or force of Thy justice showed itself magnificently in the mighty punishment of the Egyptians, by which it was magnified, that is, it became known to be great, and was reckoned by many to be great, nay boundless. It also [[15:6|hath slain the enemy|percussit inimicum]], that is, it destroyed in the sea Pharao, the chief of the enemies of Thy people, and before that had afflicted him harshly and in many ways by the ten plagues. Some, however, understand by the right hand of God His only-begotten Son: of this exposition we shall speak in the following article.

paras.t: Et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti adversarios meos. Gloria Dei hoc loco vocatur ejus majestas: quæ quamvis in se ipsa sit una simplexque, tamen propter suorum diversitatem effectuum, multiplex nuncupatur: quemadmodum et misericordia Dei, secundum illud: Misericordias Domini in æternum cantabo. Et denuo: Reminiscere miserationum tuarum, Domine, et misericordiarum tuarum quæ a sæculo sunt. Itaque ait: In multitudine gloriæ tuæ, hoc est in majestate tua multiplici per effectum, seu in multis ejus præclaris ac miris effectibus, hoc est per diversa prodigia, contrivisti Ægyptios, tam in terra eorum primogenitos occidendo, quam in mari Rubro tot millia submergendo.
paras.en: [[15:7|And in the multitude of thy glory thou hast put down|Et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti]] my adversaries [Denis reads *adversarios meos*, "my adversaries"; the Vulgate has *tuos*, "thy"]. The glory of God is here the name for His majesty, which, though in itself it is one and simple, is yet called manifold because of the diversity of its effects: as is the mercy of God too, according to that: [[Ps 88:2|The mercies of the Lord I will sing for ever|Misericordias Domini in æternum cantabo]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxviii, 1]. And again: [[Ps 24:6|Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world|Reminiscere miserationum tuarum, Domine, et misericordiarum tuarum quæ a sæculo sunt]]. So he says: [[15:7|in the multitude of thy glory|In multitudine gloriæ tuæ]], that is, in Thy majesty, manifold in its effects, or in its many glorious and wonderful effects, that is, by divers prodigies, Thou hast crushed the Egyptians, both by slaying their firstborn in their own land and by drowning so many thousands in the Red Sea.

paras.t: Misisti iram tuam, quæ devoravit eos sicut stipulam, id est, justitiæ tuæ vindictam effudisti, quæ consumpsit Ægyptios, sicut ignis stipulam valde velociter, prout de aliis fertur in Psalmo: Sicut ignis qui comburit silvam, et sicut flamma comburens montes, ita persequeris illos in tempestate tua. Et in Isaia: Sicut devorat stipulam lingua ignis, sic radix eorum quasi favilla erit. Et in spiritu furoris tui, id est in impetuoso effectu tuæ justitiæ, congregatæ sunt aquæ, id est, partes aquæ divisæ, se recollegerunt super Ægyptios pariter irruendo. Vel, Congregatæ sunt, id est, in partes seorsum quasi consolidatæ. Quod quamvis fuerit pie factum pro Hebræorum evasione, fuit tamen Ægyptiis submersionis occasio.
paras.en: [[15:7|thou hast sent thy wrath, which hath devoured them like stubble|Misisti iram tuam, quæ devoravit eos sicut stipulam]], that is, Thou hast poured out the vengeance of Thy justice, which consumed the Egyptians as fire consumes stubble, very swiftly; as is said of others in the Psalm: [[Ps 82:15|As fire which burneth the wood: and as a flame burning mountains|Sicut ignis qui comburit silvam, et sicut flamma comburens montes]] [[Ps 82:16|So shalt thou pursue them with thy tempest|ita persequeris illos in tempestate tua]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxii, 14, 16]. And in Isaias: [[Is 5:24|as the tongue of the fire devoureth the stubble|Sicut devorat stipulam lingua ignis]], [[Is 5:24|so shall their root be as ashes|sic radix eorum quasi favilla erit]]. [[15:8|And with the blast of thy anger|Et in spiritu furoris tui]], that is, in the vehement working of Thy justice, [[15:8|the waters were gathered together|congregatæ sunt aquæ]], that is, the divided parts of the water gathered themselves together again, rushing in upon the Egyptians all at once. Or, [[15:8|were gathered together|Congregatæ sunt]], that is, were as it were made solid, in parts set apart. And though this was done in mercy for the escape of the Hebrews, yet for the Egyptians it was the occasion of their drowning.

paras.t: Stetit unda fluens: id est, gurges aquæ ex sua natura mollis ac fluidus, divina virtute stetit fixus, ut tellus, atque ut loquitur Origenes. Soliditatem liquor recepit, et coactus est fluctus in cumulum, ac unda in se ipsam repressa. Nempe (sicut in libro Job legitur) superficies abyssi constringitur frigore, quanto magis, Creatore jubente, undæ ejus figuntur? Quemadmodum enim in exordio sæculorum Deus præfixit Oceano terminum sui fluxus, ne terram operiat (secundum quod ad Job testatur: Quis conclusit ostiis mare, quando erumpebat quasi de vulva procedens? Circumdedi illud terminis meis, et posui vectes et ostia, et dixi: Hucusque venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos); sic ex Dei præcepto divisum est mare Rubrum, et partes divisæ steterunt in altum fixæ, adunatæ ex Creatoris imperio. Congregatæ sunt abyssi in medio maris, id est intra ripas Rubri maris. Atque in tali divisione et consolidatione undarum fuit magna elevatio earumdem, non tamen egressæ sunt ripam. Præterea, sicut ait Salvator, Ex abundantia cordis os loquitur: ideo Moyses ex suæ devotionis fervore, et insoliti miraculi admiratione, divinorumque operum novitate et congratulatione, eamdem sententiam multoties repetit sub aliis verbis, quemadmodum et Psalmista, dicendo: Quoniam exaudivit Dominus vocem fletus mei; exaudivit Dominus deprecationem meam; Dominus orationem meam suscepit.
paras.en: [[15:8|the flowing water stood|Stetit unda fluens]]: that is, the flood of water, by its nature soft and fluid, stood fixed by divine power like solid earth; and, as Origen says, the liquid took on solidity, the wave was driven into a heap, and the water was held back upon itself. For indeed (as we read in the book of Job) [[Job 38:30|the surface of the deep is congealed|superficies abyssi constringitur]] with cold [the margin reads "… 30", that is, Job 38:30]: how much more are its waters made fast at the Creator's command? [Two further margin notes beside the next lines are unreadable in the transcription.] For just as in the beginning of the ages God fixed for the Ocean a limit to its flowing, lest it cover the earth (as He testifies to Job: [[Job 38:8|Who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth as issuing out of the womb|Quis conclusit ostiis mare, quando erumpebat quasi de vulva procedens?]] [[Job 38:10|I set my bounds around it, and made it bars and doors|Circumdedi illud terminis meis, et posui vectes et ostia]]: [[Job 38:11|And I said: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt go no further, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves|et dixi: Hucusque venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos]]), so at God's command the Red Sea was divided, and the divided parts stood fixed on high, made one by the Creator's bidding. [[15:8|the depths were gathered together in the midst of the sea|Congregatæ sunt abyssi in medio maris]], that is, within the banks of the Red Sea. And in this dividing and making solid of the waters they rose up greatly, yet did not go out over the shore. Moreover, as the Saviour says, [[Matt 12:34|out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh|Ex abundantia cordis os loquitur]]: therefore Moses, out of the fervour of his devotion, his wonder at so unwonted a miracle, and the newness of the divine works and his rejoicing in them, repeats the same thought many times in other words, as the Psalmist also does, saying: [[Ps 6:9|for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping|Quoniam exaudivit Dominus vocem fletus mei]]; [[Ps 6:10|The Lord hath heard my supplication: the Lord hath received my prayer|exaudivit Dominus deprecationem meam; Dominus orationem meam suscepit]].

paras.t: Dixit inimicus, videlicet Pharao seu quicumque de ejus exercitu: Persequar Hebræos, et comprehendam eos; dividam spolia, bona eorum diripiendo, et implebitur anima mea, id est, juxta desiderium voluntatis meæ eos tractabo ac spoliabo. Evaginabo gladium meum, interficiet eos manus mea. Præcedenti capitulo Pharao et ejus ministri dixisse leguntur: Quid voluimus facere ut dimitteremus Israel, ne serviret nobis? Circa quod dictum est, quod Pharao et Ægyptii intendebant filios Israel violenter reducere ad serviendum sibi, ut antea in Ægypto: idcirco non reor, quod nunc voluerint eos omnes occidere, sed quosdam, præsertim principaliores ac ditiores.
paras.en: [[15:9|The enemy said|Dixit inimicus]], that is, Pharao, or whoever of his army: [[15:9|I will pursue|Persequar]] the Hebrews, [[15:9|and overtake|et comprehendam]] them; [[15:9|I will divide the spoils|dividam spolia]], by plundering their goods, and [[15:9|my soul shall have its fill|implebitur anima mea]], that is, I will deal with them and despoil them as my will desires. [[15:9|I will draw my sword, my hand shall slay them|Evaginabo gladium meum, interficiet eos manus mea]]. In the preceding chapter Pharao and his servants are read to have said: [[Ex 14:5|What meant we to do, that we let Israel go from serving us?|Quid voluimus facere ut dimitteremus Israel, ne serviret nobis?]] On which it was said that Pharao and the Egyptians meant to bring the children of Israel back by force to serve them, as before in Egypt; therefore I do not think that they now wished to kill them all, but some, especially the chief and the richest.

paras.t: Flavit spiritus tuus, id est, ventus a te productus, et grandis imbrium fulgurumque tempestas, diffusa sunt super aquas. Vel, Spiritus tuus flavit, id est, ex tua indignatione motæ sunt aquæ, sicut ex flatu pulvis movetur. Et operuit eos mare; submersi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis vehementibus.
paras.en: [[15:10|Thy wind blew|Flavit spiritus tuus]], that is, a wind brought forth by Thee, and a great storm of rain and lightning, spread over the waters. Or, [[15:10|Thy wind blew|Spiritus tuus flavit]] [*spiritus*: wind, breath or spirit], that is, the waters were stirred by Thy indignation, as dust is stirred by a breath. [[15:10|and the sea covered them|Et operuit eos mare]]; [[15:10|they sunk as lead in the mighty waters|submersi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis vehementibus]].

paras.t: Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? quis similis tui? quasi dicat, Nullus omnino: quoniam omnis potestas creata, deficit infinite ab increata virtute. Alia translatio habet: Quis similis tui in diis, Domine? quasi dicat, In his apparet infirmitas falsitasque deorum gentilium, qui suos non potuerunt juvare cultores. Hinc in Jeremia scriptum est: Non est similis tui, Domine; magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine. Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium? Et rursus in Jeremia propheta Deus: Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me? Et: Quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo? Verumtamen creaturæ rationales et intellectuales dicuntur Deo assimilari. Joannes quoque apostolus in prima sua fatetur Canonica: Sicut ille est, et nos sumus in hoc mundo. Et rursus: Nondum, inquit, apparuit quid erimus. Scimus quoniam quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est. Verum in his verbis, Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? sumitur simile pro æquali. Nil autem Deo æquale est, imo finiti ad infinitum nulla est comparatio.
paras.en: [[15:11|Who is like to thee, among the strong, O Lord? who is like to thee|Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? quis similis tui]]? As if to say: No one at all; for every created power falls infinitely short of the uncreated might. Another translation has: Who is like to thee among the gods, O Lord? As if to say: In these things the weakness and falsehood of the gods of the gentiles is seen, who could not help their worshippers. Hence it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 10:6|There is none like to thee, O Lord: thou art great, and great is thy name in might.|Non est similis tui, Domine: magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine.]] [[Jer 10:7|Who shall not fear thee, O king of nations|Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium]]? And again God says in Jeremias the prophet: [[Jer 49:19|who is like to me? and who shall abide me|Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me]]? And: [[Jer 49:19|who is that shepherd that can withstand my countenance|Quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo]]? Yet rational and intellectual creatures are said to be made like to God. The apostle John too declares in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 4:17|as he is, we also are in this world|Sicut ille est, et nos sumus in hoc mundo]]. And again: [[1 John 3:2|it hath not yet appeared|Nondum]], he says, [[1 John 3:2|what we shall be. We know that when he shall appear we shall be like to him: because we shall see him as he is|apparuit quid erimus. Scimus quoniam quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est]]. But in these words, [[15:11|Who is like to thee, among the strong, O Lord|Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine]]? *like* is taken for *equal*. Now nothing is equal to God; nay, between the finite and the infinite there is no proportion at all.

paras.t: Magnificus in sanctitate, hoc est magna et mira efficiens sancte ac virtuose. Quemadmodum enim Deus dicitur magna facere in sapientia, ita et in sanctitate, quoniam sanctus est in omnibus operibus suis. Hercules autem, Alexander Magnus, Hector Trojæ, et consimiles, fecerunt aliqua magna, non in sanctitate, sed magis in vanitate. Terribilis, propter inscrutabilia tua judicia, et ob tuæ rigorem justitiæ, ac metuendos effectus. De quo ait Propheta: Venite, et videte opera Dei, terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum. Ideo sanctus Job ait: Deus, cujus iræ resistere nemo potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem. Cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest: idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor. In Evangelio quoque Christus ait: Eum timete, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam ignis. Atque laudabilis, quia virtuose, sapienter, et irreprehensibiliter omnia agens: et faciens mirabilia, juxta illud Job: Qui facit magna, et inscrutabilia, et mirabilia, quorum non est numerus. Nec solum in supernaturalibus, sed item in naturalibus, et præsertim in operibus gratiæ et gloriæ, Deus mirabilia et incomprehensibilia operatur.
paras.en: [[15:11|glorious in holiness|Magnificus in sanctitate]], that is, working great and wonderful things holily and virtuously. For just as God is said to do great things in wisdom, so also in holiness, since He is [[Ps 144:17|holy in all his works|sanctus est in omnibus operibus suis]] [the margin gives Ps. cxliv, 13, 17: the words stand in both verses]. But Hercules, Alexander the Great, Hector of Troy and the like did some great things, not in holiness but rather in vanity. [[15:11|terrible|Terribilis]], because of Thy unsearchable judgments, the rigour of Thy justice, and its dread effects. Of which the Prophet says: [[Ps 65:5|Come and see the works of God; who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men|Venite, et videte opera Dei, terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum]]. Therefore holy Job says: [[Job 9:13|God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world|Deus, cujus iræ resistere nemo potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem]]. [[Job 23:13|no man can turn away his thought|Cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest]]: [[Job 23:15|therefore I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him, I am made pensive with fear|idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor]]. In the Gospel, too, Christ says: [[Matt 10:28|fear him that can destroy both soul and body in hell|Eum timete, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam ignis]] [Denis's *qui habet potestatem*, "who hath power", is from Luke 12:5]. [[15:11|and praise-worthy|Atque laudabilis]], as doing all things virtuously, wisely and blamelessly; [[15:11|doing wonders|et faciens mirabilia]], according to that of Job: [[Job 9:10|Who doth things great and incomprehensible, and wonderful, of which there is no number|Qui facit magna, et inscrutabilia, et mirabilia, quorum non est numerus]]. Not only in supernatural things but also in natural, and especially in the works of grace and of glory, God works wonderful and incomprehensible things.

paras.t: […] scilicet Rabba Paulus, reprehendendum non esset: quoniam ira non solum ex tristitia, sed etiam ex timore causatur, imo ex desperatione potest oriri. Sunt enim diversæ ac variæ causæ, secundum Aristotelem, Gregoriumque Nyssenum ac Damascenum, prout Thomas in prima secundæ, quæstione 47, pulchre declarat, inter cetera dicens: Motivum seu causa iræ, est aliquid contra placitum irascentis commissum, sive omissum. Ideo quidquid vergit in gravamen alterius, potest in eo iram causare. Qui autem est alteri causa timoris, gravat eum: sicque ille ex tali timore potest iram concipere contra gravantem. Nihilo minus verum est, quod ira magis directe et immediatius ex tristitia quam ex timore nascatur. Denique qui alium ad tantam impellit angustiam, ut quasi desperet se posse evadere, frequenter fit illi occasio, quod acrius contra ipsum sic angustiantem insurgat per iram. Et hoc in bellis accidere solet. Propter quod Abner secundo Regum ait ad Joab: Quare non dicis populo, ut omittat persequi fratres suos? An ignoras quam periculosa sit desperatio?
paras.en: […] [A column of text is lost in the transcription here (PDF 703, p. 597): it must have held the comment on vv. 12 and 13 and the beginning of that on v. 14, *Nations rose up, and were angry*, to which what follows belongs.] namely Rabba Paulus [presumably Paul of Burgos, the converted rabbi whose Additions accompany Lyra's commentary], it would not be blameworthy: for anger is caused not only by sorrow but also by fear, and can even arise from despair. For its causes are divers and various, according to Aristotle, Gregory of Nyssa and Damascene, as Thomas finely sets out in the First Part of the Second Part, question 47, saying among other things: The motive or cause of anger is something done, or left undone, against the will of the one who is angry. Therefore whatever tends to another's hurt can cause anger in him. Now he who is a cause of fear to another hurts him; and so from such fear he can conceive anger against the one who hurts him. Nevertheless it is true that anger arises more directly and immediately from sorrow than from fear. Lastly, he who drives another into such straits that he all but despairs of escaping often gives him occasion to rise up the more fiercely in anger against the one who so presses him. And this commonly happens in wars. For which reason Abner, in the second book of Kings, says to Joab: Why dost thou not [[2 Kings 2:26|bid the people cease from pursuing after their brethren?|dicis populo, ut omittat persequi fratres suos?]] [[2 Kings 2:26|knowest thou not that it is dangerous to drive people to despair|An ignoras quam periculosa sit desperatio?]]

paras.t: Tunc conturbati sunt principes Edom, videlicet, rex et principes Idumæorum, præ admiratione eorum quæ audierant facta circa Ægyptios, et sibi tale quid posse accidere verebantur. Robustos Moab obtinuit tremor. Nam sicut in Numeris legitur, Balac rex Moabitarum convocatis principibus Moab et Madian, dixit: Ita delebit hic populus omnes habitantes in terminis nostris, sicut bos solet carpere herbam usque ad solum. Obriguerunt omnes habitatores Chanaan, id est, Chananæi ultra Jordanem morantes, in tantum expaverunt ex adventu filiorum Israel, quod timor cordis causavit tremorem in corpore, et membra eorum obrigescere fecit. Hinc in libro Josue asseritur: Postquam audierunt omnes reges Amorrhæorum, qui habitabant trans Jordanem, et cuncti reges Chanaan, quod siccasset Dominus fluenta Jordanis coram Israel donec transierunt, dissolutum est cor eorum, et non remansit in eis spiritus. Rahab quoque dixit ad exploratores Israelitarum: Pertimuimus, et elanguit cor nostrum ad introitum vestrum.
paras.en: [[15:15|Then were the princes of Edom troubled|Tunc conturbati sunt principes Edom]], that is, the king and princes of the Idumeans, in amazement at what they had heard was done to the Egyptians; and they feared that some such thing might befall themselves. [[15:15|trembling seized on the stout men of Moab|Robustos Moab obtinuit tremor]]. For, as we read in Numbers, Balac king of the Moabites, having called together the princes of Moab and Madian, said: [[Num 22:4|So will this people destroy all that dwell in our borders, as the ox is wont to eat the grass to the very roots|Ita delebit hic populus omnes habitantes in terminis nostris, sicut bos solet carpere herbam usque ad solum]]. [[15:15|all the inhabitants of Chanaan became stiff|Obriguerunt omnes habitatores Chanaan]], that is, the Chanaanites dwelling beyond the Jordan were so terrified at the coming of the children of Israel that the fear of their hearts caused trembling in their bodies and made their limbs grow stiff. Hence it is said in the book of Josue: [[Jos 5:1|when all the kings of the Amorrhites, who dwelt beyond the Jordan|Postquam audierunt omnes reges Amorrhæorum, qui habitabant trans Jordanem]], [[Jos 5:1|and all the kings of Chanaan|et cuncti reges Chanaan]], [[Jos 5:1|had heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the children of Israel, till they passed over, their heart failed them, and there remained no spirit in them|quod siccasset Dominus fluenta Jordanis coram Israel donec transierunt, dissolutum est cor eorum, et non remansit in eis spiritus]]. Rahab too said to the spies of the Israelites: [[Jos 2:11|we were affrighted, and our heart fainted away|Pertimuimus, et elanguit cor nostrum]] [[Jos 2:11|at your coming in|ad introitum vestrum]].

paras.t: Deinde divinæ præordinationi congaudens, ait: Irruat super eos formido et pavor, ut corde et corpore contremiscant, in magnitudine brachii tui, id est ex magnis et mirabilibus tuæ potestatis operibus, quæ fecisti in Pharaone et Ægyptiis, in regibus Sehon, Og, ac Madian, in divisione maris Rubri, et desiccatione fundi Jordanis. Fiant immobiles, hoc est, ad resistendum penitus impotentes, quasi lapis, donec pertranseat populus tuus, Domine, donec pertranseat populus tuus iste quem possedisti, hoc est, quousque populus Israeliticus iste tibi peculiaris, et præ ceteris tuo cultui deputatus, perambulet eremum ac Jordanem, veniatque ad terram ei promissam. Et quod ait, Donec, non est sic intelligendum, quasi postea potuerint Israelitis resistere, quamvis hoc tentaverunt, sed victi fuerunt, nisi quod viri Hai semel fugaverunt filios Israel, et aliquos prostraverunt, ut scribitur Josue septimo. Verum (ut ait Philosophus) quod modicum est, pro nihilo reputatur inter multa et magna.
paras.en: Then, rejoicing in God's foreordaining, he says: [[15:16|Let fear and dread fall upon them|Irruat super eos formido et pavor]], so that they may tremble in heart and body, [[15:16|in the greatness of thy arm|in magnitudine brachii tui]], that is, from the great and wonderful works of Thy power which Thou hast done on Pharao and the Egyptians, on the kings Sehon, Og and Madian, in the dividing of the Red Sea and the drying up of the bed of the Jordan. [[15:16|let them become immoveable|Fiant immobiles]], that is, wholly powerless to resist, [[15:16|as a stone, until thy people, O Lord, pass by: until this thy people pass by, which thou hast possessed|quasi lapis, donec pertranseat populus tuus, Domine, donec pertranseat populus tuus iste quem possedisti]], that is, until this Israelite people, Thy own peculiar people, set apart above the rest for Thy worship, has passed through the desert and the Jordan and come to the land promised to it. And *until* is not to be understood as though afterwards they could withstand the Israelites: though they tried it, they were overcome; save that the men of Hai once put the children of Israel to flight and struck some of them down, as is written in the seventh chapter of Josue[[Jos 7:5||]]. But (as the Philosopher says) what is slight is reckoned as nothing among many great things.

paras.t: Introduces eos, puta Hebræos, in terram promissionis, et plantabis in monte hereditatis tuæ, hoc est, firmiter eos facies habitare in Jerusalem, et in monte sancto, quem elegisti tibi in hereditatem populi tui. Vel, per montem intelligitur tota terra Chanaan montuosa. Plantabis etiam eos in firmissimo habitaculo tuo, quod operatus es, Domine, hoc est, in fortibus urbibus, castris et fortalitiis constitues eos ad habitandum: quæ tua virtute fient. Vel, per firmissimum habitaculum, intelligitur templum et regale palatium, quæ Deo auxiliante per Salomonem sunt facta in monte Sion, et circa, ut patet tertio Regum. Unde subjungitur: Sanctuarium tuum, Domine: quasi dicat, Firmissimum habitaculum id dico sanctuarium, id est templum tuum, Domine; quod firmaverunt manus tuæ, id est, sapientia et omnipotentia tua induxit, ditavit et illuminavit Salomonem ad construendum hoc templum. Quum enim David voluisset hoc attentare, Dominus dixit per Nathan ad eum: Tu non ædificabis mihi domum, sed Salomon filius tuus.
paras.en: [[15:17|Thou shalt bring them in|Introduces eos]], namely the Hebrews, into the land of promise, [[15:17|and plant them in the mountain of thy inheritance|et plantabis in monte hereditatis tuæ]], that is, Thou shalt make them dwell firmly in Jerusalem and on the holy mountain which Thou hast chosen for Thyself as the inheritance of Thy people. Or, by the mountain is understood the whole mountainous land of Chanaan. Thou shalt plant them also [[15:17|in thy most firm habitation, which thou hast made, O Lord|firmissimo habitaculo tuo, quod operatus es, Domine]], that is, Thou wilt settle them to dwell in strong cities, camps and fortresses, which shall be made by Thy power. Or, by the most firm habitation is understood the temple and the royal palace, which with God's help were built by Solomon on Mount Sion and round about it, as appears in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 8:1||]][[3 Kings 8:13||]]. Hence there follows: [[15:17|thy sanctuary, O Lord|Sanctuarium tuum, Domine]]: as if to say, The most firm habitation I mean is the sanctuary, that is, Thy temple, O Lord; [[15:17|which thy hands have established|quod firmaverunt manus tuæ]], that is, Thy wisdom and almighty power moved, enriched and enlightened Solomon to build this temple. For when David wished to undertake it, the Lord said to him through Nathan: [[3 Kings 8:19|thou shalt not build me a house|Tu non ædificabis mihi domum]], but Solomon thy son [the margin reads III Reg. xiii, … (perhaps viii, 19, where Solomon recalls these words); Nathan's message itself is in 2 Kings 7:5, 12–13 and 1 Par 17:4, 11–12, and David names Solomon in 1 Par 28:3, 6].

paras.t: Dominus regnabit in æternum et ultra. In Hebræo habetur, In sæculum, id est, per omne tempus veteris Testamenti regnabit specialiter in populo Hebræorum. Et ultra: quia relicto populo illo, ob suam perfidiam, regnat deinceps in populo christiano, in via per fidem usque ad mundi finem, deinde in patria per speciem sine fine in sempiternum. Æternum autem in Scripturis quandoque pro tempore alicujus usque ad vitæ suæ finem accipitur, juxta illud: Erit tibi servus in æternum.
paras.en: [[15:18|The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.|Dominus regnabit in æternum et ultra.]] The Hebrew has *for an age* [*in sæculum*], that is, through the whole time of the Old Testament He will reign in a special way among the Hebrew people. [[15:18|and ever|Et ultra]] [*et ultra*, literally "and beyond"]: because, having left that people for their faithlessness, He reigns thereafter in the Christian people, on the way by faith until the end of the world, and then in the fatherland by sight, without end for evermore. For *ever* [*æternum*] in the Scriptures is sometimes taken for a man's time until the end of his life, according to that: [[Deut 15:17|he shall serve thee for ever|Erit tibi servus in æternum]].

paras.t: Ingressus est enim eques Pharao cum curribus et equitibus ejus in mare, id est in profundum maris Rubri siccatum: et reduxit super eos Dominus aquas maris. […] Illud clarum est ex prædictis. Tamen quod ait, Enim, non denotat causam a priori, quod Dominus regnabit in æternum et ultra, sed potius notat signum hujus rei et causam a posteriori.
paras.en: [[15:19|For Pharao went in on horseback with his chariots and horsemen into the sea|Ingressus est enim eques Pharao cum curribus et equitibus ejus in mare]], that is, into the depth of the Red Sea, which had been dried up: [[15:19|and the Lord brought back upon them the waters of the sea|et reduxit super eos Dominus aquas maris]]. […] [A line or two are lost here in the transcription, at the top of the right-hand column of PDF 705.] That is clear from what has been said. Yet *for* [*enim*: the transcription reads "Latin", plainly a slip for *Enim*, the word of v. 19] does not denote the cause a priori of the Lord's reigning for ever and ever, but rather denotes a sign of it, and a cause a posteriori [a priori: the cause from which a thing follows; a posteriori: an effect from which the thing is known].

paras.t: Denique, sicut in Scholastica historia recitatur, moratus est populus Israel juxta littus maris Rubri septem diebus, jacentibus ibi cadaveribus Ægyptiorum, et cum tympanis ac musicis instrumentis veniebant singulis diebus ad littus, cantabantque Domino Moysis canticum jam explanatum, viri seorsum, et mulieres seorsum. In cujus rei memoriam, septem diebus paschalibus cantando redimus ad fontes Baptismi. Abstulerunt quoque arma, et cetera quæ eis placuerunt, ab Ægyptiis interfectis atque ejectis.
paras.en: Lastly, as is related in the Scholastic History, the people of Israel stayed by the shore of the Red Sea for seven days, while the corpses of the Egyptians lay there; and each day they came to the shore with timbrels and musical instruments, and sang to the Lord the canticle of Moses now explained, the men apart and the women apart. In memory of this, on the seven days of Easter we go back singing to the fonts of Baptism [the procession to the font at Vespers in Easter week]. They also took away the arms, and whatever else pleased them, from the Egyptians who had been slain and cast up.

15.title: Expositio allegorica ejusdem cantici: Cantemus Domino
15.title_en: Allegorical exposition of the same canticle: Let us sing to the Lord

paras.t: De Domino nostro Jesu Christo, unico Dei Filio, et ejus mysteriis, canticum istud convenienter exponitur.
paras.en: This canticle is fittingly expounded of our Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, and of His mysteries.

paras.t: Christiani igitur attendentes se virtute et meritis Christi a potestate diaboli per Pharaonem designati, atque a jugo vitiorum et servitute peccati vilissima erutos, in voce gratiarum actionis et laudis se invicem cohortentur, et ferventi ex devotione pronuntient: Cantemus Domino, creatori ac salvatori nostro propter nos incarnato, qui in femore et vestimento suo habet scriptum, Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Gloriose enim magnificatus est, quemadmodum a Michæa fuit prædictum: Et magnificabitur in medio universæ terræ. Quum enim exinanivisset se, formam servi accipiens, in ipsa forma servili, id est humanitate assumpta, magnificatus est ab angelis qui in ejus nativitate cecinerunt, et ei in deserto ministraverunt. Magnificatus quoque est in miraculis tot et tantis, quod videntes dixerunt: Nunquam sic apparuit in Israel. Magnificatus est item a Patre, qui in baptismo et transfiguratione dixit ad eum: Tu es Filius meus dilectus, in te mihi complacui. Magnificatus est etiam a Spiritu Sancto, qui in specie columbæ descendit et mansit super eum. Quumque factus fuisset Patri obediens usque ad mortem crucis, exaltavit illum Pater, et dedit ei nomen quod est super omne nomen, ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur, cœlestium, terrestrium, et infernorum. Deinde per Apostolorum prædicationem atque miracula, per omnia mundi regna. Estque copiose impletum, quod a Daniele erat prædictum: Filius hominis, scilicet Christus, ad Antiquum dierum pervenit, id est ad Patrem æternum, et ipse dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum: et omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Potestas ejus potestas æterna, quæ non auferetur, et regnum ejus quod non corrumpetur.
paras.en: Christians, then, considering that by the power and merits of Christ they have been rescued from the power of the devil, signified by Pharao, and from the yoke of vices and the most vile servitude of sin, should exhort one another with the voice of thanksgiving and praise, and say out of fervent devotion: [[15:1|Let us sing to the Lord|Cantemus Domino]], our Creator and Saviour, made flesh for our sake, who has written on His thigh and His garment: [[Apoc 19:16|KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]]. [[15:1|For he is gloriously magnified|Gloriose enim magnificatus est]], as was foretold by Michæas: And he shall be magnified in the midst of the whole earth[[Mich 5:4||]] [Denis's wording; the Vulgate has 'he shall be magnified even to the ends of the earth']. For when He had [[Phil 2:7|emptied himself, taking the form of a servant|exinanivisset se, formam servi accipiens]], in that very form of a servant, that is, in the humanity He had taken, He was magnified by the angels who sang at His birth[[Luke 2:13||]] and ministered to Him in the desert[[Matt 4:11||]]. He was magnified also in miracles so many and so great that those who saw them said: [[Matt 9:33|Never was the like seen in Israel|Nunquam sic apparuit in Israel]]. He was magnified likewise by the Father, who at His baptism and transfiguration[[Matt 17:5||]] said to Him: [[Luke 3:22|Thou art my beloved Son. In thee I am well pleased|Tu es Filius meus dilectus, in te mihi complacui]]. He was magnified too by the Holy Ghost, who came down in the form of a dove [[John 1:32|and he remained upon him|et mansit super eum]]. And when He had been made [[Phil 2:8|obedient|obediens]] to the Father [[Phil 2:8|unto death|usque ad mortem crucis]] of the cross, the Father [[Phil 2:9|hath exalted him and hath given him a name which is above all names|exaltavit illum Pater, et dedit ei nomen quod est super omne nomen]]: [[Phil 2:10|That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth|ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur, cœlestium, terrestrium, et infernorum]]. Then He was magnified through the preaching and miracles of the Apostles[[Mark 16:20||]], through all the kingdoms of the world. And so there was abundantly fulfilled what Daniel had foretold: [[Dan 7:13|the Son of man|Filius hominis]], namely Christ, [[Dan 7:13|came even to the ancient of days|ad Antiquum dierum pervenit]], that is, to the eternal Father, [[Dan 7:14|And he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom: and all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him: his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed|et ipse dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum: et omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Potestas ejus potestas æterna, quæ non auferetur, et regnum ejus quod non corrumpetur]] [the margin's reference here is partly unreadable: Dan. vii, …; the words are those of Dan 7:13–14].

paras.t: Equum et ascensorem dejecit in mare. Per equos possunt intelligi universi indomiti christianæ fidei inimici, puta Judæi increduli, ceterique tyranni, quorum ascensores fuerunt diaboli, a quibus instigabantur ad Christianorum persecutionem et Christi blasphemiam: quos Christus post suam in cælum ascensionem projecit in mare, id est in profundum damnationis tartareæ, quod instar maris inquietum, amarum et suppliciorum fluctibus plenum est. Verumtamen multos illorum misericordissime traxit ad fidem, salubriterque projecit in mare, id est in fontem Baptismi, qui secundum aliam maris proprietatem significatur per mare. Circa hunc locum loquitur Origenes: Sunt equi quos Dominus ascendit, et circumeunt omnem terram. Sunt autem et equi, qui ascensorem habent diabolum et angelos ejus. Judas equus fuit; et quamdiu ascensorem habuit Deum, de equitatu fuit salutis. Etenim apostolus missus, ægris salutem donavit, et sanitatem languentibus præstitit. Sed ubi diabolo se prostravit, ascensor ejus factus est Satanas, cujus habenis ductus, cœpit contra Dominum et Salvatorem nostrum equitare. Omnes ergo qui persequuntur justos et sanctos, equi sunt hinnientes, ascensoresque habent angelos malos: idcirco feroces sunt. Si ergo aliquando videris persecutorem tuum sævientem nimium, scito quia ab ascensore suo diabolo perurgetur. Hæc Origenes.
paras.en: [[15:1|The horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea|Equum et ascensorem dejecit in mare]]. By the horses may be understood all the untamed enemies of the Christian faith, for instance the unbelieving Jews and the other tyrants, whose riders were the devils, by whom they were urged on to the persecution of Christians and the blasphemy of Christ: these Christ, after His ascension into heaven, cast into the sea, that is, into the depth of the damnation of hell, which like the sea is restless, bitter, and full of the waves of torments. Yet many of them He most mercifully drew to the faith, and cast them, to their salvation, into the sea, that is, into the font of Baptism, which by another property of the sea is signified by the sea. On this passage Origen says: There are horses which the Lord mounts, and they go round the whole earth. But there are also horses which have the devil and his angels for their rider. Judas was a horse; and as long as he had God for his rider, he was of the cavalry of salvation. For, sent as an apostle, he gave health to the sick and restored soundness to the ailing. But when he prostrated himself before the devil, Satan became his rider, and led by his reins he began to ride against our Lord and Saviour. All, therefore, who persecute the just and the holy are neighing horses, and have evil angels for their riders: that is why they are fierce. If, then, you ever see your persecutor raging beyond measure, know that he is being spurred on by his rider, the devil. Thus far Origen.

paras.t: Fortitudo mea et laus mea Dominus. Ipse etenim contestatur: Sine me nihil potestis facere. Idcirco ipsum in cunctis laudare debemus. Et factus est mihi in salutem. Ipse etenim dixit: Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Et rursus: Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat. De quo et in Isaia legitur: Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Qui in Osee fatur: Ego Dominus Deus tuus, et salvator non est præter me. De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos. Ero mors tua, o mors! morsus tuus ero, inferne! Verumtamen non credentibus et ingratis, carnalibus et iniquis, ipse Christus et passio ejus sanctissima, est occasio gravioris damnationis, petraque scandali et lapis offensionis, secundum quod justus Simeon prophetavit: Positus est hic, inquiens, in ruinam et in resurrectionem multorum in Israel. Iste Deus meus. Christus namque est Deus verus et vita æterna, ut in prima sua Canonica fatetur Joannes evangelista. De quo et in Isaia prædictum est: Vocabitur nomen ejus Admirabilis, Consiliarius, Deus, Fortis, Pater futuri sæculi, Princeps pacis. Unde et in Michæa fertur de eo: Egressus ejus a principio, a diebus æternitatis. Atque in Psalmo: Adorabunt eum omnes reges, omnes gentes servient ei. Et glorificabo eum, id est, ejus majestatem corde credam, ore confitebor, et conversatione honorare non desinam. Ipse etenim dixit: Beatus est qui non fuerit scandalizatus in me. Ideo quanto propter me humilior et contemptibilior ac miserabilior factus est, tanto sublimior, honorabilior, et gloriosior est in corde meo. Deus patris mei. Omnes etenim patres nostri, viri vere catholici, ejus deitatem sunt fassi: idcirco hos reputo patres meos; non autem hæreticos, qui ejus deitatem non crediderunt, ut Arius, Eunomius, Photinus, Nestorius, Ebion, et Cerinthus. Et exaltabo eum, ejus sublimationem ad dexteram Dei Patris recognoscendo.
paras.en: [[15:2|The Lord is my strength and my praise|Fortitudo mea et laus mea Dominus]]. For He Himself testifies: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]. Therefore we ought to praise Him in all things. [[15:2|And he is become salvation to me|Et factus est mihi in salutem]]. For He Himself said: [[John 10:15|I lay down my life for my sheep|Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. And again: [[Luke 19:10|the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost|Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat]]. Of whom we read also in Isaias: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. It is He who speaks in Osee: [[Osee 13:4|I am the Lord thy God|Ego Dominus Deus tuus]], [[Osee 13:4|and there is no saviour beside me|et salvator non est præter me]]. [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos. Ero mors tua, o mors! morsus tuus ero, inferne!]]! Yet to the unbelieving and the ungrateful, to the carnal and the wicked, Christ Himself and His most holy Passion is the occasion of a heavier damnation, [[1 Pet 2:8|a rock of scandal|petraque scandali]] and [[1 Pet 2:8|a stone of stumbling|lapis offensionis]], as the just Simeon prophesied: [[Luke 2:34|this child is set|Positus est hic]], he says, [[Luke 2:34|for the fall and for the resurrection of many in Israel|in ruinam et in resurrectionem multorum in Israel]]. [[15:2|He is my God|Iste Deus meus]]. For Christ is [[1 John 5:20|the true God and life eternal|Deus verus et vita æterna]], as John the Evangelist confesses in his first Canonical Epistle [the margin gives 1 Joann. ii, 25; the words are those of 1 John 5:20]. Of whom it was foretold also in Isaias: [[Is 9:6|his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace|Vocabitur nomen ejus Admirabilis, Consiliarius, Deus, Fortis, Pater futuri sæculi, Princeps pacis]]. Hence it is said of Him in Michæas too: [[Mich 5:2|his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity|Egressus ejus a principio, a diebus æternitatis]]. And in the Psalm: [[Ps 71:11|all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him|Adorabunt eum omnes reges, omnes gentes servient ei]]. [[15:2|And I will glorify him|Et glorificabo eum]], that is, I will believe His majesty with the heart, confess it with the mouth, and not cease to honour it by my way of life. For He Himself said: [[Matt 11:6|blessed is he that shall not be scandalized in me|Beatus est qui non fuerit scandalizatus in me]]. Therefore the humbler, the more despised and the more pitiable He became for my sake, the more exalted, the more honourable and the more glorious He is in my heart. [[15:2|The God of my father|Deus patris mei]]. For all our fathers, truly Catholic men, confessed His Godhead: therefore I reckon these my fathers, and not the heretics who did not believe in His Godhead, such as Arius, Eunomius, Photinus, Nestorius, Ebion and Cerinthus. [[15:2|And I will exalt him|Et exaltabo eum]], by acknowledging His exaltation to the right hand of God the Father.

paras.t: Dominus quasi vir pugnator. Christus Dominus vere vir fuit, de quo Jeremias prædixit: Novum faciet Dominus super terram: Mulier circumdabit virum. Fuit equidem vir etiam in materno utero Virginali, non utique corporis quantitate, sed omni divinorum charismatum perfectione, omni sapientia et virtute. Fuit item pugnator, qui ad debellandas aereas potestates processit ut gigas. De quo Psalmista prædixit: Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio. Ipse quippe fortem armatum, hoc est diabolum, ligavit, et vasa ejus diripuit, quia peccatores salvavit, secundum quod per Isaiam Pater prædixit: Dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia. Omnipotens nomen ejus. Propterea, sicut jam allegatum est, Isaias inter sex nomina Christi posuit, Fortis. Et ipsemet Filius Dei ait: Quæcumque facit Pater, hæc et Filius similiter facit. Per quod evidenter insinuat, quod sit æqualis, imo et ejusdem potestatis cum Patre.
paras.en: [[15:3|The Lord is as a man of war|Dominus quasi vir pugnator]]. Christ the Lord was truly a man, of whom Jeremias foretold: [[Jer 31:22|the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Novum faciet Dominus super terram: Mulier circumdabit virum]] [Denis has 'shall make' for 'hath created']. Indeed He was a man even in His Virgin Mother's womb, not, of course, in size of body, but in all perfection of divine gifts [Latin charismata, the gifts of grace], in all wisdom and virtue. He was also a warrior, who went forth [[Ps 18:6|as a giant|ut gigas]] to overthrow the powers of the air. Of Him the Psalmist foretold: [[Ps 23:8|the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle|Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio]]. For He bound the [[Luke 11:21|strong man armed|fortem armatum]], that is, the devil, and plundered his goods, because He saved sinners, as the Father foretold through Isaias: [[Is 53:12|will I distribute to him very many, and he shall divide the spoils of the strong|Dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia]]. [[15:3|Almighty is his name|Omnipotens nomen ejus]]. For this reason, as has already been cited, Isaias set Mighty among the six names of Christ[[Is 9:6||]]. And the Son of God Himself says: [[John 5:19|what things soever he doth, these the Son also doth in like manner|Quæcumque facit Pater, hæc et Filius similiter facit]]. By which He plainly gives us to understand that He is equal to the Father, indeed of one and the same power with Him.

paras.t: Currus Pharaonis et exercitum ejus projecit in mare. Quemadmodum viri sancti et veri doctores, idoneique prælati, sunt currus populi christiani et gregis eis commissi, quoniam sua perfectione, pietate, doctrina, paternaliter ferunt, supportant, dirigunt ac deducunt proximos suos ad patriam Beatorum: propter quod non solum currus, sed et aurigæ vocantur, quemadmodum quarto Regum beatissimi viri Elias et Eliseus currus Israel et auriga ejus dicuntur; sic hæresiarchæ, seductores, principes et prælati iniqui, et qui alios trahunt ad vitia, sunt currus Pharaonis, id est diaboli, cujus exercitus sunt collectio vitiosorum, quos omnes projicit Christus omnium judex in mare tartareum, ubi moratur Leviathan. Electi principes ejus submersi sunt in mari Rubro: quia angeli tenebrarum qui cum Lucifero ceciderunt, et qui in hominibus deteriores, ac per hoc, diabolo placentiores fuerunt, simul cum illo jam perierunt, aut disperibunt, præsertim in die judicii, quum pariter audient: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[15:4|Pharao's chariots and his army he hath cast into the sea|Currus Pharaonis et exercitum ejus projecit in mare]]. Just as holy men and true doctors and fit prelates are the chariots of the Christian people and of the flock entrusted to them, since by their perfection, piety and teaching they carry, support, direct and lead their neighbours, as fathers, to the fatherland of the Blessed (for which reason they are called not only chariots but also drivers, as in the fourth book of Kings the most blessed men Elias and Eliseus are called [[4 Kings 2:12|the chariot of Israel, and the driver thereof|currus Israel et auriga ejus]][[4 Kings 13:14||]]): so heresiarchs, seducers, wicked princes and prelates, and those who draw others to vice, are the chariots of Pharao, that is, of the devil, whose army is the gathering of the vicious; and all these Christ, the Judge of all, casts into the sea of hell, where Leviathan dwells. [[15:4|His chosen captains are drowned in the Red Sea|Electi principes ejus submersi sunt in mari Rubro]]: because the angels of darkness who fell with Lucifer[[Is 14:12||]], and those among men who were worse, and for that very reason more pleasing to the devil, have already perished together with him, or will perish, above all on the day of judgment, when they shall hear together: Depart, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]].

paras.t: Abyssi operuerunt eos, id est fluctus iniquitatum, quibus repleti sunt. Descenderunt in profundum quasi lapis. Nunc enim descendunt in voraginem vitiorum, deinde in infima infernorum.
paras.en: [[15:5|The depths have covered them|Abyssi operuerunt eos]], that is, the floods of iniquities with which they are filled. [[15:5|They are sunk to the bottom like a stone|Descenderunt in profundum quasi lapis]]. For now they go down into the whirlpool of vices, and afterwards into the lowest parts of hell.

paras.t: Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine. Per dexteram Dei intelligitur Unigenitus Patris æterni, qui etiam brachium Patris vocatur: nam Pater per Filium omnia operatur. Sic et Spiritus Sanctus dicitur digitus Dei, quia per eum Pater ostendit nobis omnem veritatem necessariam ad salutem. Itaque, o Domine Pater, dextera tua magnificata est in fortitudine, id est, Unigenitus tuus magnificatus est vehementer, tam in sua fortitudine increata, quam in fortitudine sua creata, suæ humanitati collata. Nam data est ei omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. De hac dextera ait Psalmista: Salvavit sibi dextera ejus, et brachium sanctum ejus. De quo et in Isaia habetur: Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium. Dextera tua, Domine, percussit inimicum, quia vicit diabolum, sicut in libro Job continetur: Prudentia ejus percussit superbum; et obstetricante manu ejus, eductus est coluber tortuosus.
paras.en: [[15:6|Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength|Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine]]. By the right hand of God is understood the Only-begotten of the eternal Father, who is also called the arm of the Father: for the Father works all things through the Son. So too the Holy Ghost is called the finger of God[[Luke 11:20||]], because through Him the Father shows us all the truth necessary for salvation. Therefore, O Lord Father, [[15:6|Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength|dextera tua magnificata est in fortitudine]], that is, Thy Only-begotten has been exceedingly magnified, both in His uncreated strength and in His created strength, bestowed on His humanity. For [[Matt 28:18|All power is given|data est ei omnis potestas]] to Him [[Matt 28:18|in heaven and in earth|in cœlo et in terra]]. Of this right hand the Psalmist says: [[Ps 97:1|His right hand hath wrought for him salvation, and his arm is holy|Salvavit sibi dextera ejus, et brachium sanctum ejus]]. Of which we have also in Isaias: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]]. [[15:6|Thy right hand, O Lord, hath slain the enemy|Dextera tua, Domine, percussit inimicum]], because He conquered the devil, as is contained in the book of Job: [[Job 26:12|his wisdom has struck the proud one|Prudentia ejus percussit superbum]]; [[Job 26:13|and his obstetric hand brought forth the winding serpent|et obstetricante manu ejus, eductus est coluber tortuosus]].

paras.t: Et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti adversarios meos. Quemadmodum Salomon profitetur, Gloria patris, filius sapiens: quanto magis Christus, qui est ipsa Sapientia increata, est gloria sui Patris? Itaque Pater in multitudine gloriæ suæ, hoc est per multiplicem passionem, per virtutes ac merita Filii sui, universos hostes nostræ salutis dejecit, videlicet spiritum superbiæ, spiritum fornicationis, spiritum iracundiæ, spiritum cupiditatis.
paras.en: [[15:7|And in the multitude of thy glory thou hast put down|Et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti]] my [[15:7|adversaries|adversarios]] [Denis reads 'my adversaries', the Vulgate 'thy adversaries']. As Solomon declares, the glory of a father is a wise son[[Prov 15:20||]] [the margin gives Prov. xv, 20, which reads 'A wise son maketh a father joyful']: how much more is Christ, who is uncreated Wisdom itself, the glory of His Father? So the Father, in the multitude of His glory, that is, through the manifold Passion and through the virtues and merits of His Son, has cast down all the enemies of our salvation, namely the spirit of pride, the spirit of fornication, the spirit of anger, the spirit of covetousness.

paras.t: Misisti iram tuam, quæ devoravit eos sicut stipulam, hoc est, justo judicio expulisti illos a vasis misericordiæ tuæ, sicut et Christus passione instante fassus est: Nunc judicium est mundi, nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Christus quoque passim depulit dæmones ab obsessis. Unde dixerunt: Jesu, Fili Dei summi, venisti ante tempus torquere nos? Quod et per suos copiosissime fecit discipulos, quibus dixit: Dæmones ejicite.
paras.en: [[15:7|thou hast sent thy wrath, which hath devoured them like stubble|Misisti iram tuam, quæ devoravit eos sicut stipulam]], that is, by a just judgment Thou hast driven them out from the vessels of Thy mercy, as Christ too declared when His Passion was at hand: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc judicium est mundi, nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. Christ also drove out devils from the possessed in many places[[Mark 1:34||]]. Hence they said: [[Matt 8:29|Jesus Son of God|Jesu, Fili Dei]] most high, [[Matt 8:29|art thou come hither to torment us before the time|venisti ante tempus torquere nos]]? [the margin gives Luc. iv, 34; Denis's words are those of Matt 8:29, with 'most high' as in Mark 5:7 and Luke 8:28]. This He did also most abundantly through His disciples, to whom He said: [[Matt 10:8|cast out devils|Dæmones ejicite]].

paras.t: Et in spiritu furoris tui congregatæ sunt aquæ. Per aquas, populi designantur, juxta illud in Apocalypsi: Aquæ multæ, populi multi. Unde et Ecclesiastes scribit: Mitte panem tuum super transeuntes aquas. Congregatæ sunt itaque aquæ in spiritu furoris Dei, quando impiissimi incredulique Judæi, qui Christum et ejus discipulos gravissime fuerunt persecuti in Jerusalem, pariter sunt a Romanis obsessi, et miserabilissime cruciati secundum quod Christus apud Lucam prænuntiavit: Videns enim civitatem, flevit super illam, dicens: Circumdabunt te inimici tui undique; eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ. Hunc Propheta prædixit: Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos. Stetit unda fluens; hoc est, exercitus Romanorum instar undæ copiosus atque discurrens, tunc in gyro Jerusalem fixit gradum. Congregatæ sunt abyssi, id est populi Judæorum, in medio mari, hoc est in medio Jerusalem, quæ tunc omni vitiorum inquietudine et infidelitatis amaritudine fuit repleta: imo ut mare aquis, ita miseriis plena fuit, juxta illud in Threnis: Magna velut mare contritio tua.
paras.en: [[15:8|And with the blast of thy anger the waters were gathered together|Et in spiritu furoris tui congregatæ sunt aquæ]]. By the waters peoples are signified, according to that saying in the Apocalypse: Many waters, many peoples[[Apoc 17:15||]]. Hence Ecclesiastes too writes: [[Eccles 11:1|Cast thy bread upon the running waters|Mitte panem tuum super transeuntes aquas]]. So the waters were gathered together in the spirit of God's fury when the most impious and unbelieving Jews, who had most grievously persecuted Christ and His disciples in Jerusalem[[Acts 4:1||]][[Acts 5:1||]] [the margin gives Act. iv et v], were in their turn besieged by the Romans and most miserably tormented, as Christ foretold in Luke: For [[Luke 19:41|seeing the city, he wept over it, saying|Videns enim civitatem, flevit super illam, dicens]]: [[Luke 19:43|thy enemies|inimici tui]] shall [[Luke 19:43|compass thee round|Circumdabunt te]] [[Luke 19:43|on every side|undique]], [[Luke 19:44|because thou hast not known the time of thy visitation|eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ]]. This the Prophet foretold: [[Ps 68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them|Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos]] [the margin's reference here is unreadable; the words are those of Ps 68:25]. [[15:8|The flowing water stood|Stetit unda fluens]]: that is, the army of the Romans, abundant like a wave and running to and fro, then set its foot round about Jerusalem. [[15:8|The depths were gathered together|Congregatæ sunt abyssi]], that is, the peoples of the Jews, [[15:8|in the midst of the sea|in medio mari]], that is, in the midst of Jerusalem, which was then filled with all the restlessness of vices and the bitterness of unbelief: indeed, as the sea is full of water, so was it full of miseries, according to that saying in the Lamentations: [[Lam 2:13|great as the sea is thy destruction|Magna velut mare contritio tua]].

paras.t: Dixit inimicus: Persequar et comprehendam, dividam spolia, implebitur anima mea; evaginabo gladium meum, interficiet eos manus mea. Hoc tam de visibilibus, quam de invisibilibus fidei christianæ atque fidelium hostibus, potest exponi. Visibilis equidem inimicus, videlicet populus Judæorum incredulus, deinde imperatores Romani, principes judicesque terreni ac perfidi condixerunt ac præsumpserunt se populum christianum penitus deleturos, et spolia ejus juxta propria desideria divisuros. Invisibiles quoque hostes, fidelium animas tentare aut persequi, eorumque spirituales divitias demoliri conati sunt, imo et electos quosque ac sanctos se posse vincere præsumpserunt: contra quos, suos gladios specialiter extraxerunt, ab occultis insidiis in apertas infestationes et interdum in corporales flagellationes ac læsiones crudeliter erumpendo, ut patuit in sacratissimo abbate Antonio, multisque aliis.
paras.en: [[15:9|The enemy said: I will pursue and overtake, I will divide the spoils, my soul shall have its fill: I will draw my sword, my hand shall slay them|Dixit inimicus: Persequar et comprehendam, dividam spolia, implebitur anima mea; evaginabo gladium meum, interficiet eos manus mea]]. This can be expounded both of the visible and of the invisible enemies of the Christian faith and of the faithful. The visible enemy, namely the unbelieving people of the Jews, and after them the Roman emperors, and earthly and faithless princes and judges, agreed together and presumed that they would utterly destroy the Christian people and divide its spoils according to their own desires. The invisible enemies too strove to tempt or persecute the souls of the faithful and to pull down their spiritual riches; indeed they presumed that they could overcome even the elect and the saints: against these they drew their swords in particular, breaking out cruelly from hidden snares into open assaults, and at times into bodily scourgings and wounds, as was seen in the most holy abbot Anthony and in many others.

paras.t: Flavit spiritus tuus, et operuit eos mare. Nam adspirante Spiritu Sancto, victi sunt invisibiles hostes a famulis Dei. Effusa quoque justa Dei indignatione, perierunt visibiles inimici. Nam super Judæos pervenit ira Dei usque in finem; sed et tyranni idololatræ defecerunt, et Romanum imperium fidei christianæ se subdidit. Sicque evidenter impletum est, quod in Isaia Christus prædixit: Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea. Submersi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis vehementibus: quia in propriarum iniquitatum profluviis, in suarum fluctibus pravitatum damnati sunt. Porro justi, quorum corda per caritatem sursum moventur, et igne Spiritus Sancti in cœlestia elevantur, super has ambulant aquas. Interdum tamen ex fragilitate humana vacillant: quod per Petrum signatum est, cui super aquas ambulanti ac trepidanti locutus est Christus: Modicæ fidei, quare dubitasti? Hinc asserit Origenes: Quis ita beatus est, qui sic tentationum pondus expediat, ut nulla ambiguitatis cogitatio, menti ejus obrepat? Vide quid magno illi Ecclesiæ fundamento ac solidissimæ petræ, super quam Christus fundavit Ecclesiam, dicatur a Domino: Modicæ fidei, quare dubitasti? Hæc Origenes. In quibus verbis antiquus ille et excellentissimi ingenii doctor, magnificum exhibet testimonium auctoritati ac eminentiæ, gloriosissimo archiapostolo Petro collatis a Christo.
paras.en: [[15:10|Thy wind blew and the sea covered them|Flavit spiritus tuus, et operuit eos mare]] [Latin spiritus, both 'wind' and 'spirit']. For by the breathing of the Holy Ghost the invisible enemies were overcome by the servants of God. And when God's just indignation was poured out, the visible enemies perished. For the wrath of God came upon the Jews to the end; the idolatrous tyrants also failed, and the Roman empire submitted itself to the Christian faith. And so there was plainly fulfilled what Christ foretold in Isaias: [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]] [the margin gives Is. lxiii]. [[15:10|They sunk as lead in the mighty waters|Submersi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis vehementibus]]: because they were damned in the floods of their own iniquities, in the waves of their own wickedness. But the just, whose hearts are moved upward by charity and lifted up to heavenly things by the fire of the Holy Ghost, walk upon these waters. Yet at times they waver through human frailty: which was signified in Peter, to whom, as he walked upon the waters and was afraid, Christ said: [[Matt 14:31|O thou of little faith, why didst thou doubt|Modicæ fidei, quare dubitasti]]? Hence Origen says: Who is so blessed as to bear the weight of temptations so that no doubting thought creeps into his mind? See what is said by the Lord to that great foundation of the Church and most solid rock, upon which Christ founded the Church: [[Matt 14:31|O thou of little faith, why didst thou doubt|Modicæ fidei, quare dubitasti]]? Thus far Origen. In which words that ancient doctor of most excellent genius bears splendid witness to the authority and pre-eminence conferred by Christ on the most glorious chief Apostle Peter.

paras.t: Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? quis similis tui? Fortes fuerunt sancti Apostoli, de quibus cantatur in Psalmo: Dii fortes terræ vehementer elevati sunt. Nullus tamen eorum æqualis est Christo; imo ab increata ejus perfectione deficiunt infinite, a creata quoque perfectione ineffabiliter valde. Dæmones insuper naturali fortitudine fortes sunt et subtiles; et qui in idolis habitaverunt, divina potentia se præditos confinxerunt: et tamen Christi virtute sunt dissipati, et idololatria fuit destructa longe lateque, quamvis non in toto ubique. Magnificus in sanctitate. Christus in sanctitate magnificus fuit, quia sanctissime vixit, evangelicam legem omni perfectione ornatam proposuit, et suæ sanctitatis virtute innumerabilia egit miracula. Terribilis, quoniam omnium constitutus est metuendissimus judex; atque laudabilis, quoniam peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus: et faciens mirabilia: nam usque in præsens præclara facit per Sanctos suos miracula. Porro in animabus electorum suorum facit assidue mirabilia vere sublimia, irradiando interius, præcordia inflammando, consolationes supernas infundendo, voluntatem immutando, vitiosos, carnales, vagos et vanos subito ac misericordissime convertendo, et quasi de extremo ad extremum potentissime transferendo, in tantum, ut tales in adolescentiæ flore, in juventutis vigore, universa quæ mundi sunt deserant, religionem intrantes. O vere mutatio dexteræ Excelsi!
paras.en: [[15:11|Who is like to thee, among the strong, O Lord? who is like to thee|Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? quis similis tui]]? Strong were the holy Apostles, of whom it is sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 46:10|the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted|Dii fortes terræ vehementer elevati sunt]] [the margin gives Ps. xlvi]. Yet none of them is equal to Christ; rather, they fall infinitely short of His uncreated perfection, and unspeakably far short of His created perfection too. Moreover the devils are strong and subtle by their natural strength; and those that dwelt in idols pretended to be endowed with divine power: and yet they were scattered by the power of Christ, and idolatry was destroyed far and wide, though not wholly everywhere. [[15:11|glorious in holiness|Magnificus in sanctitate]]. Christ was glorious in holiness, because He lived most holily, set forth the law of the Gospel adorned with all perfection, and by the power of His holiness worked innumerable miracles. [[15:11|terrible|Terribilis]], since He has been appointed the most fearsome Judge of all; [[15:11|and praise-worthy|atque laudabilis]], since He [[1 Pet 2:22|did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth|peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus]] [the margin gives Is. liii (see Is 53:9); Denis's words are those of 1 Pet 2:22, which quotes it]; [[15:11|doing wonders|et faciens mirabilia]]: for to this day He works glorious miracles through His Saints. Moreover in the souls of His elect He constantly works wonders that are truly sublime: enlightening them within, inflaming their hearts, pouring in heavenly consolations, changing the will, suddenly and most mercifully converting the vicious, the carnal, the wandering and the vain, and most powerfully carrying them over, as it were, from one extreme to the other, so much so that such men, in the flower of youth and the vigour of early manhood, forsake all that is of the world and enter religion. O truly [[Ps 76:11|the change of the right hand of the most High|mutatio dexteræ Excelsi]]!

paras.t: Extendisti manum tuam, et devoravit eos terra. Extendit Christus potestatem suam in actum, quando (ut dictum est) vastavit et dispersit Judæos, ita quod in terram absorpti sunt, quia projecti fuerunt in foveas, viliterque sepulti. In cruce quoque extendit manum ad populum non credentem, qui ob suam incredulitatem disperiit. Denique universi carnales et cupidi devorantur a terra, quia terrenis et carnalibus rebus jugiter sunt intenti, et in illis figunt spem suam. Ideo sordibus et cupiditatibus suis ipsi deglutiuntur a terra tenebrosa et operta mortis caligine: ubi umbra mortis, et sempiternus horror inhabitat et abundat.
paras.en: [[15:12|Thou stretchedst forth thy hand, and the earth swallowed them|Extendisti manum tuam, et devoravit eos terra]]. Christ stretched forth His power into act when (as has been said) He laid waste and scattered the Jews, so that they were swallowed up in the earth, for they were thrown into pits and basely buried. On the cross too He stretched forth His hand to a people that believed not, which perished for its unbelief[[Is 65:2||]] [the words 'a people that believeth not' are those of Rom 10:21, which quotes this verse]. Lastly, all the carnal and covetous are devoured by the earth, because they are ever intent on earthly and carnal things and fix their hope in them. Therefore, through their own filth and covetousness, they are swallowed up by [[Job 10:21|a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death|terra tenebrosa et operta mortis caligine]]: [[Job 10:22|where the shadow of death|ubi umbra mortis]], and [[Job 10:22|everlasting horror dwelleth|sempiternus horror inhabitat]] and abounds.

paras.t: Dux fuisti in misericordia tua populo quem redemisti. Dominus etenim Jesus locutus est: Ego sum pastor bonus, et cognosco oves meas. Ipse est rector et dux populi christiani per inspirationem divinam, per directiones angelicas, per prælatos et prædicatores, per evangelicam legem, per Sanctorum exempla, signa ac documenta. Et portasti eum in fortitudine tua ad habitaculum sanctum tuum: quia non solum ad militantem, sed item ad triumphantem Ecclesiam, quemadmodum ad Hebræos legitur: Accessistis ad montem Sion et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam, et Ecclesiam primitivorum, qui conscripti sunt in cœlis.
paras.en: [[15:13|In thy mercy thou hast been a leader to the people which thou hast redeemed|Dux fuisti in misericordia tua populo quem redemisti]]. For the Lord Jesus said: [[John 10:14|I am the good shepherd|Ego sum pastor bonus]], [[John 10:14|and I know mine|et cognosco oves meas]]. He is the ruler and leader of the Christian people through divine inspiration, through the guidance of angels, through prelates and preachers, through the law of the Gospel, through the examples, signs and teachings of the Saints. [[15:13|And in thy strength thou hast carried them to thy holy habitation|Et portasti eum in fortitudine tua ad habitaculum sanctum tuum]]: that is, not only to the Church militant but also to the Church triumphant, as we read in the Epistle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the company of many thousands of angels|Accessistis ad montem Sion et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam]], [[Heb 12:23|And to the church of the firstborn who are written in the heavens|et Ecclesiam primitivorum, qui conscripti sunt in cœlis]].

paras.t: Ascenderunt populi, et irati sunt. Increduli namque Judæi atque pagani, multipliciter se opposuerunt evangelicæ legis prædicationi. Dolores obtinuerunt habitatores Philistiim. Per quos designantur gulosi, quia Philistiim interpretantur, potione cadentes. Tunc conturbati sunt principes Edom, id est avari et principes cupidorum, quoniam Edom interpretatur, terrenus sive sanguineus. Robustos Moab obtinuit tremor. Per robustos Moab intelliguntur superbi, qui specialiter dicuntur et sunt filii diaboli. Moab equidem interpretatur, ex patre. Et talibus ait Salvator: Vos ex patre diabolo estis. Obriguerunt omnes habitatores Chanaan. Chanaan interpretatur, commotio. Per habitatores itaque Chanaan, recte accipiuntur luxuriosi, qui specialiter instabiles corde sunt, vani et stolidi, passionibus variis agitati, nusquam ad Deum sincere erecti. Hi omnes audientes prædicari evangelicam legem, in qua præfata vitia condemnantur, et virtutes oppositæ, scilicet sobrietas, liberalitas, paupertas, humilitas, castitas, edocentur, commendantur, jubentur, irati et conturbati fuerunt. Quumque vidissent legem hanc prævalere, et Romanum imperium esse ei subjectum, expaverunt et contremuerunt. Innumerabiles quoque eorum conversi sunt, qui salubriter timuerunt.
paras.en: [[15:14|Nations rose up, and were angry|Ascenderunt populi, et irati sunt]]. For the unbelieving Jews and pagans opposed themselves in many ways to the preaching of the law of the Gospel. [[15:14|sorrows took hold on the inhabitants of Philisthiim|Dolores obtinuerunt habitatores Philistiim]]. By these the gluttonous are signified, because Philisthiim is interpreted 'falling by drink'. [[15:15|Then were the princes of Edom troubled|Tunc conturbati sunt principes Edom]], that is, the avaricious and the princes of the covetous, since Edom is interpreted 'earthly' or 'blood-red'.
